items.statement: TAN production estimated at 160,000-170,000 tons in FY27 assuming 9 months operation
items.quote: So, let's assume that we have got about nine months production to be very conservative. So, we are saying that we have roughly about 1,60,000 - 1,70,000 tons of production would be possible.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at Rs 500 crores including TAN balance and routine Rs 170-180 crores
items.quote: The total put together should be around Rs. 500 crores balance, I mean, Urea and TAN put together.

items.statement: New urea plant (1.3 MT) brownfield cost estimated at Rs 9,500-10,000 crores
items.quote: The price is INR 9,500 crores to INR 10,000 crores. That is the upper bound as far as brownfield projects are concerned.

items.statement: Complex fertilizer stocks secured till July-August 2026 via strategic early purchases
items.quote: Secondly, as far as Chambal is concerned, we did make some strategic purchases, very big, early in the beginning of the year, and we are covered at least till July-August in terms of our stocks.

items.statement: Urea business operates on cost-plus basis; higher gas costs passed through via subsidy
items.quote: So, if you understand this business, it is basically a cost-plus kind of business. So, government recognizes the cost and therefore, in terms of higher prices of gas, except for that impact on working capital, we are able to pass on the cost to the government in the form of subsidy, increased subsidy.

items.statement: Current gas cost around USD 18.5 per MMBtu for Q1 FY27
items.quote: Currently, what I understand, it is USD 18 plus, USD 18.5 plus. It may be around the same number.

items.statement: TAN market demand growing at 6-7% annually; market currently short due to Russian export curbs
items.quote: And it is a healthy growth, I would say, given that we are already at 1.2 million tons or so of demand. So, if you are saying 6%-7% growth, we are talking about 70,000 tons per year, add on year to year, that kind of number.

items.statement: Crop protection, specialty nutrients and biologicals revenue grew 30% YoY to Rs 1,203 crores in FY26 with 23.5% EBIT margin
items.quote: For FY '26, the segment delivered strong performance revenues increasing by 30% year-on-year to INR 1,203 crores as compared to INR 926 crores in FY '25, and EBIT margins remained healthy at around 23.5%.

items.statement: Biologicals volumes up 30% and revenues up 57% in FY26; 14 new crop protection products planned for FY27
items.quote: The biological business continued to scale up well, with robust increases of about 30% in volumes and 57% growth in revenues, reflecting increased farmer adoption of sustainable agricultural solutions.

items.statement: Phosphatic fertilizer availability constrained by logistics (28-29 ships stuck at Hormuz), not production
items.quote: We have many ships, about 28 or 29 ships, which are stuck up in the Hormuz. They are carrying material. They are loaded up there and so on. So, it is more a question of logistics than production.

items.statement: G-3 urea profitability clarity expected in a month; new regime starts Dec 1, 2026
items.quote: Too premature to give you any guidance on this, but it is moving. That much I can say, because we are to be in this regime from December 1st onwards.

items.statement: IMACID JV P2O5 capacity expansion to 7 lakh MT by Dec 2026; sulphuric acid capacity expansion in FY27
items.quote: The increase in P2O5 production capacity from 5 lakh metric tons to 7 lakh metric tons is expected to be implemented in December 26. Further, Sulphuric acid capacity is also being increased, which is expected to be implemented a year ahead in FY '27.

items.statement: Final dividend of Rs 6 per share recommended, total Rs 11 per share for FY26
items.quote: Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of Rs. INR 6 per share, totaling to Rs. 11 per equity share for FY '26.

items.statement: Crude steel production target of 22.5 million tons for FY27 including 0.6 million tons RINL volumes
items.quote: Our capacity is 21 million tons, and we are targeting to produce 22 million tons. I think it is 22.5 million tons so far as our target is concerned for '26-'27.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR15,000 crores for FY27, rising to INR18,000-19,000 crores in FY28 and INR20,000-25,000 crores annually thereafter
items.quote: Guidance for '26-'27 is INR15,000 crores. And since our expansion projects are ongoing in different, different plants. So in '27-'28, the capex figures will be in excess of INR20,000 crores.

items.statement: Expansion projects at IISCO (INR35,000 crores, 4.5 mt), Bhilai (INR30,000 crores, 3.5 mt), and Bokaro (INR18,000 crores, 3 mt) with major spend from FY28-29
items.quote: capex of IISCO is around INR36,000 crores -- maybe INR35,000 crores. And Bhilai, which is yet to be announced is around INR30,000 crores, and Bokaro is somewhere around INR18,000 crores, something like that.

items.statement: Margins expected to improve further in FY27 due to firm steel prices, rupee depreciation, and cost reduction efforts despite higher coking coal costs
items.quote: With the coal price remaining in range bound -- coal prices remaining on the higher side range bound actually, we hope that the margins will continue to improve further.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 NSR: Longs INR53,400/t, Flats INR51,000/t; April-May NSR: Longs ~INR57,600-57,800/t, Flats ~INR56,000-56,700/t
items.quote: In quarter 4, NSR of -- average NSR of long products was INR53,400 and flat was INR51,000. When we compare this with April, NSR of long products is INR57,600 and NSR of flat is INR56,700.

items.statement: Coking coal procurement cost rose from INR18,200/t in Q4 to INR21,000/t in April and INR21,800/t in May; blended consumption impact lower due to 30-day stock
items.quote: Coking coal, when we look at actually in quarter 4, the coking coal average price is INR18,200, which has gone up in April and May. April average price is INR21,000 and May average price is INR21,800.

items.statement: Demand muted in Q1-Q2 FY27 due to seasonal destocking; expected to pick up from Q3 onwards
items.quote: Generally, demand remains muted in quarter 1 and quarter 2, as all of us have seen, on the back of more sales in quarter 4. So there are events of destocking in quarter 1.

items.statement: Rail price revision for FY25 to be finalized in FY27; impact uncertain (could be positive or negative); no arrears in FY26
items.quote: So far as '26-'27 is concerned, we can't say anything about whether we'll get an advantage from rail price revision or we'll get a negative on rail price revision.

items.statement: Wage revision effective Jan 1, 2027; provision to be made in Q4 FY27 based on government guidelines; cost over and above current employee cost guidance
items.quote: As I told clearly, actually, government notification, etcetera, will come regarding pay revision. And after that, we'll make a provision in quarter 4 of next year, '26-'27.

items.statement: Employee count reduced by 3,400 to 49,752 as of Apr 1, 2026; further reduction of 3,400-3,500 per year expected in FY27-28 plus VRS targeting 500-1,000
items.quote: So as on 1st April 2026, the numbers are 49,752 as compared to 53,159 opening of this year. So a reduction of around 3,400 numbers.

items.statement: Iron ore production target raised to 56 million tons in FY27 from 38 million tons in FY26; aiming for 80 million tons; no major lease renewal issues except Chiria
items.quote: Last year we produced 38 million tons, while this year, we have kept a target of 56 million tons, out of which some quantity will be sold. And going forward, we are trying to ramp up to 80 million tons.

items.statement: Salem stainless steel plant: targeting yield improvement from 84% to 90% at CR mill, LPG to PNG conversion, cheaper power, and slab imports to utilize spare capacity
items.quote: So in CR mill, where the yield right now is only 84%, 83%, we are trying to increase it to 90%. We have taken a couple of other actions like replacing LPG with PNG.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at 11-13% low double-digit range for long term; EBITDA growth expected slightly ahead of revenue growth
items.quote: If you look at our full year growth, Mihir, it is 13%. And we've so far guided to a low double-digit growth in the range of 11% to 13%. And for a longish period of time, we will hold on to the same guidance.

items.statement: Raw material supply secured until at least mid-July with weekly inventory expansion; no volume impact from Middle East crisis in Q4
items.quote: We've made sure that availability is adequately covered till at least at this point in time till middle of July, and we continue to increase that on a weekly basis. So therefore, on availability, we are in a strong position.

items.statement: Middle East crisis affecting raw material availability and cost; supply secured till mid-July; proactive price increases implemented weekly; competitive advantage seen for market share gains
items.quote: The crisis has affected both the availability and cost of our key raw materials. We are proactively navigating the situation with a clear and structured approach. We are prioritizing supply security for our customers while ensuring that cost impact gets fully passed on.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA improved to 0.52x; ROCE improved 96bps to 19%; Thailand greenfield investment $5M; sustainable tubes 38% of sales; EcoVadis Platinum rating achieved
items.quote: Strong EBITDA and PAT performance, combined with healthy cash flow generation have enabled a further deleveraging of our balance sheet with net debt to EBITDA improving to 0.52x. Return on capital employed also improved to 19%, expanding by 96 basis points.

items.statement: Management declined to provide FY27 guidance for revenue, margins, order inflow, capex, working capital or net debt due to macro uncertainty; will revisit after Q1 FY27.
items.quote: We have decided not to give any guidance for FY27. However, we will revisit this decision, maybe when we will have -- we have some clarity after conclusion of the first quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR 83,004 crore as of 31 March 2026, up 16% YoY, highest ever; book-to-bill ~4x across seven verticals.
items.quote: Our consolidated order book as of 31st March '26, stood at INR 83,004 crores, which is about 16% increase over the last year, and highest in the company's history.

items.statement: Standalone order backlog INR 72,259 crore; subsidiary order backlog INR 10,745 crore.
items.quote: Standalone order backlog is INR 72,259 crores, and for a subsidiary company, it is INR 10,745 crores.

items.statement: Standalone segment-wise order backlog: Buildings INR 22,740 cr, Transportation INR 15,320 cr, Water & Railways INR 10,400 cr, Electrical INR 13,800 cr, Irrigation INR 4,950 cr, Mining INR 6,750 cr.
items.quote: Buildings, it is INR 22,740 crores. Transportation, INR 15,320 crores. Water and Railways, INR10,400 crores. Electrical, you can take INR 13,800 crores. Irrigation, you can take it as INR4,950 crores and mining, INR6,750 crores.

items.statement: JJM (Jal Jeevan Mission) total order book INR 26,000 crore; executed INR 20,142 crore; balance INR 6,181 crore as of 31 March 2026.
items.quote: The overall order book, what we have received for the JJM projects, including groundwater, surface water is INR26,000 crores. We have already executed projects up to INR 20,142 crores, leaving a balance of INR6,181 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex plan INR 500 crore (INR 100-150 crore for mining equipment, INR 350-400 crore regular replacement/refurbishment).
items.quote: FY27, the capex plan is INR500 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin 8.44% vs 9.21% YoY; consolidated EBITDA margin 8.83% vs 9.07% YoY.
items.quote: At the stand-alone level, we achieved an EBITDA of 8.44% for Q4 FY26 as against 9.21% of the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: 74% of contracts have escalation clauses; management unsure if price increases will be fully covered; potential material availability/logistics issues.
items.quote: About 74% of the contracts, we have escalation clauses. But I'm not very sure whether the increase in the prices will completely get covered under the escalation clauses. There may be some impact.

items.statement: Prospective project pipeline ~INR 2.5 lakh crore; active bidding continues based on risk/reward; INR 1,700 crore orders already bagged in April FY27.
items.quote: We continue to see a very interesting pipeline of prospective projects. If I were to put a number, this number would be close to INR 2.5 lakh crores.

items.statement: No international exposure except a small Qatar project (~INR 20-25 crore remaining); private clients only 4-5% of order book; no payment issues seen from government clients.
items.quote: At the moment, we do not have any international exposure. We have only one project in Qatar, which is almost completed at the final stage.

items.statement: Smart meter SPV debt closed at 9.15%; working capital facilities adequate, utilisation <80-90%; access to commercial paper and invoice discounting below 8%.
items.quote: As far as the projects which we have received on smart meters are concerned, we have done financial closure for those projects at a very competitive rate of 9.15%.

items.statement: Vizag Urban Infra outstanding INR 291 crore; expect full recovery of INR 250-291 crore in FY27.
items.quote: Coming to the Vizag Urban status, I've already explained to you, we will be collecting about INR250 crores and the outstanding is INR291 crores.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated capex guided at ~Rs 20,000 cr, >60% in India
items.quote: During FY2026, our total spend on capex was about Rs 14,000 crores on a consolidated basis and we intend to increase the same in FY2027 to around Rs 20,000 crores of which more than 60% will be spend in India.

items.statement: FY27 cost transformation savings target ~Rs 7,100 cr vs FY26
items.quote: In FY2027 we are aiming to achieve cost transformation related savings of ~Rs 7,100 crores vs. FY2026 levels.

items.statement: India volume growth at least 2 Mt YoY in FY27 driven by Kalinganagar ramp-up
items.quote: The volume will be at least 2 million tons better in this financial year compared to the previous financial year with most of it coming in India, largely because the Kalinganagar ramp up is pretty much complete.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 India realisations up ~Rs 6,000/t QoQ; UK up ~£80/t; Netherlands up ~€80/t
items.quote: In India we expect 1Q to be about Rs. 6,000 /t higher than 4Q. In UK, we expect it to be about £80/t higher in 1Q compared to 4Q and in Netherlands we expect it to be about €80/t higher in 1Q compared to 4Q.

items.statement: NINL expansion to 10 Mt site; FEL3 advanced, announcement in few months
items.quote: On NINL, the initial work on the site preparation has already started. We are getting permissions on different parts and the FEL3 which is our basis, for making the final allocation of capital, is also very advanced. So, in the next few months, we should be able to announce that.

items.statement: Downstream target 50-60% of volumes; Tubes to 4 Mt, Wires to 1 Mt, double Packaging & Colors
items.quote: We feel that we can do much more in color-coated steels. We were in some sense limited by the JV and that's why we bought out the BlueScope share and we plan to double the size of the Colors business also in the next 12-24 months. So, I think we want our downstream businesses to at least be about 50-60% of our volume.

items.statement: TSN material uncertainty from regulator letter on Coke & Gas Plant permits; planned closure discussed
items.quote: We have received a letter post the Balance Sheet date from the local environment agencies regarding their intent to revoke permits without any specifics-this causes the material uncertainty element for Tata Steel Netherlands while preparing the basis of preparing the financial statements.

items.statement: Board proposed dividend Rs 4/share (FV Rs 1) for FY26
items.quote: Board has proposed Dividend of Rs 4 per share for fully paid share of face value of Rs 1 each.

items.statement: UK prices up ~£80/t in Q1 vs Q4 FY26; Netherlands prices up ~€80/t in Q1 vs Q4 FY26; UK EBITDA losses to shrink further in Q1 and Q2
items.quote: 1Q prices will be about £80 /t higher in UK compared to 4Q and in Netherlands , it will be about €80 /t higher. The co al cost in Netherlands are going up about $10/t. So obviously from that point of view, there is a n expansion, and we expect margin s to improve in UK . Like I just described EBITDA losses to shrink ,

items.statement: India capex of Rs 12,000 crore in FY27 allocated across downstream (tinplate, wires, HRPGL Tarapur 0.8 MTPA), coke ovens Jamshedpur, Kalinganagar tail payments, sustainable projects, NINL, mining
items.quote: taking all that into account is Rs. 12,000 crores. If you are looking for whether we have allocated money for NINL, the answer is yes.

items.statement: NINL expansion: FID expected between July-September 2025, first steel target around 2029-30
items.quote: On NINL, I think between July and September, we should be able to get the FID and once we get the FID, the target date is somewhere around 2029-30.

items.statement: Next EAF project likely in Maharashtra (west), ~1.5 MTPA, can be built in ~2 years like Ludhiana; board approval after FEL3 detailing and all approvals in place
items.quote: We also plan that in the next year or so, we will announce the next E AF project, maybe somewhere in the west, possibly in Maharashtra. That is something, like you saw in Ludhiana, can be built in two years. So that can come up quite fast.

items.statement: Retail channel (Aashiyana) GMV ~Rs 5,000 crore, selling at same EBITDA margin as rest of Tata Steel, no discounts; DigECA for SMEs also growing well
items.quote: As you saw, we have the retail business Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) growing very fast, and this is being sold with no discounts at the same EBITDA margin that you see in the rest of Tata Steel. This is almost Rs. 5 ,000 crores now

items.statement: Netherlands to remain EBITDA positive even after coke oven closure, though with margin compression; Europe pricing converging to US levels due to quotas/CBAM
items.quote: going forward, if the coke ovens close, we expect it to continue to be EBITDA positive, maybe making less EBITDA than we had hoped we would make, but it will always be EBITDA positive.

items.statement: UK system EBITDA ~Rs 12,000/t on slab transfers (Rs 7,000-8,000/t from India slab supply + Rs 4,000-4,500/t UK conversion); target to increase slab supply from 1.2 to 1.8 MTPA
items.quote: on a system basis for the slabs going to the UK , we as Tata Steel consolidated make about Rs. 12,000/t of EBITDA. So that model will continue till the EAF starts

items.statement: Flat products holding up due to rising China prices (+$20-25/t), lower Chinese exports (<10 Mt), strong auto demand; long products under pressure from secondary producers' distress selling and construction slowdown
items.quote: Flat products is still holding out because prices in China have gone up over $20 -$25/t in the last 3-4 weeks. So international prices are going up. In fact, Indian flat product producers also have export options now. Export prices are not too bad. The weaker Rupee is also helping exports. So, export options are growin

items.statement: Retail Tiscon sales doubled to >200,000 t/month; shifting from cold rolled to galvanised/auto for better realisations; downstream focus (HRPGL 0.8 MTPA, tinplate 0.3-0.4 MTPA, tubes/wires) to capture value growth over volume growth
items.quote: Retail for us is far more attractive than projects. So, over the years, we have increased or pretty much doubled our sales to retail, which used to be at one point in time, 100,000-120,000 tons a month, is today over 200,000 tons a month.

items.statement: Netherlands: coke oven closure requires safe/controlled timeline, physical segregation of CGP, regulatory approvals, social license for future investment; UK: ~12-month delay in electricity infrastructure for EAF commissioning
items.quote: Once that happens, there are projects which have to be undertaken to segregate the CGP's physically from the rest of the plant. So that will take time and that is the reason why we are saying safe and control led closure.

items.statement: Iron ore costs rising sharply in India (bids >100% premium); coal import dependency increasing with weak INR; shifting value pools from upstream to downstream
items.quote: the cost of iron ore in India is going up. So, the value pools will shift. Value pools are not necessarily upstream going forward. Some of those value pools will shift downstream. For us , we've been buffered a bit because we've had our own iron ore , b ut if you generally look at cost of iron ore in India it is really

items.statement: Increasing stake in TMILL (logistics JV) from 51% to 74%, buying out IQ Martrade; TMILL operates 55 rakes, handles 5% of Indian Railways freight revenue; BRPL slurry pipeline capacity to double
items.quote: It was already a JV with 51% holding , and it will go to 74%, with NYK the balance. We will look at the next stage of growth in our logistics and want to make it integral to our growth plans also.

items.statement: India iron ore production ~45 Mt in FY26, sold ~4 Mt; washed coal ~3 Mt (raw ~6 Mt); post-2030 strategy: prudent auction bidding, Maharashtra iron ore linkage, imports (tested Canadian shipment), coastal capacity advantage (Kalinganagar, NI
items.quote: I think iron ore production would be close to 45 million tons and I think we've sold about 4 million tons , if I'm not mistaken . And we will continue to produce what we need for our own use and we will continue to maximi se the sales.

items.statement: JLR FY27 financial guidance to be given at Investor Day on June 17, 2026
items.quote: We'll give financial guidance at Investor Day in June. So, a great reason to join us here in Gaydon. That's going to be on the 17th of June.

items.statement: TMPV targets industry-beating growth in FY27 with healthy order book and lean inventory
items.quote: TMPV will look to deliver industry-beating growth in FY27. And for that, our growth levers are well in place. We have a healthy order book across models, lean channel inventory and are seeing strong sustained traction across models

items.statement: Industry PV growth pegged at ~10% in FY27 with high double-digit growth in H1
items.quote: I am pegging the number around 10% because the first half of last financial year was a low base. And therefore, in H1, you are going to see very strong double-digit growth

items.statement: TMPV FY26 capex was Rs 4,300 Cr (7.5% of revenue) within guidance range
items.quote: Capex for the year stood at about Rs. 4,300 Cr that translated to about 7.5% of revenues, well within the guidance range that we gave from the combined Capex for PV and EV.

items.statement: TMPV has healthy order book across models with lean channel inventory
items.quote: We have a healthy order book across models, lean channel inventory and are seeing strong sustained traction across models, which will serve us well in the coming quarters.

items.statement: JLR targets GBP 1.7 billion savings over two years to bring breakeven volume back to 300,000 units
items.quote: Together, we're targeting GBP1.7 billion of savings over two years to bring our breakeven volume back down towards 300,000 units a year.

items.statement: TMPV Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 9.4%, EBIT margin 4.7%; full year margins muted due to adverse pricing and commodity increases
items.quote: We ended the year with 9.4% EBITDA margin for the quarter and 4.7% EBIT margin. The PBT before extraordinary expenses in Q4 stood at Rs. 1,100 Cr.

items.statement: JLR VME at 7% in Q4 FY26; expected to remain relatively stable in FY27
items.quote: I think generally, it is relatively stable. I think it remains to be seen in China, how the industry absorbs the extra 10% luxury tax that was implemented in the middle of last year. But we are not seeing it rise considerably from the levels that we saw at the back end of the last financial year.

items.statement: JLR Range Rover EV has 78,000 expressions of interest; three EV reveals in H2 FY27
items.quote: We have expressions of interest, and there are 78,000 of those at the last count. So that's where we stand. It's coming. I've driven it, and it is fab.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility, protectionism, regulatory changes and supply chain challenges are structural supply-side pressures for JLR
items.quote: The splintering and volatility of geopolitics creates challenges from increasing protectionism, differing electrification appetites and technology concerns that, for example, mean we have to duplicate large parts of our ADAS developments.

items.statement: Segment B (Electro-Mechanical Projects) carry-forward order book at INR 6,200 crores as of March 31, 2026, with INR 4,500 crores domestic and INR 1,700 crores international
items.quote: As of 31st March 2026, the total carry forward order book in Segment B stood at close to INR 6,200 crores, providing strong revenue visibility and reinforcing confidence in the long-term growth opportunities across domestic and international projects business.

items.statement: RAC price hikes: 5% on 3-star (75% mix), 10% on 5-star (25% mix) = blended 6-7%; additional 2-3% for copper; further hikes likely as commodity costs hit
items.quote: Actually, each model as far as the first round of increases was concerned, it was a blended 6%-7% because it was 5% for the 3-star which is a larger portion, 75% mix, and 10% for 5-Star is around 25%. In addition, there was some other impacts because of the copper and commodities going up even before the war started. S

items.statement: Management expects double-digit cost inflation from war-related commodity and currency moves; will pass through progressively as inventory turns
items.quote: I completely agree that these numbers are not by any stretch of imagination, a small number. We are seriously talking about double-digit inflation. And it will get passed through as and when the costs start hitting us.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions and Middle East conflict caused operational disruptions in international projects; mitigated via crisis response teams, safety protocols, daily monitoring of operations, liquidity, and collections
items.quote: Within the international project business, geopolitical tensions and Middle East conflict created operational disruptions across travel, logistics, site execution and commercial settlements. Despite these challenges, Voltas responded with agility and discipline by activating dedicated crisis response teams, implemented

items.statement: No incremental fleet growth at current high asset prices; will continue switch transactions (sell old, buy newer)
items.quote: Replacing we will continue to do. Increasing we will not do for current yield.

items.statement: Cash breakeven for fleet around $9,000-9,500/day; book breakeven around $11,000-12,000/day
items.quote: Our book breakeven levels are probably around $12,000 a day between $11,000 and $12,000 a day. Our cash breakeven is probably in the $9,500 a day, something like that.

items.statement: LPG fleet moving partly to floating rate/spot exposure; one vessel starting floating rate charter this month
items.quote: We would like to run more on spot. We have made a small step in that direction with a floating -- with a floating rate -- part floating rate charter on one of our vessels. That will start this month sometime.

items.statement: Consolidated NAV improved by INR 200/share in Q4 FY26; highest ever quarterly dividend INR 11.70/share; full year dividend INR 35.10/share
items.quote: Our NAV continues to move higher, moving by about INR 200 between end of December and end of March. And we've also declared our highest ever quarterly dividend of INR 11.70 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR35.10 per share.

items.statement: Volume guidance of around 7 million tonnes for FY27, implying ~15% growth over FY26
items.quote: Based on this, we expect our volumes to be in the range of around 7 million tonnes for FY '27.

items.statement: EBITDA per tonne expected to reach close to ₹600 in FY27 from ₹445 in Q4 FY26
items.quote: I think in the current year itself, we should be very close to ₹600 because the significant improvement for us has come from the cost itself Mr. Rajat.

items.statement: Pending capex of ₹190 crore for three ongoing projects (Andhra ₹140 cr, Gudipadu ₹17 cr, Jeerabad ₹33 cr) to be completed in FY27
items.quote: Yes, ₹190 crores is the total CapEx that is pending for three ongoing projects, but there is undrawn credit.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of ~₹50 crore per year across all units
items.quote: the general maintenance CapEx across all the units should be around ₹50 crores sir.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA/tonne at ₹445 vs ₹218 in Q4 FY25; structural cost efficiencies from WHRS, solar, logistics and plant upgrades to drive improvement
items.quote: Our EBITDA per tonne for the quarter stood at ₹445 as against ₹218 per tonne reported during Q4 FY '25. Going forward, we expect profitability to improve, supported by structural cost efficiency initiatives.

items.statement: Pet coke prices up from ~$120 to $136-140 CIF; potential ₹100-150/tonne cement cost impact from mid-Q2 if sustained; inventories cover till mid-Q2
items.quote: At cement level, it should definitely add close to ₹100 to ₹150 on the current kind of a blend for us. But we expect things to shape up better and fairly quickly, but we have inventories all the way up to middle of Q2.

items.statement: Total pencilled cost increase of ₹225-250/tonne including fuel, bags, explosives and diesel hike
items.quote: we have pencilled in almost additional ₹100. So we are factoring around ₹225 to ₹250 per tonne kind of a price increase on account of both fuel and as well as miscellaneous expenditure.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook across core regions; state-wise growth estimates: AP/Telangana strong, Tamil Nadu 5-10%, Karnataka 5%, Odisha 5%, Madhya Pradesh 5-7.5%
items.quote: we do expect a strong demand growth in both Telugu states of AP and Telangana. Yeah, we do expect anywhere between 5% to 10% growth in Tamil Nadu. Karnataka, we expect a 5% growth for the coming year.

items.statement: New Superfine Building Materials division approved (GGBS/fly ash ultra-fines 10k-20k Blaine); targeting minimum 30% EBITDA margin; premium pricing vs commoditised GGBS
items.quote: what we do except is off of 30% kind of a margin as a minimum in that business line.

items.statement: Vizag land monetisation expected ₹350 crore over 18-24 months (₹150 cr Year 1, ₹200 cr Year 2); net ₹3.5 cr/acre on 100 acres
items.quote: Net of expenditure, we are likely to receive around ₹3.5 crores per acre. And we have around 100 acres. So we were expecting ₹350 crores spread over two years' time.

items.statement: Amalgamation of Andhra Cements with Sagar Cements approved in principle by Board (March 30, 2026)

items.quote: As far as the current geopolitical situation is concerned, we may see short to medium-term structural changes play out. I think we are keenly watching out for the macro environment.

items.statement: New subsidiary Kirloskar Advanced Systems formed for defense and systems integration opportunities
items.quote: We have incorporated a new subsidiary called Kirloskar Advanced Systems Private Limited. We believe there's significant potential in advanced technology, particularly to serve key accounts in sectors like defense.

items.statement: Netherlands subsidiary incorporated for efficient international structuring and energy transition technologies
items.quote: Given international is a very big component of our five-year goal, it's just important for us to structure ourselves efficiently as we're growing to create value for our stakeholders.

items.statement: Management reiterated 15% AUM growth guidance for FY27, to be reviewed after Q1/Q2
items.quote: Always in the first quarter, we have always been giving a guidance of 15% only. So, as usual, last 10 years, we have been giving 15% guidance in the first quarter.

items.statement: Plans to open 200-300 branches at Muthoot Finance and ~200 gold loan branches at Belstar Microfinance in FY27
items.quote: Okay, so probably last year, we opened 170 branches or so. This year, maybe 200-300 branches. That's it.

items.statement: Raised interest rates by 0.5-1% on certain loan types last quarter, contributing to yield increase
items.quote: Last quarter, we increased our rates by about 0.5% to 1% over certain types of loans. So, that is why we see the yield has gone up.

items.statement: Reported yield of 20.76% includes one-off auction income (INR 50 cr) and ARC income (INR 35 cr); sustainable yield lower
items.quote: So, there was an auction income of about 50 crores. ARC, I think it is around INR 35 crores. So, totally INR 85 crores. And there was some increase in the pricing also in the last quarter.

items.statement: Stage 3 NPA rose to 2.34% due to RBI-mandated borrower-wise classification; LTV on NPA book only 58%, fully recoverable
items.quote: So, the stage 3 increase has happened primarily because RBI has advised us to do a borrower wise classification. So, earlier we were doing this classification at the loan level.

items.statement: Unsecured personal loan book ~INR 4,000 cr, mainly cross-sell to existing gold loan customers
items.quote: These are unsecured personal loans, salaried personal loan and unsecured personal loans, which is doing actually quite well. We have about INR 4,000 crores of portfolios, mostly cross-sell.

items.statement: Muthoot Money gold loan AUM grew 151% to INR 9,794 cr; received INR 1,000 cr capital infusion; credit rating upgraded to AA+
items.quote: Muthoot Money, which is doing vehicle finance, has been running down its vehicle finance business and has gone into the gold loan business. And gold loan, the AUM stands at INR 9,794 crores versus INR 3,900 crores last year, a growth of 151%.

items.statement: Belstar Microfinance collection efficiency improved to 99.85%; opened 81 gold loan branches to diversify
items.quote: The collection efficiency in the microfinance increased by 0.69% and now stands at 99.85%, which was 99.16% last year.

items.statement: Declared highest ever dividend of 300% (INR 30/share); 14th consecutive year since IPO
items.quote: Muthoot Finance declared the highest dividend of 300% or INR 30 per share and this is the 14th year of consistent dividend declaration since our IPO in 2011.

items.statement: Assessments order book for FY27 is 80-85% of FY26 full-year revenue, indicating healthy revenue growth ahead
items.quote: As we speak, the order book for FY27 for the Assessments business is almost close to 80 to 85% of the entire revenue we achieved in the full year of FY26.

items.statement: EdTech profitability to improve from Q1 FY27 despite flat revenues, due to cost structure recalibration
items.quote: While revenues may stay flat for another four quarters before they begin to see an uptick, on the profitability side, we will definitely see the needle beginning to show a positive upward movement from Q1 itself.

items.statement: MarTech targeting steady revenue growth with enhanced margins over next 12-24 months via mix shift to CEP, VOSMOS, VIRSA
items.quote: With enhanced focus over the next 12 to 24 months, this business should continue to grow at a steady, stable revenue growth rate with enhanced margins.

items.statement: Assessments EBITDA grew 50% YoY to ₹51 crore on 9% revenue growth, showing operating leverage
items.quote: The assessment business revenue grew from ₹ 205 crores to ₹ 223 crores, generating an operating EBITDA of about ₹ 51 crore versus ₹ 34 crores last year.

items.statement: EdTech average realization down 12-14% YoY due to shift to modular products at ₹2,000-4,000 vs full programs at ₹30,000-60,000
items.quote: The average realization saw a dramatic downward movement of about 12 to 14%, which resulted in our overall revenue declining by about 11% from the previous year.

items.statement: Higher education enrollments expected to grow from 4.5 crore to 8 crore in 5-6 years, 60% via online programs from top 200 universities
items.quote: The expected growth of higher education enrollments in colleges and universities is expected to grow from 4.5 crores to 8 crores. And about 60% of them are expected to come through online university programs offered by the top 200 universities.

items.statement: CL-DEXIT empaneled with top 200 NIRF universities for enrollment, job readiness, career training and placement
items.quote: Among these top 200 universities, we will now begin our work to help them in enrollment, job readiness and career training, and also placement.

items.statement: RPS capital reduction of ~₹193-194 crore (including interest) pending NCLT approval; order reserved, next hearing tomorrow
items.quote: The cash that was left behind was approximately ₹ 182 crores, and it has generated interest during the time it has been with us — for almost a year — to the tune of about ₹ 11 to 12 crores. So as on date, there are approximately ₹ 193 to 194 crores of the cash that you see on our balance sheet which belongs to NSE.

items.statement: Expects double-digit or high single-digit billing growth, double-digit revenue growth, and PAT more than doubling in Q1 FY27 vs Q1 FY26
items.quote: We are highly confident in delivering robust financial performance, anticipating either double -digit billing growth or high single-digit growth in billing, double-digit revenue growth and more than doubling of profit compared to Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Expects double-digit or high single-digit billing growth for full FY27
items.quote: We expect double digit billing growth also possibly this year as well. So, the high single digit growth or double -digit growth for the FY’27 as well.

items.statement: Matchmaking EBITDA margin improved to 22% in Q4 FY26 from 19.2% in Q3 FY26 and 17.7% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for the Matchmaking business in Q4 is at 22% as compared to 19.2% in Q3 and 17.7% a year ago.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 12.4% in Q4 FY26 from 11.3% in Q3 FY26 and 10.8% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our EBITDA margins in Q4 are at 12.4% as compared to 11.3% in Q3 and 10.8% a year ago.

items.statement: Matchmaking average transaction value increased 15.3% YoY and 3.6% QoQ in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Average transaction value for the Matchmaking business increased by 15.3% year-on-year and 3.6% over previous quarter.

items.statement: Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets combined are larger than Tier-1 market
items.quote: Tier-2, Tier-3 combinied is bigger than Tier-1 market.

items.statement: Opened first Elite Matrimony Center in Hyderabad in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Considering the immense potential to grow our Personal Service segment, we opened our first ever Elite Matrimony Center in Hyderabad in Q4 of FY26.

items.statement: Wedding Services segment losses widening; breakeven not expected in near future, focus on product-market fit
items.quote: In terms of when it will breakeven, definitely it's a long way to go. But it's more of getting the product market fit and getting the opportunity right, then it's more of scaling up.

items.statement: Marketing expenses expected to remain at similar levels (around INR 180 cr annually) unless strong need to change
items.quote: The marketing expenses at this point of time is expected to be at the similar level until otherwise if there is any strong need to increase or decrease. So, we tend to operate at a similar level.

items.statement: ManyJobs monetization started in Tamil Nadu with 1M+ users and 10K+ companies; may expand to South or pan-India by year-end upon revenue milestones
items.quote: Currently, we are starting only in Tamil Nadu, we already got more than 1 million users registered to ManyJobs platform and more than 10,000 companies are using it. We started monetizing. So, again, still in the early stages. So, the end of the year, once we reach our revenue milestone, then we may expand to South or e

items.statement: Completed share buyback of INR 58.5 cr in Q4 FY26; will continue evaluating shareholder reward opportunities
items.quote: We completed a share buyback in Q4 of FY26, amounting to INR 58.5 crores to reward our shareholders. We will continue to evaluate opportunities to reward our shareholders in the future as well, subject to necessary Board and Shareholders’ approval.

items.statement: Invested in AI-based astrology startup 'Bharat Ek Khoj'; early stage, monitoring progress
items.quote: In terms of investment on the’ Bharat Ek Khoj’, it's an investment into one of the AI -based astrology company. It's a recent investment. It's one of the startup. So, we see an opportunity. And so it's a startup and we will continue to monitor.

items.statement: Luv.com (serious matchmaking) launched, early stages with good traction in metros
items.quote: We also got into serious matchmaking . We launched Luv.com. And again, still in the early stages, but having a good traction. So, Luv.com is a serious matchmaking service from Matrimony.com group.

items.statement: Standalone revenue growth guided at 10-15% with EBITDA margins of 10-15% for FY27
items.quote: For the standalone business, we expect revenue growth of 10% to 15% with EBITDA margins in the same 10% to 15% range.

items.statement: Innoxel revenue growth guided at 35-45% with EBITDA margins of 20-25% for FY27
items.quote: For Innoxel, we expect revenue growth of 35% to 45% with EBITDA margins of 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Varenyam Healthcare revenue growth guided at 20-25% with EBITDA margins of 8-13% for FY27
items.quote: For Varenyam Healthcare, we expect revenue growth of about 20% to 25% with EBITDA margins of 8% to 13%.

items.statement: Standalone order book stands at INR 171 crores providing visibility for FY27
items.quote: The order book today stands at INR 171 crores, which gives us reasonable visibility for FY '27.

items.statement: Varenyam Biolifesciences facility approved budget INR 160 crores, CWIP INR 33 crores, 20% complete
items.quote: Our approved budget is around INR 160 crores and our CWIP at the year-end was around INR 33 crores. So we're about 20% of the way through in terms of cost.

items.statement: Standalone capacity utilization at 48% General, 21% beta-lactam, 24% cephalosporins with headroom for 10-15% growth without fresh capex
items.quote: We are at 48% on the General, 21% on beta-lactam, and 24% on cephalosporins. There is meaningful headroom here and we don't need fresh capex to grow the standalone business by 10% to 15% next year.

items.statement: Varenyam Healthcare to expand field force to 250+ and launch 7 new products including Remishot and second gynecology division in FY27
items.quote: We expect the field force to expand upwards of 250 people, seven new product launches including Remishot, which will be India's first made-in-India and the launch of our second division, which will operate in gynecology.

items.statement: Innoxel FY27 EBITDA margins 20-25% driven primarily by milestone payments, commercial CMO supply starting Q2 FY27
items.quote: This would be for FY '27 on the margin front at Innoxel primarily it would be due to milestone payments because though the commercial supplies will start it is -- it would still be for maybe two or at max three products and not more.

items.statement: Standalone growth impacted by PIC/S and EUGMP inspections in FY27 causing production disruptions, full recovery expected by FY28
items.quote: We still expect a little bit of disruption due to two major audit events which would be at the standalone facilities which is, like I said, PIC/S and EU GMP. So there would be certain disruptions due to, owing to those.

items.statement: Varenyam Biolifesciences commercial supply delayed to Q4 FY29 due to geopolitical disturbances causing 3-month delay
items.quote: The current geopolitical disturbance has had an impact on the, I wouldn't say too much of an impact, but we are 3 months, at least one quarter running behind on schedule as to what we had expected earlier.

items.statement: Innoxel targets 10 new filings, 20 new partner deals (10 advanced), first MHRA and Health Canada filings, out-licensing income INR 70-90 crores in FY27
items.quote: Additionally, I would like to point out that there would be 10 new filings from Innoxel this year. 20 new partner deals which are targeted, out of which 10 are at advanced stages of discussions and due diligence, our first MHRA and Health Canada filings during the year, and overall out-licensing income is expected betw

items.statement: $27 million standalone tender order supply resumed, 90% to be covered in FY27 with small spillage into FY28
items.quote: I would say that we would be covering 90% of that remaining 90% of the order in this year, and then there would be some spillage that we expect, which would be a smaller spillage in the next year, start of next year.

items.statement: Innoxel two 505(b)(2) assets on track: one Europe filing this month, US filing Q3 FY27; other US filing Q4 FY27
items.quote: We plan on filing this asset in Europe later this month. Going forward, I would say that for this particular asset, the US bio studies once completed, the target date for filing the product would be somewhere in Q3 of this FY '27. And as far as the other 505(b)(2) oral liquid product is concerned, that the target date

items.statement: Innoxel Q4 FY26 turned EBITDA positive for first time at INR 1.4 crores, full year EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 6.9 crores from INR 30.4 crores
items.quote: In Q4 FY '26, Innoxel turned EBITDA positive for the first time. We did INR 1.4 crores of EBITDA in the quarter against losses in every prior quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth guidance of 12-13% for FY27 excluding GLP-1 upside
items.quote: As a consol, we are looking at around 13%, 12% to 13% growth. So it's a mix of both Cenexi and base business. This is excluding the GLP, whatever we get upside on that.

items.statement: Four-year consolidated CAGR target of 15%
items.quote: The next four years, we're looking at a CAGR of 15% at a consol basis.

items.statement: Cenexi FY27 revenue target of close to EUR200 million
items.quote: So we might touch about close to EUR200 million in FY '27 but the majority of the growth might come next year when we put up this additional line in August of this year, that will add capacity.

items.statement: Cenexi FY27 EBITDA target of mid to high single-digit margin
items.quote: So for FY '27, our target is to reach at least mid-single digit, high single-digit EBITDA. By the end of this year, we should get there, yes.

items.statement: Cenexi mid-term EBITDA margin target of mid-teens
items.quote: The ongoing investment in capacity increase and the fast-growing business pipeline reinforce our confidence that we will achieve our mid-term objective of a mid-teen EBITDA.

items.statement: Capex outlay of INR2,000 crores over next five years for capacity expansions
items.quote: To cater to this demand, we are investing in the capacity expansions, capex outlay of INR2,000 crores over the next five years.

items.statement: Major CDMO project expected to commercialize in H2 FY28 with USD25-30 million annual revenue potential
items.quote: One of the major CDMO projects announced earlier is progressing well and is expected to be commercialized in H2 of FY '28 with an estimated annual revenue potential of USD25 million to USD30 million.

items.statement: Base business CDMO expected to contribute additional $40-50 million revenue in FY27
items.quote: So FY '27, it's almost, I would say, [$]40 million, [$]50 million will come from CDMO. See the additional growth coming from the CDMO contracts in FY '27 will be between [$]40 million to [$]50 million.

items.statement: Cost efficiency programs contributing 1-2% margin improvement
items.quote: On the cost front, our focus on yield improvement, alternate sourcing, energy optimization and process efficiencies continues to deliver results, contributing to approximately 1% to 2% margin improvement.

items.statement: CDMO business grew 28% YoY and represents 46% of total consolidated revenues in FY26
items.quote: For the full year FY '26, our revenue stood at INR64,307 million, registering a growth of 14.5%. Adjusted EBITDA came in at INR16,826 million, with margins of 26%, while adjusted PAT stood at INR10,455 million, with margins of 16%. The CDMO business represented 46% of total revenues supported by healthy growth of 28%.

items.statement: Strong demand for Dalbavancin and multivitamin launches expected to be meaningful contributors in FY27 and beyond
items.quote: Dalbavancin has been launched in U.S. and European markets and is already seeing strong demand and ramp-up. Similarly, our multivitamin portfolio is expected to have a steady revenue contribution. These products are expected to be meaningful contributors to growth in FY '27 and beyond.

items.statement: GLP-1 revenue excluded from guidance due to dependency on partner approvals and volumes
items.quote: As we said, we are not actually talking any numbers for GLP. Even the guidance we're giving is excluding GLP because it all depends on these partners getting approvals in different markets and volumes. So we're not giving any numbers out yet.

items.statement: Cenexi adding new high-capacity ampoule line in Fontenay by 2027 adding 30 million ampoule capacity
items.quote: We are also actively preparing the replacement this summer of another old ampoule line with a new high-capacity line that will add additional 30 million ampoule capacity by 2027.

items.statement: Base business EBITDA margin strong at 41% for Q4 and 38% for full year FY26
items.quote: For the base business, excluding Cenexi, adjusted EBITDA margin remained strong at 41% for the quarter and 38% for the full year FY '26, highlighting the inherent strength of our core operations.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth guidance of 12-13% for FY27 on constant currency basis
items.quote: So this is based on constant currency growth. So if any fluctuation currency happens, then that will be an upside.

items.statement: Base business EBITDA margin guided at 33-35%, consolidated at 25-26%
items.quote: So we still guide for the year as a base business around 35%, 33% to 35% and as a consol basis, around 25%, 26% EBITDA.

items.statement: Cenexi targeting mid-teen EBITDA margin in midterm
items.quote: So we are looking at mid-teen EBITDA level in the midterm.

items.statement: INR 2,000 crores capex planned over next 3 years plus INR 300 crores this year
items.quote: So around INR2,000 crores, we're investing in the next 3 years in addition to about INR300 crores this year.

items.statement: INR 500 crores capex expected in FY27
items.quote: FY '27, we expect about INR500 crores.

items.statement: INR 650 crores from base business and INR 150 crores from Cenexi (ex-forex, ex-GLP-1) driving FY27 growth
items.quote: So together, about INR650 crores is from the base business and about INR150 crores will come from the Cenexi business excluding the forex and the GLP-1

items.statement: Key growth drivers: RTU bag portfolio, complex injectables/suspensions, sterile API complex injectables, CDMO (CMS project, pen devices)
items.quote: I think our CDMO pipeline is very strong, I would say. The RTU bag portfolio is strong again. So several products in that, they are under patent and which goes off patent. So that is one big growth driver. One is the complex injectables, suspension products.

items.statement: Cenexi Fontenay site at ~100% utilization, Osny solid orals at ~90%, two other sites at 50-60%
items.quote: So Cenexi, some sites are operating at full level. Like Fontenay is at almost 100%. That's why we kept -- we'll add a line and one more line we're adding, replacing that so that we can increase the capacity. So there is a demand -- higher demand than what we are able to supply today. Osny again, solid orals, it's almos

items.statement: Middle East conflict may cause 1-2% revenue impact from vial/glass cost increases (5-6% supplier requests) and solvent delays
items.quote: But from vials and glass, yes, there is a request from the suppliers to increase it by 5% to 6%. So we are studying the impact on the long run. It's too early to tell, but probably there could be an impact of 1%, 2% overall.

items.statement: GLP-1 revenue excluded from FY27 guidance due to uncertain approval timelines, mostly post-2030 US volumes
items.quote: Like I said, our guidance is ex-GLP, want to see how the market forms and when these customers get approvals and how many units they can sell. So it's too early to give a guidance on that.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to improve as Cenexi profitability improves, blended rate to come down from ~30%
items.quote: Tax rate will improve because Cenexi profitability as it improves, there will be -- the blended tax rate will be better. It will come down.

items.statement: GLP-1 cartridge capacity 140M units (all GLP-1), insulin to utilize 30-40M units until 2030 ramp-up
items.quote: So the insulin vial and cartridges might occupy 30 million to 40 million in the next couple of years. It will be a ramp up, but at least that will cover till 2030, majority of the costs.

items.statement: Guides FY27 capex at INR 40 crores including retail expansion
items.quote: overall capex for this year will be around the INR40 crores.

items.statement: FY26 net cash capex outflow was INR 70-75 crores after supplier credit netting
items.quote: Net cash out for capex would be about INR70 crores, INR75 crores.

items.statement: Capex of INR250-300 crores over 2 years (FY27-28) for multi-sector capacity expansions
items.quote: as far as the capex is concerned, it's a rough figure.we're looking at around INR250 crores to INR300 crores of capex, which we are looking at to build all these capacities, multiple capacities for the customer.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity target ~0.5x for next 2 years; will use debt for capacity expansion, repaying as cash flows allow
items.quote: we wanted to maintain a debt-to-equity ratio of, for next 2 years, in the range of around 0.5. We'll see how it goes.

items.statement: Nuclear order book INR650+ crores to execute over 3-3.5 years; expects more orders from reactor refurbishment (5 reactors) and new builds (Mahi Banswara/ASHVINI tenders this year)
items.quote: MTAR has been in civil nuclear program for more than 35 years. And now, we have the strongest order book of INR650 crores plus, and all these orders have to be executed over the next 3 to 3.5 years.

items.statement: Management declined to provide FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance due to macro uncertainty and geopolitical events
items.quote: We are waiting for this Chinese summit to end, then this Russia summit to end to understand where the world stands in terms of crude oil, what is our supply positions in terms of crude oil. We are so dependent on macro that it is very difficult to really tell you how do we see this financial year.

items.statement: Performance Chemical 2 plant commercialization expected by September 2026; validation in Q3, commercial production in Q4, ramp-up in FY28
items.quote: So I think typically, validation Q3, commercial production -- I mean, commercial, some business Q4 and then pick up FY28. So it's a standard process.

items.statement: FY27 capex budget estimated at INR 80-100 crores; Clean Fino-Chem greenfield capex possible in H2 FY27
items.quote: It could be in the range of max INR80 crores to INR100 crores.

items.statement: HALS quarterly volume exceeded 1,000 tonnes in Q4 FY26, up from 350-360 tonnes/quarter 8 quarters ago
items.quote: I think, overall, we did about over 1,000-plus tonnes for the quarter.

items.statement: Clean Fino-Chem subsidiary achieved first positive EBITDA of INR 7 crores in Q4 FY26; March HALS utilization ~40%, blended realization INR 460/kg
items.quote: Company reported a positive EBITDA of INR 7 crores in Q4, marking its first quarter of positive EBITDA following an EBITDA breakeven performance in the preceding quarter.

items.statement: HALS export mix shifted from 20% to 50% in select products; exports growing to Europe, Middle East, US; exploring Southeast Asia and LatAm
items.quote: Earlier, we were predominantly India import substitute. We were only trying to cater majorly to Indian market. So we were roughly 80% India, 20% export. Today, we stand at 50% export in select products.

items.statement: Favorable HALS product mix improving with higher-grade HALS (including HALS 2020) scaling; debottlenecking and backward integration underway for key intermediates
items.quote: And I think over the period, our expensive grades of HALS are also being -- I mean, we have been able to also start selling those on larger scale.

items.statement: Chinese raw material cost advantage (phenol, acetone) creating price arbitrage; imported majority of phenol/acetone from China in recent months; June still competitive
items.quote: I can tell you, we bought majority of phenol and acetone from China, which was never the case in last many years.

items.statement: Promoter directors forfeited substantial performance bonus for FY26; bonus reduced to <1% of PBT vs entitled 4%, saving ~INR 11 crores
items.quote: Consequently, the performance bonus for FY26 is reduced to less than 1% of PBT as against entitled 4% PBT for this financial year.

items.statement: Board declared final dividend of INR 4 per equity share (400% of face value)
items.quote: the Board in today's meeting has declared a final dividend of INR 4 per equity share, amounting to 400% of face value of INR1 per share.

items.statement: Hydroquinone/Catechol plant (commissioned Dec 2025) under stabilization; expects optimal operations in 1-2 quarters; currently at 10-15% utilization
items.quote: Very low. It's quite low compared to what we -- yes, it is less than -- it is 10%, 15%-odd right now. And we want to ramp up.

items.statement: Pharma intermediate plant refurbished and converted to HALS intermediates; dropped pharma intermediate product
items.quote: We realized there is too many issues which we did not anticipate. And fortunately, we were able to refurbish those plants very quickly to make the HALS intermediates where we were dependent on just some Chinese sources.

items.statement: Noida hospital expected to break even in second half of FY27
items.quote: So we do expect this unit to break-even during the course of this year. But I would say that probably we would look at the second half of next year rather than to look at giving you a number on Q2.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR 800-900 crore; FY28 at INR 600-700 crore
items.quote: Capex spend for the year FY27 will be somewhere around INR 800 crores to INR 900 crores. Next year, it will be in the range of INR 600 crores to INR 700 crores.

items.statement: Total project capex over next 5 years approximately INR 45,000 million
items.quote: Across the entire expansion pipeline, total project capex over the next 5 years is approximately INR 45,000 million.

items.statement: Noida hospital operationalized 382 beds, 98 ICU beds, 14 OTs; 200+ doctors onboarded
items.quote: We have operationalized 382 beds, 98 ICU beds and 14 operating theaters. The hospital has onboarded over 200 doctors and 75+ senior clinicians.

items.statement: Mature hospital margins stable at 24-25% range; Q4 FY26 mature margin 26.7%
items.quote: We are feeling fairly confident about the margin profile remaining in this kind of 24% - 25% range. We don't see any real reason for any kind of dips.

items.statement: No tariff hikes taken in Patna for 4.5 years; may consider increases in Patna and Lucknow based on market conditions
items.quote: Patna has been operational now for approximately 4.5 years. We have not taken a single rupee of tariff increase in Patna. So there may be some tariff adjustments that we may look at in Patna basis the market conditions there, maybe some in Lucknow as well.

items.statement: Strong demand across network; IPD volumes up 16% YoY, OPD up 19% YoY in FY26
items.quote: Volume growth remained robust. Inpatient count increased by 16% and outpatient count increased by 19% year-on-year.

items.statement: Competition in Gurugram from new hospitals; potential talent war for clinicians
items.quote: There is always a shortage of high-quality talent, and therefore, we will see some amount of a war for talent in the clinical side at least.

items.statement: Capital plan fully supported by internal accruals and project-specific debt; net cash INR 5,906 million
items.quote: The capital plan is fully supported by a combination of internal accruals and project-specific debt that we may take. Our balance sheet strength gives us the flexibility to execute this growth pipeline with appropriate discipline.

items.statement: Actively exploring inorganic opportunities including M&A and O&M partnerships beyond greenfield
items.quote: We are actively exploring various types of transactions, both pure acquisition as well as partnerships or O&M types of models beyond the greenfield.

items.statement: Greenfield projects (Varanasi, Guwahati, South Delhi, Mumbai, Pitampura) expected operational around FY30
items.quote: Maybe if you are sitting in May of 2026, you could say May of 2029 hospitals could be up and running. But that may not be FY29 numbers, that may be more FY30 numbers.

items.statement: Noida revenue INR 906 million, EBITDA loss INR 783 million in FY26; Q4 loss reduced to INR 236 million
items.quote: From a financial standpoint, Noida has delivered revenue of INR 906 million and an EBITDA loss of INR 783 million during FY2026. Importantly, Q3 FY2026 was the peak quarterly loss for Noida at INR 320 million. Q4 loss reduced to INR 236 million

items.statement: Developing hospitals (ex-Noida) margins improved to 31.5% in FY26 from 30.1%
items.quote: Our developing hospitals, excluding Noida, continue to outperform recording 29% year-on-year revenue growth to INR 14,130 million and EBITDA of INR 4,470 million, a growth of 35% with margins improving to 31.5% compared to 30.1% in the same period last year.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target set at around Rs 800 crore
items.quote: For FY27, the target is around 800 cr.

items.statement: FY27 capex limited to ~Rs 20 crore for maintenance and balance needs
items.quote: we expect only around 20 crore of maintenance and balance CAPEX during financial year 27
