items.quote: ADR grew 13% to INR 12,500. RevPAR grew 10% to INR 8,000 and TRevPAR grew at 12% to INR 15,000.

items.statement: Batim Land branded residence project in design stage; plan to raise capital for this development
items.quote: Batim Land, a branded residence, is also work in progress at design stage. So we plan to, as I've explained in previous quarters, raise some capital on that.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue INR 2,666 crores (+24%), EBITDA INR 1,299 crores (+28%), margin 49% (+200bps); PAT crossed INR 500 crores
items.quote: For the full year FY26, revenue stood at INR 2,666 crores up 24%, while EBITDA grew at 28% to INR 1,299 crores. Full year EBITDA margin improved to 49% compared to 47% last year.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected to be better than FY26's 26.7% YoY growth
items.quote: Compared to '26, better. We are going to do better '27.

items.statement: Current order book approximately INR1,000 crores with 8-10 month execution timeline
items.quote: Current order book approximately today we have order in hand approximately above INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex INR40 crores; FY27 planned INR65 crores for Greenfield project (total INR130 crores over 2 years)
items.quote: FY26, I think we invested in INR40 crores. And coming '27 we are planning to -- 2 years, coming 2 years INR130 crores we are going to invest on one facility.

items.statement: Existing plant modernization: INR35-40 crores planned for FY27
items.quote: last year we invested INR40 crores, another INR35 crores to INR40 crores we are going to invest.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin pressure from commodity price increases and deliberate manpower investments for future growth
items.quote: On margins, Q4 saw some pressure on EBITDA, primarily driven by commodity prices increases in key input raw materials. We are also making deliberate investments on manpower as we gear up for what we expect to be an even stronger year ahead.

items.statement: Export revenue doubled in FY26 vs FY25; expecting similar growth in FY27 with global inquiries across Europe, US, Middle East
items.quote: compared to last year this -- the FY26 our revenue is doubled, export revenue. So we are expecting '27 also this is going to grow.

items.statement: C2C Engineering FY26 revenue INR24 crores, targeting INR60 crores in FY27 with INR46-47 crores order book
items.quote: This year actually we finished with INR24 crores. And next year we are targeting INR60 crores is possible, INR60 crores.

items.statement: Scigenics FY26 revenue ~INR20 crores, targeting INR60 crores in FY27
items.quote: FY26 Scigenics did, I think INR20 crores something we did, this year -- only -- because of last quarter only we that full -- but the total I think this year also we are going to touch INR60 crores.

items.statement: Metal price volatility impacting margins; company booking raw materials immediately upon order receipt to hedge
items.quote: Yes, some challenges already they are facing. Because today metal cost is X, tomorrow is X plus one. That is, we are facing already, not only us, whole industry is facing. So once order received immediately we are also against, we are also booking the raw materials.

items.statement: M&A strategy confirmed: combination of organic and inorganic growth for sustainable expansion; acquisitions planned but not just for adding numbers
items.quote: So, the organic growth, the combination of organic growth and the inorganic growth is necessary for our sustainable growth. So, we're not just looking at one or two -year growth, but we are looking at the sustainable continuous growth. So, yes, the answer is yes, we will be acquiring some companies in the future.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15-20% over FY26's INR 1,007 crore; traditional product margins stable, BESS converter margins targeted to improve from 10-12% to 17-18% at scale
items.quote: The guidance is around 15% and 20%. With regards to our traditional product line, I think we are happy with the margins where we are. Maybe a couple of points here and there because of the conflict and the related price increases. With regards to BESS, I need to make it clear, whatever is the battery pass-through at th

items.statement: Consolidated order book exceeds INR 1,400 crore (1.4x FY26 revenue); QP standalone INR 520 crore, Mehru INR 430 crore, Endoks INR 450 crore; added INR 600+ crore fresh orders in Q4
items.quote: We enter FY27 with an order book of over INR 1,400 crores, about 1.4x last year's revenue.

items.statement: New Sangli factory (global coil, HVDC, PCS, CTC, magnet wire) targeting Q3 FY27 commissioning; Mehru INR 17.2 crore GIS/high-voltage test capex; Endoks PCS facility at Nigde targeted December 2026; new Turkey expansion under evaluation
items.quote: capital work-in-progress has scaled to INR 73 crores, reflecting active deployment across the Sangli global coil manufacturing facility, the HVDC, PCS, CTC, magnet wire facility on track for Q3 FY27 commissioning. Mehru's INR 17.2 crores capex program for GIS and high-voltage testing equipment, and the new Endoks PCS f

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 23.5% (vs guided ~22%), Q4 19.1% due to INR 25.7 crore non-cash Ind AS 29 hyperinflation charge; normalized FY26 PAT would exceed INR 210 crore; gross margin expanded to 47.7% in Q4
items.quote: normalized for this Ind AS 29 charge, our consolidated PAT for FY26 would have crossed INR 210 crores. I would strongly encourage analysts to model Endoks on an Ind AS 29 normalized basis when projecting forward, treating these monetary loss or gain entries as below-the-line non-operating items.

items.statement: Strong pipeline >INR 1,100 crore for QP alone (FACTS, renewables, data centers); robust visibility across Middle East, Europe, US, Australia; US data center reactor market estimated INR 1,500 crore/year; HVDC opportunities in Australia, Ind
items.quote: Our business pipeline remains highly encouraging as we currently pursue opportunities exceeding INR 1,100 crores for QP alone, including strong opportunities in FACTS systems, renewables and data center infrastructure. Demand visibility continues to remain robust across the Middle East, Europe, the United States and Au

items.statement: Board approved enabling authorization to raise up to USD 75 million for international expansion, acquisitions, technology investments; promoters waiving dividend entitlement to conserve cash; funds to be called as needed
items.quote: The board has also approved an enabling authorization to raise up to USD 75 million across permissible modes, strategic dry powder for international expansion, acquisitions, and technology investments.

items.statement: Execution challenges in insulators and winding conductors; mitigation via in-house cable manufacturing; geopolitical tensions, logistics disruptions, commodity volatility, supply chain constraints persist; Ind AS 29 hyperinflation accountin
items.quote: We are currently facing certain execution challenges related to insulators and winding conductors. However, mitigation initiatives are already underway, including our own cable manufacturing initiatives that will improve supply reliability going forward.

items.statement: Sangli factory trial production expected July-August 2026; peak revenue potential INR 1,500 crore subject to CTC cable expansion and insulator supply resolution; Mehru capacity headroom ~20-30% (from ~INR 320 crore base); new Turkey expansi
items.quote: Sir, the Sangli factory, I think the peak revenue that we can go in is about INR 1,500 crores, subject to we completing our CTC cable expansion and clear out our insulator problems. With regards to Mehru, I think another 20%, 30% before they scale down, because the plant would then saturate.

items.statement: Targets INR 1,500-1,800 cr order book before FY28 start; current consolidated order book ~INR 1,400 cr
items.quote: I think we should be targeting at least INR 1,500 crores to INR 1,800 crores of order book before the start of next year.

items.statement: PCS (Power Conversion Systems) for BESS now in production at Turkey; orders US$31 mn booked, targeting US$80 mn this year; revenue to flow next FY
items.quote: US$31 million is already in the back. We believe another US$50 million is our target internally. So, that would mean that at least $80 million is what we carry forward next year from the production.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin ~46% in Q4; management expects near-term dip of a few percentage points in Q1-Q2 due to commodity volatility but booked orders at similar/higher margins
items.quote: I cannot guide the same kind of numbers, but I can only guide that when we booked it, we booked it at similar or higher margins. We may have some small change in margins in the next one or two quarters, but that would be a short-term impact.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through occurs with a lag; no price variation clauses in contracts
items.quote: It will be done with a lag. It will be done with a lag.

items.statement: Supply chain constraints (insulators 18-24 month lead times) capping growth; geopolitical risk in Turkey acknowledged but 16-year track record cited
items.quote: Even if we ship the cables on time, there are insulators where the deliveries are already going 18 to 24 months. So, some of our projects are getting hurt because of some critical components.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,920-1,950 crores, implying ~30% growth in Prefab division
items.quote: So this FY27, we are targeting a growth of 30% in our Prefab division. So it will take us to around INR1,920 to INR1,950 crores kind of a revenue for this year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 10.5%-11.5% range for FY27, with at least 10%+ throughout the year
items.quote: Our guidance has always been that it will be range bound between 10.5% to 11.5% and we could achieve 10.5% last year. FY27 also our guidance is the same, it will be at least 10% plus throughout the year.

items.statement: FY27 capex of ~INR150 crores for three capacity additions: Mambattu line 2, Ghiloth greenfield, Gujarat greenfield
items.quote: We plan to do a total capex of close to INR150 crores in this financial year to ramp up our capacities for the fabricated steel and the sandwich panel line.

items.statement: Gujarat greenfield (50k tons PEB) capex ~INR100-110 crores (INR38 crores spent on land); commercial production from FY28
items.quote: Close to about INR100-INR110 crores, out of which we have already spent about INR38 crores on the land and the balance like I said is about INR60-INR65 crores we will spend on building the capacity.

items.statement: Ghiloth sandwich panel line capex ~INR90 crores (of INR102 crores total); operational Q3 FY27
items.quote: When we are doing it in Ghiloth, Rajasthan, then we have earmarked a total capex of INR102 crores. So, in this, the capex towards the sandwich panel line, I would say is almost 90%, so it works out to be INR90 crores.

items.statement: War-related uncertainty minimal; companies proceeding with capex due to government scheme commitments; order inflow and pipeline strong
items.quote: Since last 1 month we've seen, people or companies have been going forward with their capex plans because they understand this is a short-term phenomena and they don't want to derail their expansion plans.

items.statement: PAT margin expected to improve to ~6.5% in FY27 from 6.1% in FY26 due to ~20-25bps finance cost reduction from debt repayment
items.quote: 6.1% is what we have done last year, and going by the impact of the reduction in the finance cost, which will be to the tune of 0.2% to 0.25%, it will add up on that. So yes, we can predict the PAT at around 6.5% easily.

items.statement: Peak capacity revenue potential ~INR2,300-2,400 crores (147k tons PEB + sandwich panel + EPS business)
items.quote: On a peak capacity level, you know, 1,50,000 -- 1,47,000 of PEB capacity plus sandwich panel is about 2,200-2,300 plus EPS business of about INR 200 crore. So the revenue at the moment is about Rs. 2,300-2,400 crores at a peak capacity level.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin target early double-digits; 100-120 bps annual improvement till FY28, then 200-250 bps annually
items.quote: We believe in a business like this, early double-digit steady-state EBITDA margins are sustainable. So, that's the view we have. And I think the way we have planned for is that for the next couple of years, we are giving a guidance of 100 basis points to 120 basis points in terms of improving profitability till FY28.

items.statement: Pin codes expanded from 15,600 to target 17,000 by end FY27; 120-150 new pin codes added monthly
items.quote: We have hit 15,600 pin codes out of the 19,300 available pin codes in India. We'll be hitting about 17,000 odd pin codes by end of FY27.

items.statement: Lost shipment/quality cost at 6.1% of revenue in Q4 (down from 6.3% Q3); target 4-5% long-term
items.quote: Q4 it's come down further to 6.1%. Our view is in the longer term, we actually we felt even 5% was a high number. Our long-term goal was to bring it down to about 4% to 5%.

items.statement: 3PL market share ~28-29% in Q4 FY26 vs ~17-18% year ago; gaining from weaker 3PLs and some captive insourcing
items.quote: As part of the 3PL industry, and as per our internal estimate, we have hit about close to 28%, 29% market share for the full quarter, which would have been about close to 17%, 18% one year back.

items.statement: Expects sustained BOPET margin improvement for 18-24 months and significantly stronger FY27
items.quote: Our take is that when we look at the global supply- demand dynamics and the domestic supply-demand dynamics, we see that the sustenance of BOPET margins is going to continue for around 18 to 24 months at least.

items.statement: Targets VAS film share to grow from 25% to 60%+ in 2-3 years to reduce cyclicity
items.quote: Our target is to grow this 25% share of VAS films to 60% plus in next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Expects Specialty Polymers revenue to reach INR200 crores in FY27 with 20% growth trajectory
items.quote: We are confident. We would not like to be specific with the numbers, but the plans that we have, and the detailed annual operating plan that we have prepared, we should be achieving that number.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin 15.5%; expects margins far better than last 12-15 months average
items.quote: Excluding mark-to-market and reinstatement losses of INR10.24 crores on foreign currency term loan, adjusted EBITDA would have been INR53.6 crores, implying an adjusted EBITDA margin of 15.5%

items.statement: Expects ROCE >20% in next 8-10 quarters as performance normalizes
items.quote: in the next 8 to 10 quarters, we are going to get a return on capital employed of more than 20%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 average BOPET spread INR32-33/kg for 12-micron VA; expects Q1 FY27 spread INR30-35/kg
items.quote: the average spread in Q4 was around INR 32 to INR33 for 12-micron VA, right? And as we go into this quarter, we are expecting that the average for this quarter should be somewhere between INR 30 to INR35 as well.

items.statement: VAS films grew 14.5% YoY in FY26 to 25% of volumes; rPET volumes surged 258% YoY to 5,325 MT
items.quote: The volume of VAS products stood at 25% of total sales volume in FY 26. In volumetric terms, the growth in VAS products was 14.5% despite adverse effect of USA volume loss partially due to the trade tariffs.

items.statement: Secured INR165.25 crores against INR175 crores share warrant issue post balance sheet date
items.quote: We are pleased to report that subsequent to balance sheet date, the company has successfully secured INR165.25 crores against its INR175 crores share warrant issue.

items.statement: Targets net debt reduction of ~INR45 crores in FY27 (INR85 crores repayment vs <INR40 crores new borrowing)
items.quote: the total repayment is around INR85 crores for the next year. And we are trying to limit our borrowings for the next year to below INR 40 crores. So that is going to give me a leverage of INR45 crores on the debt side.

items.statement: Existing asset base can generate INR2,000-2,200 crores revenue at 100% utilization with minimal growth capex until ELITe
items.quote: with the current asset base, if we run at 100%, we are looking at INR 2,000 crores to INR2,200 crores kind of turnover.

items.statement: Targets double-digit volume growth for FY27 long-term; near-term margins may compress if raw material inflation persists
items.quote: We do see, obviously, as we move ahead, that this would come to a double-digit sort of a growth from a long-term perspective

items.statement: Implemented ~9.7% price increase in Decorative by mid-May 2026; RMC inflation at 24-25% implies ~13.5% cost pressure, leaving 3-4% gap
items.quote: As we speak today, till the 15th of May when tomorrow, when the last tranche of a price increase gets executed, we would have taken close to about 9.7% of price increase

items.statement: EBITDA margin protected at ~14.4% in FY26 despite price cuts and elevated spends; near-term compression risk from raw material inflation
items.quote: we could largely protect our EBITDA percentages last year comparable which is and we are at around 14.4%

items.statement: Offtake growth similar to volume growth; pre-buy limited to 1-2 weeks; demand recovery seen but crude/forex volatility remains key risk
items.quote: Basically, we see offtake also on the similar line. And as a result, yes, though there is a little bit of pre-buy, but offtake which we capture through is also on the similar lines

items.statement: Strong order book in Marine & Protective (oil & gas, blade, dry-dock); Coil business won marquee projects including Navi Mumbai Airport
items.quote: Marine and Protective, we've had one of the highest revenues in the month of March. It's -- we've got strong order book in oil and gas infrastructure and both on blade and dry-dock business

items.statement: Capacity utilization 55-60% decorative, 70-80% industrial; cross-manufacturing with JSW Paints underway; capacity expansion and localization planned
items.quote: Currently, we operate anywhere between 55% to 60% on decorative paints and on performance on our industrial products, we are even as high as 70%, 80%

items.statement: Key risks: elevated raw material inflation (crude/forex), competitive intensity, integration execution; margin compression possible for a quarter if RM stays high
items.quote: the journey ahead, if it continues at these elevated levels, we'll see a bit of compression maybe for a quarter on the margins

items.statement: Cultural integration progressing well; HR integrated; dealer integration for projects done in 7 metros; retail integration early next year; SAP integration targeted post-Diwali
items.quote: On the second part, which is on the dealer integration, we've only integrated our projects business. Starting in Mumbai and then now in 7 metros in the later of this month, will be integrated teams selling both JSW Dulux and JSW Paints

items.statement: Final dividend of INR 50 per share approved for FY26; real estate sale completed in March 2026 yielding INR 64.8 crore
items.quote: the Board has approved a final dividend of INR50 per share, the financial year at '25-'26, which is subject to the shareholders' approval

items.statement: Target 25-30% revenue CAGR to reach INR 1,000 crore by FY29-30 from INR 370 crore in FY26
items.quote: The target revenue is to grow and take this company in the short term to a INR 1,000 crore company. We are looking at a 25% to 30% target revenue growth CAGR till FY29. FY29 -2030 is when we are looking at hitting a INR1,000 crore mark.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR 500 crore+ with double-digit EBITDA margin (10%+)
items.quote: We are looking at a double digit plus actually. We are looking at a 10% plus margin EBITDA margin and we are looking at a INR 500 crore plus top line as well.

items.statement: Target double-digit EBITDA margins (10-13%+) driven by R&D, cost control, and solar power installation
items.quote: We're also targeting to take this up even higher to double digit EBITDA margins, going up from 10 % to 11 % to 12 %, and then 13% plus EBITDA margins, stabilized and sustainable EBITDA margins.

items.statement: INR 20-30 crore capex planned for ancillary machines, flux cored wire lines, and facility shift from Thane land
items.quote: So we are looking at shifting those to another facility where we've already identified around INR20 crores to INR30 crores of capex on ancillary and these flux code wire lines and everything.

items.statement: Flux cored wire production starting July 2026 targeting INR 50 crore+ annual revenue; import substitution via BIS mandate
items.quote: We are planning to get around more than INR50 cr. revenue from flux core wires every annum. We are starting for July and then we will keep adding the lines of the same.

items.statement: Strong demand across power (nuclear, thermal, hydro), railways (bullet train, metro, 20,000+ bogies), defense (INS Vikrant, submarines), and exports (TUV approval for EU)
items.quote: So, these three sectors and power, railway, export, all these three centres are going to drive. And fourth is the defence. There's a major investment.

items.statement: Defense orders expected to double to INR 25 crore; Inconel pending orders >20 tons; Cobalt alloy business to double from INR 10 crore
items.quote: Last year, I think we have got a share of more than INR10 cr. to INR 12 cr. of that particular project. And this year, which we are planning that it will go more than double.

items.statement: Able to pass on commodity inflation to customers with ~1 month lag; prices 6-7% below ESAB/Ador in retail, at par in projects
items.quote: Whatever the inflation happening, of course, it does take time to pass on it over, but we are able to pass it over all our whatever increase in price to our end customers. It takes a month to transfer.

items.statement: Q1 seasonally weak due to monsoon and labor shortage; working capital cycle elongated but improving via asset monetization
items.quote: Q1 is something very slow driven compared to all other quarters. As you know, the Q1 where there is extreme shortage of labour across all the sectors.

items.statement: Thane land monetization to generate INR 400+ crore over 5 years; proceeds for dividends, share value growth, and acquisitions (welding equipment, safety, maintenance) targeting INR 2,000 crore in 5-6 years
items.quote: The Wagl e Industrial Estate is where the company already has more than 13,000 approximate square meter of land parcel, which it will, it's planning to develop into commercial space and unlock its value and generate cash flows of more than INR400 cr. approximately into the company over the next five years.

items.statement: Solar power installation planned this year or next to improve EBITDA margins and reduce finance costs
items.quote: Soon, this year or next year, we are also planning to install solar power into our factories, which will also, it was a good, it will help us to improve our EBITDA margins, and as well as our finance cost, I think will considerably will go down in the current year compared to last year.

items.statement: Export revenue <10% currently (INR 350+ crore domestic of INR 370 crore); targeting 3x export growth in 2 years via TUV, ADNOC, Saudi, Russia approvals
items.quote: Export currently, of course, doesn't even constitute 10% in the few years back it did. But right now, the majority of the revenue is coming, I think, hardly out of INR370 crores, around INR350-plus crores comes from domestic.

items.statement: EBITDA target INR 45 crore for FY27 (annualized from Q4 INR 11 crore) despite Q1 seasonality
items.quote: So INR45 crores of EBITDA, of course, is something that we are looking at for this year as well.

items.statement: TIG wire TUV approval underway for EU market access targeting 250+ tons/month export; cladding fluxes submitted to BHEL Trichy for testing
items.quote: This year, we are also planning to take approvals of TUV, and which will give us opening in Europe market and especially after India and European market treaty that there will be 0% duty. So, we believe that we will have a good chance and it will be opening an exposure for around more than 250 tons per month to export

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth estimated at 20-30% driven by Alloys and Relays ramp-up
items.quote: I would put the estimate between 20% to 30%, maybe more also depending on the orders that we click in the Alloys business and Relays business.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 15-18% similar to current levels
items.quote: Yes, EBITDA, roughly that level, 15%, 17%. 15% to 18% you can say.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR 40-50 cr for PML and INR 40-50 cr for Quantum Magnetics
items.quote: It could be between INR 40 crores to INR 50 crores for PML itself and another INR 40 crores to INR 50 crores could be the plan in Quantum, roughly.

items.statement: Alloys division furnace at 80-90% utilization in Q4 FY26; targeting 3-4x revenue in FY27
items.quote: utilization was almost at about 80%, 90%, almost full capacity we utilized until the end of the year. And now ramp-up, approximately, as per current estimates, we are looking this year to about, let's say, in financial year '27 to maybe about 3 to 4 times what we have done in the last year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 Alloys sales mostly virgin metal (lower margin); FY27 expects mix of virgin and scrap
items.quote: In the last quarter, we did more of the virgin metal alloy sales. Orders were there more for that product. And in coming year, it's a mix of both.

items.statement: Relays commercial ramp-up expected H2 FY27; peak revenue potential INR 25-50 cr at full capacity
items.quote: we can expect maybe in FY27 maybe between INR 25 crores to INR 50 crores, maybe something like this could be possible.

items.statement: Quantum Magnetics Phase 2 (block cutting, machining) implementation Q3-Q4 FY27; assembly sales ~INR 10-15 cr in Q4 FY27
items.quote: FY27, we will, because now we are implementing Phase 2, so that will happen by July to November sometime. And then after that December onwards, sales should start. So that we are estimating maybe about INR10 crores, INR15 crores, something like that may happen in quarter 4.

items.statement: Chinese export restrictions on rare earth magnets caused zero revenue in FY26; customers shifting to light rare earth alternatives
items.quote: There was no revenue in FY26 because of the restrictions from China for export of magnets. So, we could not do any business in FY26.

items.statement: Relays capex ongoing; initial INR 5-6 cr spent on testing equipment; production equipment purchase depends on order finalization
items.quote: The initial capex we have done for testing equipment and end of the line equipment all that we have done. The production equipment, some of it is yet to be purchased.

items.statement: Capex funding via combination of debt and equity; $5 million ECB already taken in subsidiary
items.quote: So, we will do a combination, maybe in debt and equity, maybe we will do. That we are yet to finalize.

items.statement: New consolidated factory near Vasai (Ahmedabad highway) to merge 6 Mumbai plants; INR 20 cr capex allocated (land already acquired)
items.quote: We have around 6 plants here in around Mumbai. So, we will be combining all 6 plants together at one place, where we have purchased land on Ahmedabad highway near Vasai.

items.statement: Long-term Quantum Magnetics target 5,000 tonnes capacity by FY30-31; potential revenue INR 3,000-4,000 cr
items.value: INR 3,000 crores to maybe INR 4,000 crores
items.quote: And in totality, 5,000 tonnes, depending on the sale price, it can range from somewhere between, let's say, INR 3,000 crores to maybe INR 4,000 crores, something like that, 5,000 tonnes.

items.statement: Relays addressable market INR 6,500-7,000 cr for 25 cr meter replacement; per meter value INR 250-300
items.quote: The total addressable market is about for the entire 25 crores meter replacement, you can say it can be about between INR 6,500 crores to INR 7,000 crores.

items.statement: Relays project delayed; commercial ramp-up now H2 FY27 vs original timeline due to longer testing and customer approvals
items.quote: On the Relays project, we are behind the original timelines with commercial ramp-up now expected from second half of financial year '27. Testing is currently underway and customer approvals are in progress, both of which have taken longer than our initial expectations.

items.statement: Consolidated sales growth guidance for FY27 is 4-4.5%, or 11-12% excluding Foskor and Awuko revenue
items.quote: At the consolidated level, we expect the sales to grow approximately 4 % to 4.5 % in FY27. However, if we exclude the revenue contributed from Foskor Zirconia and CUMI Awuko, which accounts to INR 343 crores in FY26 sales, and compare it with our business plan, comparable growth will be 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Consolidated Abrasives sales growth guidance for FY27 is 5.5-6%, or 11-12% excluding Awuko
items.quote: Consolidated Abrasive sales are expected to grow by 5.5% to 6%. However, if we exclude the revenue from Awuko, which is about INR 108 crores in FY26, sales growth will be 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Consolidated Ceramics sales growth guidance for FY27 is 15-15.5%
items.quote: Consolidated Ceramic growth is expected to be in the range of 15 % to 15.5%.

items.statement: Consolidated Electrominerals sales expected to decline 6.5-7% in FY27 due to Foskor closure, but grow 8-9% excluding Foskor
items.quote: Consolidated Electrominerals sales are expected to decline by 6.5% to 7% on account of the closure of Foskor Zirconia, which accounted for INR 235 crores in FY26. However, if we exclude the revenue contribution from Foskor Zirconia in FY26 and compare it with what we are planning to do in FY27, the growth would be 8% t

items.statement: Consolidated Abrasives margin guidance for FY27 is 9.5-10%, up from 7.9% comparable in FY26
items.quote: Consolidated Abrasives margins are expected to be around 9.5 % to 10%. The reported margin in FY26 is 4.3 %. However, if we exclude Awuko losses, the comparable margin % for FY26 would be 7.9 %. So, basically, it will grow from 7.9 % to 9.5 to 10 %.

items.statement: Consolidated Ceramics margin guidance for FY27 is 20.5-21%, up from 20.2% in FY26
items.quote: Consolidated Ceramics margin would be 20.5 % to 21%. The reported margin is 20.2 %.

items.statement: Consolidated Electrominerals margin guidance for FY27 is 9-9.5%, up from 9.1% comparable in FY26
items.quote: Consolidated Electrominerals margin could be 9% to 9.5%. In FY26, the reported margin is 5.6%. However, if we exclude the loss of Foskor Zirconia and compare it, the FY26 margin would be 9.1 %. So, basically, from 9.1, it would be 9. 0% to 9.5%.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 is approximately INR 400 crores
items.quote: We expect to do a CAPEX of about INR 400 crores in FY27.

As you will probably see in the balance sheet today, there is a significant amount of liabilities that have been held for disposal that has been reported. And we don't expect to receive anything as a result of this asset sale process.

items.statement: Standalone FY26 revenue INR 973 crores (+25% YoY), EBITDA INR 121 crores (+28% YoY), PBT INR 100 crores (+63% YoY); net debt/equity 0.28x, working capital days improved to 142 from 159, ROCE improved to 21.16% from 12.40%

items.quote: Out of that, the investment-related impairment, that INR 153 crores that will be -- that's a capital loss. So that will be available for us for the future for, any capital gains set off, whereas the other items have been used to offset against the profits made during the current year.

items.statement: Semiconductor equipment anchor customer progressing well; discussions with 2-3 other semiconductor customers in preliminary stages; >80 new product introductions completed in FY26

items.quote: We feel fairly confident that we will maintain these high-teen EBITDAs, which we've been giving guidance for.

items.statement: Ashoka brand targeting 30-35% growth in FY27 via deeper penetration, new markets, new products

items.quote: So I would say the growth is more 60%, 65% towards the volume growth. There has been some benefit with the devaluation, but majority of the growth has come through with volume growth.

items.statement: PLI incentive INR16 crores in FY26; final year of scheme in FY27 with similar amount expected
items.quote: So from a PLI perspective, for the full year, our number is roughly around INR16 crores for FY '26.

items.statement: Surat facility to contribute INR40-50 crores in FY27; full capacity potential INR200-250 crores by Year 3
items.quote: So we expect in terms of revenue around INR40 crores to INR50 crores contribution from the Surat facility in this fiscal year. At its full capacity, the Surat plant will give us upwards of INR200 crores in top line.

items.quote: Our growth is coming to 7% to 8% as an industry. And we do expect that, that growth is likely to happen in Venky's also.

items.quote: Up to September, I think we'll be doing equivalent, if not better than this quarter.

items.statement: Poultry Q4 FY26 operating margin ~14% driven by broiler realization and input costs; management expects similar future performance subject to ingredient prices
items.quote: With regard to quarter 4, the main attributing factor was broiler realization and, of course, input costs. So that is the reason why the percentage and the overall absolute profit was higher.

items.statement: Animal Health Products EBITDA margin 29% in Q4 FY26; full year FY27 expected to sustain 22-23%+ despite raw material cost pressure in Q2-Q3

items.quote: In April, as far as the prices of broiler is concerned, it is ranging somewhere around INR97, INR98, or say INR100 is round figure.

items.statement: Poultry demand strong: non-veg share of poultry risen from 35-40% to >55%; consistent placement by integrators reducing volatility; industry growth 7-8%
items.quote: If you see overall pie graph of non-veg segment, earlier, poultry was having 35% to 40% in non-veg segment. Now it is crossing more than 55%.

items.statement: Animal Health shifting to natural solutions, therapeutics (new plant), expanded distribution (6-7 day nationwide reach); exports tiny (<2-3%) but growing
items.quote: We started developing a lot of products for the natural solutions, which is into those kind of growth promoters, which was natural.

items.statement: Oil Seed increasing outside sales from 20% to target 33% of DOC production; outside revenue target 60-65% vs 35% in-house; reduces group dependence
items.quote: We are trying to increase it to 1/3 of our production of a DOC. So that means our dependence on the group will become lower and our 60% to 65% revenue will be coming out from the outside the group only.

items.statement: CCI investigation notice received regarding parent breeding farm practices; Venky's India Limited not directly affected as it doesn't deal in those products
items.quote: This CCI investigation is regarding certain practices in the parent companies or the parent breeding farms in which Venky's as such, do not deal in those products.

items.statement: Maize/soya price volatility expected due to global factors (Brazil/Argentina cheaper), crude oil, ethanol policy; but availability sufficient
items.quote: The price is there, which are fluctuating in nature, but we don't see much impact on that because of the global factors.

items.statement: No plans to increase debt or working capital limits; sufficient working capital (INR160 cr) and inventory in place; receivables down to INR544 cr from INR553 cr despite higher turnover

items.quote: The Board has further approved INR101 crore for the expansion of epoxy-led formulated resins capacity by 36 kilotons per year, increasing the total formulated resins capacity to 50 KTPA. The same is expected to be commissioned by Q2 financial year '28.

items.statement: Overall FY27 capex guidance range of INR 1,000-1,200 crore including approved and pipeline projects.
items.quote: So that should be in the range of around INR1,000-INR1,200 crore including the normal capex as of now, which has been let us say approved by the board, but we have few projects in the pipeline as well.

items.statement: Fenesta Building Systems order book up 15% year-on-year.

items.quote: PBDIT for the segment improved by 68% to INR39 crore led by higher prices and further supported by lower energy costs and better operating efficiencies.

items.statement: Current ECU (electrochemical unit) realization at INR 32,000-33,000 per metric ton for lye.
items.quote: The current ECU is in the range of INR32,000 to INR33,000 per metric ton.

items.statement: Fenesta seeing good demand with record order book; retail cost pass-through difficult but institutional contracts have tolerance-based pass-through.
items.quote: Now in terms of your second question on demand, I think we are seeing good demand even now. If you see our Q4 numbers also, they were pretty good. So, we have had record order book. So, demand is pretty good right now.

items.quote: Now actually the plant is running at close to 60% to 70% capacity utilization and we a re ramping up the capacity. The product approval from customers has been coming in regularly and so we expect a steady ramp-up in the coming next quarter or two.

items.statement: Raised funds via sustainability-linked NCDs from IFC in March 2026, integrating ESG targets into capital structure.
items.quote: Further, in March 2026, we have raised funds through the sustainability -linked non -convertible debentures from the International Finance Corporation, IFC. This partnership is more than a financial transaction. It is a global validation of our ESG roadmap.

items.statement: Ethanol sector viability at risk: OMC allocations only 1,100 crore litres vs 1,900 crore capacity; sugarcane-based feedstock restricted to 28%; policy misalignment with cane costs.
items.quote: Against a national capacity of ~1900 crore litres, OMC allocations stand at just about 1100 crore litres, with share of sugarcane-based feedstocks restricted to a mere 28%. This penalizes integrated players who invested in distillation capacities based on stable blending assumptions.

items.statement: CEO targets 25% revenue growth for FY27 but emphasizes uncertainty and will assess quarter-by-quarter; aims to maintain 12-14% operational EBITDA margin
items.quote: What we want to achieve is 25%. But to tell you specifically where we will end up is quite difficult. Even all the uncertainty is in front of us.

items.quote: We are positive that we will be able to operate between 12% to 14%.

items.statement: Zetor tractor exports targeting 1,000 units in FY27; aim 5,000-6,000 units by FY30 with new variants launching this year

items.statement: Price increase taken end of April across power tillers and tractors; commodity and fuel inflation rising, full pass-through difficult but operational efficiencies buffering impact
items.quote: We have taken a price increase towards end of April. We are watching this closely. If this continues to grow or inflation continues to sustain, it will be difficult to pass on the entire inflation to the consumer.

items.statement: Electric weeder and tiller launched; all-India rollout planned for early Q2 FY27 after real-world testing
items.quote: We are intending to do a all India wide launch across India in early Q2 of this year.

items.statement: Retail finance penetration target 20% in FY27 (up from 10% in FY26) via Project Chatrapati village-level expansion
items.quote: We want to grow it to 20% retail finance this financial year.

items.statement: Inventory disciplined at 36 days; receivables reduced from 75 to 51 days with further improvement targeted via TOC supply chain and SRM digitization
items.quote: We are at about 36 days of inventory. In FY25 we had taken receivables to about 75 days. We have brought it down this year to 51 days.

items.statement: Music vertical (licensing, artist management, retail) revenue CAGR guidance of 20-23% with annual EBITDA margin of 60-65%
items.quote: For the music vertical, which is licensed music, artist management and retail, all combined, we continue with our medium-term guidance of 20-23% CAGR in terms of revenue with our annual EBITDA guidance for this vertical being anything between 60-65%.

items.statement: New content budget for FY27 expected between INR 300-350 crores
items.quote: It's also part of the presentation that we are expecting our new content budget to be anything between INR 300-350 crores this year. That's a range it will be in.

items.quote: But the fact of life is, it's seeing no traction and all the music labels globally and in India are working very closely with the leading three global streaming platforms, making it very clear that when the content pool is going to get distributed across the labels, no value should get assigned to content which is gett

items.statement: Pocket Aces reached breakeven in FY26; profitability expected to improve further

items.quote: Our spend of INR 235 crores on new content was lower than what we had planned, and this specifically happened because some of the bigger movies that we had planned to release in Q4 actually got pushed.

items.quote: During this quarter, the company completed its strategic investment in Bhansali Productions through a significant minority ownership. items.statement: Confirms INR 1,000 cr cumulative new content investment over FY25-27; FY28+ to grow linearly at high single-digit to low double-digit YoY
items.quote: FY25, '26, '27 was INR 1,000 crores odd, and we will be in that ballpark in that space only. Our intent is from FY28 onwards increase it only in a linear fashion

items.statement: Video vertical (TV/digital series) targets 8-18% net margin with minimal capital allocation; short-format bets only in lakhs
items.quote: You're looking at margins that are anything between 8- 18% Net Margin.

items.statement: US revenue target of $375-400 million for FY28, not exit run rate

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration upwards of 20% and gross margins 58-60%

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin 18.1%, impacted by INR20 crore higher logistics/air freight costs

items.quote: We made the highest investment in R&D within the industry during FY26 with R&D expenditure amounting to 8% of revenue, which is around INR72 crores in absolute terms.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volume growth expected at higher end of 6-8% range; EBITDA per metric ton at higher end of INR19,000-21,000 range
items.quote: Q1, we are looking that you'll be able to -- we'll be delivering close to the higher end of the volume guidance range of 6% to 8%. And EBITDA as well at the higher end of the range of INR19,000 to INR21,000 metric tonne.

items.statement: Full year FY27 guidance conditional on Q1 conditions persisting; no formal FY27/FY28 guidance given due to geopolitical uncertainty
items.quote: If the current scenario continues the way it is, that's my rider. If nothing -- it may not improve, but it's not worsen. If this is the situation what we have in Q1 continues, I think we'll also be able to deliver that for the full year.

items.statement: No new growth capex commitments for FY27; only routine/replacement capex and some WIP capitalization expected
items.quote: I don't see any growth capex given what -- there may be some work in progress that will get capitalized. But nothing new commitments that we are seeing in this year other than certain brownfield that we do or we may do some routine capex, replacement capex.

items.statement: FY26 full year EBITDA per metric ton at ~INR19,000; Q4 FY26 at INR20,114/MT vs INR21,715/MT in Q4 FY25
items.quote: On a full year, we were at around INR19,000.

items.statement: AMET region demand expected to improve from Q1 FY27 as supply disruptions ease; no fundamental demand destruction
items.quote: So you're talking about degrowth that happened 15%, majorly was supply-led, very clearly, which should start getting taken care from the Q1 of this year.

items.statement: Raw material prices (petchem, oleochemicals) up significantly; pass-through to customers with lag; no weekly price changes possible
items.quote: Now everything has gone up significantly. In fact, petrochemical prices -- base feedstocks have gone up much more than the oleochemical feedstock prices.

items.statement: EPC project revenue not material in FY25/FY26; bulk of revenue recognition expected in FY27
items.quote: Bulk of it will be in this financial year.

items.statement: U.S. specialty pipeline reinitiated post tariff reversals; strong growth potential in premium specialty products
items.quote: Our specialty pipeline in the U.S. has been reinitiated post tariff reversals, and we are seeing encouraging traction and strong growth potential in premium specialty products.

items.statement: Launched Galsoft Lumithic, next-gen mild surfactant for cosmetics; self-thickening, amino acid-based, suited for sensitive applications
items.quote: We further advanced our innovation agenda with the launch of Galsoft Lumithic in in cosmetics Paris, a next-generation mild surfactant which is self-thickening, amino acid-based surfactant that simplifies formulation.

items.statement: Management declined to provide specific revenue or EBITDA outlook for FY27 and FY28, focusing on quarter-over-quarter improvement instead.
items.quote: We will not give any outlook at this point. I would like to believe that the good performance in this quarter is a start to many such good quarters. But at this point in time, my priority and my team's priority is going to be just dig our heels in here and try to do better quarter-over-quarter.

items.statement: Base business operates at 26% EBITDA margin and 54% gross margin; consolidated Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin was 16% at INR 61 crores.
items.quote: It operates at 26% EBITDA margin with gross margins of 54%.

items.statement: No greenfield or brownfield capex planned; focusing on incremental debottlenecking projects to unlock capacity for high-margin products.
items.quote: We are not planning to take up any greenfield projects. There's no big capex that we're going to invest. In our existing facilities itself, we have around 30% capacity available. So, I think it's going to be all about how smartly and wisely we can use this capacity for our high-margin products.

items.statement: Base business has a healthy order book driving strong utilization across facilities; no one-off spot orders or inventory restocking benefits.
items.quote: On the base business, Sajal, we have a very healthy order book, and you've seen that in our numbers as well. So I'm very encouraged looking at this order book and the utilization across our facilities that there is a strong performance, and it is not factors outside our control that are really favoring our business.

items.statement: Developed markets contribute 75% of sales; base business momentum driven by new customer acquisition, geography expansion, and share of wallet gains.
items.quote: Business contribution from our developed markets, which is our mainstay, continues to be at 75% of overall sales.

items.statement: Ibuprofen business recorded negative EBITDA; board appointed bankers to evaluate strategic options (sale or conversion to multiproduct facility), decision expected in H1 FY27.
items.quote: Our Board has appointed bankers to evaluate strategic options for ibuprofen, and we expect this process to finish in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Vizag facility mothballed since 2024, incurring INR 12-15 crores annual fixed costs; future use depends on ibuprofen strategic decision.
items.quote: However, we have certain fixed cost expenditure for the Vizag site which is INR12 crores to INR15 crores annually.

items.statement: No further capital raise planned after rights issue; internal target to become debt-free (including working capital debt) by FY29.
items.quote: We also concur with kind of similar views. So we have an internal target of making Solara debt-free by FY '29.

items.statement: Top 15-20 products contribute ~75% of revenue across ~70 commercialized products; no single molecule dependency.
items.quote: Roughly, we have commercialized close to 70 products in the entire portfolio, what we sell currently, of which roughly top 15 to 20 products has a mix of close to 75% of the entire business.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization ~70% in base business (ex-ibuprofen); 30% spare capacity available for growth without major capex.
items.quote: If you look at our capacity, we are currently using around 70% of our capacity. So, there is enough capacity -- there's around 30% capacity left that we can utilize.

items.statement: Debt reduced by ~INR 158 crores in FY26 (21% reduction); INR 113 crores from rights issue first call, INR 45 crores from operational cash flows; targeting ~INR 503 crores by end May 2026 after second call money.
items.quote: We have been able to reduce our debt by roughly INR158-odd crores during FY26, which actually signifies close to 21% reduction in the debt during the year, out of which INR113 crores came off from the first call money of rights, which we had in May '26. And then balance INR45 crores were actually paid off from our oper

name: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Ltd

items.statement: AUM target to cross INR5 lakh crore in H1 FY27; steady growth thereafter with replacement of low-margin railway assets by higher-margin diversified assets
items.quote: So going forward, we expect that in the year FY27, the magic figure of INR5 lakh crores for AUM, we should touch sometime in H1, maybe early to that, let us see.

items.statement: FY26 sanctions INR74,000 crore (vs guidance >INR60,000 crore); disbursements INR35,000 crore (vs guidance ~INR30,000 crore); key deals include DFCCIL refinance INR10,000 crore and HURL refinance >INR12,000 crore
items.quote: Against what we gave the guidance of INR60,000 crores, we crossed the mark or we reached the mark of nearly INR74,000 crores for the year in terms of sanction of assets. And against the guidance of INR30,000 crores for disbursement, we could do around INR35,000 crores.

items.statement: Tax-free status for 5-7 years due to accumulated depreciation; PBT=PAT; new metro leasing to replenish depreciation shield
items.quote: On tax, we have enough depreciation kind of thing in our kitty. So this company will remain tax-free with the kind of already accumulated depreciation that we have for next 5 to 7 years.

items.statement: FY26 PAT record INR7,000+ crore; net worth INR56,000+ crore; AUM net growth to INR4.85 lakh crore from flat INR4.6 lakh crore; Q4 PAT flat due to provisions/CSR but revenue up 9%
items.quote: We have crossed the magic figure of PAT of INR7,000 crores this year. Our net worth is consistently growing from INR52,000-odd crores, now it is INR56,000-odd crores plus.

items.statement: Management expects 25-30% year-on-year revenue growth for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: So with the current trend that is going on, we are quite optimistic that this trajectory of growth that has been witnessed in past few years should keep continuing. But our sense is that it could be more than 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Order book consistently revolving at INR3,000+ crores providing multi-year revenue visibility
items.quote: Our order book remains robust, revolving consistently over INR3,000 crores, providing multiyear revenue visibility and reinforcing confidence in our long-term growth outlook.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to be maintained at 44-45% year-on-year with minor variation
items.quote: So EBITDA would be -- remain on growth trajectory only. And probably what we believe is we should be able to maintain EBITDA of 44%, 45% year-on-year. It may vary 1% or 2% here and there, but no major movement.

items.statement: Strategic priorities: PEC contracts, higher capacity drilling rigs (2,000 HP), and offshore fleet expansion
items.quote: See, if we talk about top 3 priorities, of course, PEC is one. Second priority for us is higher capacity drilling rigs. And third priority definitely to add a fleet into offshore segment as well.

items.statement: PEC contracts have free gas price mechanism; higher gas prices increase order book value
items.quote: Yes, definitely. Because in PEC, we are having a free gas price mechanism. And as you rightly said, with increase in gas price, this order book can increase upward.

items.statement: New 2,000 HP drilling rig capex estimated at INR100-120 crores, funded through internal accruals and debt
items.quote: So our primary estimate is the rig can be of around INR100 crores or INR100 crores to INR120 crores, but that depends on the availability of equipment as well.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of INR500-600 crores submitted; new PEC tender (15-year) recently received but not yet bid
items.quote: It's close to around INR500 crores, INR600-odd crores.

items.statement: Dolphin Offshore expected FY27 revenue of INR150 crores with ~60% EBITDA margin on single asset
items.quote: But with the single assets which we are already operating, we are expecting top line of around INR150 crores from this financial year and the current FY27 with EBITDA of almost 60%.

items.statement: QIP plan cancelled due to improved cash flows
items.quote: No. So we have decided not to go ahead with QIP.

items.statement: Long-term vision: company could double in 3-5 years given government push and market share in onshore services
items.quote: But barring that, now that government has a great move, on this sector, it won't be surprised company could even get double in next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Management expects to sustain EBITDA margins in the 30-32% range going forward despite geopolitical uncertainty.
items.quote: However, we remain confident in the strength of our business fundamentals and our ability to sustain EBITDA margins in the range of 30% to 32% going forward.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR 540 crores, fully funded by internal accruals, focused on Solapur greenfield and R&D.
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY27, we plan to incur a capex of about INR540 crores, which includes carryover commitments from FY26 as well as fresh capital investments. Importantly, this entire capex will be funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: Solapur Phase 1 (370 KL BI block, 120 KL API block) expected operational in Q2 FY27; initial utilization 40-50%.
items.quote: Solapur Phase 1 is progressing as planned and is expected to be operational in Q2 of this year.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 360 bps to 33.6%, highest in history, driven by mix, cost management, and operational efficiency.
items.quote: We delivered EBITDA margins of 33.6%, expanding by 360 basis points, highlighting the inherent strength and operating efficiency of our business.

items.statement: Price erosion of ~5.5% on non-GPL, non-CDMO base business; raw material (solvents) and freight costs rising but largely passed through to customers.
items.quote: So on that, the price erosion is about 5.5% is what we have seen on the non-GPL, non-CDMO.

items.statement: Strong demand visibility across regulated markets; non-GPL revenue grew 13% YoY in FY26; chronic therapies 67% of revenue.
items.quote: Our revenue for the year stood at INR2,552 crores, registering a 6.9% year-on-year growth and in the non GPL business leading the momentum with 13% growth.

items.statement: Non-GPL contribution rose from 59% (FY22) to 71% (FY26); CDMO share increased from 6% to 7%; high-potency API pipeline advancing (12 validated).
items.quote: This is reflected in the strong and consistent performance of our non-GPL segment, whose contribution to the overall business has steadily increased over the years from 59% in FY 22 to 71% in FY 26.

items.statement: CDMO recovery from Q3 FY26; 4th/5th projects ramping; targeting 2 new CDMO deals in H2 FY27.
items.quote: So CDMO, the fourth and fifth project have kicked in really nicely. There's some revival even on the earlier projects. And so we expect that CDMO will continue this momentum. As far as new projects go, we hope to close 2 new deals in the second half early second half of this year.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflicts (war) creating supply chain constraints, elevated logistics/energy costs; Dahej fire caused INR 20 cr loss (booked in other expenses).
items.quote: From an expense perspective, yes, we have booked a loss due to fire in our other expenses to the extent of INR20 crores.

items.statement: R&D spend at 3.6% of sales in FY26; expected to rise to ~4% over next 1-2 years, focused on flow chemistry, HPAPI, pellets/granules, CDMO.
items.quote: As far as settling down, I don't think we'll cross 4%, right? We'll probably be at 4% in the next year or 2. And then it should settle down.

items.statement: Asset turnover may dip below 2x temporarily as Solapur/brownfield capacity comes online, but expected to recover as utilization ramps.
items.quote: I mean it would temporarily go down below 2 as well, right? But it would come back up once the utilization picks up, like I explained earlier.

items.statement: Net debt-free with INR 782 cr cash (Mar'26); generated INR 984 cr operating cash over 2 years, invested INR 472 cr capex, paid INR 61 cr dividends.
items.quote: As of 31st March 2026, our cash and cash equivalents stood at INR782 crores, with capex for the year being INR306 crores.

items.statement: Forex gain of INR 31 cr for FY26 (INR 11 cr in Q4) due to rupee depreciation; net exporter benefits.
items.quote: For the entire year on the P&L, we have seen a net gain of about INR31 crores on the P&L. There is about INR11 crores of gain that we have booked for Q4.

items.statement: Expects 15-17% revenue growth in FY27 and high-teen growth in FY28, excluding potential recovery of lost US business
items.quote: for fiscal 2027, what we expect as on date is maybe a mid-teen growth, 15% to 17% growth, something like that. And again, same kind of growth would be there or maybe a bit on a higher -- a high-teen growth in the fiscal 2028.

items.statement: Expects US order flows to resume meaningfully from Q1 FY27 as tariffs normalize
items.quote: With duties now normalizing, we expect U.S. order flows to resume meaningfully from Q1 of current fiscal, that is FY 2027.

items.statement: Annual capex of INR 30-40 crores minimum plus maintenance capex; broadly INR 50 crores per year for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: there would be there a minimum INR30 crores to INR40 crores bare minimum capex plus maintenance capex, etcetera, that would require for a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Monthly dispatch schedule of INR 115-125 crores for H1 FY27; expects INR 160-165 crores incremental revenue in FY27 from order book ramp-up
items.quote: on an average, INR115 crores to INR125 crores dispatches planned for this first half on a monthly basis.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded to 51.5% in FY26 from 49.4% in FY25 due to product mix shift and raw material management; expects normalized gross margin range of 49-53%
items.quote: our gross margin expanded meaningfully from 49.4% to 51.5% in fiscal 2026, reflecting the positive shift in product mix towards higher-value machine auto components and a better raw material management.

items.statement: Expects operating EBITDA margin not less than 20.5-21% on conservative basis, with potential improvement from scale benefits
items.quote: I expect on a conservative way, operating EBITDA would not be less than 20.5%, 21% kind of thing. And with the incremental growth, further it may improve because maybe I'll be getting the benefit of scale of economy and fixed cost absorption.

items.statement: Quarterly raw material cost pass-through with majority of overseas customers; half-yearly with a few customers
items.quote: With the majority of our overseas customers, we have a quarterly pass-on for the raw material cost. Maybe with a couple of customers, it's on a half yearly base kind of thing.

items.statement: Container availability delays of 2-3 weeks and extended transit times; managing with premium payments and inventory buffering
items.quote: there is a delay of maybe two to three weeks on availability of container and maybe a bit of extended transit days also. But we try to manage our inventory at warehouse and consignment stock.

items.statement: Board approved buyback of 1 crore shares at INR 180/share (INR 180 crores); promoters not participating; considering dividend but preserving cash for capex and uncertainties
items.quote: In April 2026, our Board approved a buyback of 1 crores shares at INR180 per share, aggregating to INR180 crores. The promoters /promoters group has chosen not to participate, ensuring that full benefit of this buyback flows directly to all public shareholders.

items.statement: Fully settled Right of Recompense obligation of INR 101 crores on March 31, 2026; now debt-free with no legacy obligations
items.quote: In March 2026, precisely on 31 st of March 2026, Rolex Rings has honored its Right of Recompense obligation in full, making total payment of INR101 crores to our consortium lenders.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 62-63%; forging equipment at 80-85% utilization in certain product ranges requiring capex
items.quote: My utilization is almost same what we had, as you have seen that my top line is almost at same -- this thing. So, we are in the range of 62% to 63% of utilization of my available or achievable capacity.

items.statement: Expect 200-225 net new stores in FY27, with KFC contributing 100-110 stores
items.quote: We expect to add approximately 200 to 225 net new stores in FY27 as DIL. KFC is expected to contribute 100 to 110 stores of these additions with the balance being driven by Costa Coffee, Biryani By Kilo and international businesses.

items.statement: Merger with Sapphire Foods on track for completion by end of current fiscal year
items.quote: We continue to expect completion of the merger by end of the current financial year.

items.statement: Tech-driven changes to be managed within existing budgets including Yum! charges
items.quote: we will be able to manage all the tech-related changes within our existing budgets, including whatever charges we pay to the Yum!.

items.statement: Ended FY26 with 2,256 system stores, net addition of 217 stores over last 12 months
items.quote: We ended FY26 with a system store count of 2,256 stores, representing a net addition of 217 stores over the last 12 months.

items.statement: KFC brand contribution margin improved to 17.0% in Q4 FY26, up from prior year
items.quote: Brand contribution grew nearly 20% year-on-year to reach INR 99 crore with brand contribution margins improving to 17.0% for the quarter.

items.statement: KFC menu price increase less than 0.5 percentage point on portfolio basis in recent quarter
items.quote: There was a very small correction. So, on a portfolio basis, I would say it was maybe less than 0.5 percentage point.

items.statement: International business grew 20% YoY, crossed INR 500 crore quarterly revenue for first time
items.quote: As a result, the international business grew 20% year-on-year and crossed INR 500 crore in quarterly revenues for the first time.

items.statement: Shifted KFC promotional focus from online to dine-in channel to drive store traffic and SSSG
items.quote: we have shifted the focus now more to dine-in and more to the dine-in customers. And therefore, we are tailoring the offers and the price points and the promotions to make sure that the dine-in customers are attracted

items.statement: Gas crisis continues in parts of country, monitoring closely; mitigating via electrical equipment evaluation
items.quote: The gas crisis continues to be an issue in some parts of the country, and we are still not fully out of it. We are monitoring the situation very closely and continue to effectively manage the situation.

items.statement: Discontinuing Tea Live brand in India and Thailand next quarter after testing
items.quote: Having tested Tea Live in India and Thailand, we have decided to discontinue the brand, and the same will happen in the next quarter.

items.statement: New leadership team largely in place by next quarter including CTO, CMO, COO hires
items.quote: I am happy with the progress made and feel very confident that we will be able to largely have the new team in place by next quarter.

items.statement: Pizza Hut SSSG -3.7% in Q4 but improved sequentially; ADS stable at ~INR 30,000/store/day
items.quote: While SSSG was at minus 3.7%, the SSSG performance improved on a sequential basis, with ADS remaining stable at ~INR30,000 per store per day.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 29-30% and PAT margin 19-20% for FY27
items.quote: We hope to keep margins stable between the 29% to 30% EBITDA margins as well as in the PAT around 19% to 20%.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR3,000-3,500 million for Site 5 and new R&D site
items.quote: The total capex for financial year '26 was INR3,838 million and the capex expected for financial year '27 is INR3,000 million to INR3,500 million.

items.statement: Remaining capex across Site 5 and R&D expansion ~INR1,500-1,600 crores over next 4 years
items.quote: It will be approximately all put together, the Site 5 is the major site and the Site 1 where we are expanding the R&D. So all put together, it will be approximately INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores, all in next 4 years.

items.statement: 3 new LSM products (2 pharma, 1 agro) from Site 5 to commission by May-end/early June; validation done, orders in hand
items.quote: There are 3 new large-scale manufacturing products, 2 in pharmaceutical and one agrochemical from Site 5, which will be commissioned by May end or starting of June 1st week. Validation batches are done and orders are already in hand.

items.statement: LSM pricing up >20% YoY and 18% QoQ in Q4; sustained in April-May; medium-term sustainable
items.quote: Pricing has been exceptionally strong over 20% year-on-year and 18% quarter-on-quarter in Q4. We believe this pricing environment is sustainable in the medium term.

items.statement: No demand disruption from oil market conflict; steady demand across products; no hoarding
items.quote: We have seen a steady demand in all our products as such. So there is no hoarding of material happening in this instance during this war.

items.statement: Target 70% revenue from CRAMS+CEM, 30% LSM over next 3-4 years; currently 55% CRAMS+CEM
items.quote: We are very confident of achieving our vision of 70% of revenues coming from CRAMS and contract exclusive manufacturing business models by fiscal year '30.

items.statement: Fire at external warehouse near Site 1 on Mar 11 '26 caused INR70M inventory provision; Site 2 fire claim settlement expected by end Q1 FY27
items.quote: Further, a provision for loss of inventory on account of fire at an external warehouse near Site 1 on March 11, '26 a mounting to INR70 million has been provided in Q4 of financial year '26.

items.statement: Debt to increase by INR200-250 crores in FY27 as QIP funds deployed; sequential drawdown
items.quote: Approximately by end of financial year '27, you can expect INR200 crores to INR250 crores additional in the debt, not more than that.

items.statement: Site 5: 4 of 16 blocks built, 2 ready for commercial production; 4 more blocks excavation started; 20 blocks total across Site 5 and Site 5+
items.quote: We have already completed the construction of 4 blocks. Two blocks are already ready to run. So water trials and solvent trials are ongoing. I think we'll have a good news very soon when we start the commercial production on 2 production blocks.

items.statement: Semiconductor materials: Phase 1 target 400 tonnes at $40-50/kg; opportunity seen tripling by 2030
items.quote: We are looking at producing on the first phase of 400 tonnes of particular set of molecules and where the average price would be $40 to $50 per kilo.

items.statement: Expecting margins to bounce back to previous levels in FY27
items.quote: No, no, we'll bounce back to our previous levels.

items.statement: Total portfolio 7.5 lakh sq ft with 4.92 lakh sq ft booked and 2.40 lakh sq ft available inventory
items.quote: Our total project portfolio consists of 7.5 lakh square feet, out of which 4.92 is booked and 2.40 lakh available inventory.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with capital employed around INR 80-90 crores as of March 31
items.quote: It will be upwards around INR80, INR90 crores.

items.statement: Dombivli hospital expected to reach EBITDA breakeven by end of 2 years of operation (calendar year end 2027-28)
items.quote: 2 years of operation, calendar year '26, we have started. So, calendar year end of, '27, '28, you should expect it.

items.statement: Dombivli EBITDA burn estimated at INR2-3 crores per month on average for the full year
items.quote: So, we have said between INR2 crores to INR3 crores a month on an average for the whole year.

items.statement: Total expansion pipeline of ~1,700 new beds across 4 greenfield projects at average cost of INR1.5 crores per bed
items.quote: Across the 4 hospitals in this cycle, from Dombivli all the way to BKC, the 1,700 beds will come up at an average cost of around INR1.5 crores per bed.

items.statement: FY26 capex deployment of ~INR500 crores for Dombivli, BKC land payment, Pune and Mira Road projects
items.quote: we deployed around INR500 crores in capex this year, Dombivli, BKC land payment , and ongoing Pune and Mira Road projects.

items.statement: Remaining 75% of BKC land cost to be paid in FY27
items.quote: It should be paid in this financial year. Everything will be paid in this financial year.

items.statement: Internal accruals over next 4-5 years plus debt at under 3x EBITDA expected to fund all announced projects
items.quote: Our current view is that the internal accruals over the next 4 -odd years, combined with debt at under 3 times EBITDA, should be sufficient to fund everything that we have announced.

items.statement: Pune South on track to open in calendar year 2028; Mira Road excavation expected to begin by end of 2026
items.quote: Pune South is on track to open in calendar year '28, as we had committed. Mira Road has completed its architectural drawings and is undergoing regulatory clearances. We expect excavation to begin by the end of the year.

items.statement: Key cost risk is depreciating rupee increasing capex costs; consumable costs linked to global supply chains being monitored
items.quote: On the cost side, the only thing that I am watching out for very keenly is the depreciating rupee and the cost of capex, so that is kind of a national reality.

items.statement: Insurance revenue share at 55.4% of total revenue; government revenue at 1%
items.quote: The insurance revenues now make up 55.4% of our revenue mix, while government stands at just 1%.

items.statement: Thane occupancy ~75%, Pune ~65%, Indore 45-50% for FY26
items.quote: For Thane, the occupancy has been around 75%; Pune, close to 65% and Indore is between 45% and 50%

items.statement: Indore Phase 2 expansion (111 beds) to be considered once occupancy crosses 60%
items.quote: Once the occupancy crosses 60% or near 60%, then we will think about the next phase of bed addition.

items.statement: FY27 launch target set at over INR150 billion GDV
items.quote: we are estimating that we'll do new launches in excess of INR150 billion

items.statement: FY27 sales target set at near INR100 billion
items.quote: we expect to do sales which are nearing INR100 billion

items.statement: FY27 revenue recognition and collection targets set at INR50 billion each
items.quote: Completion and collection go hand-in-hand and hence, we've kept a target of INR50 billion for both of these metrics

items.statement: FY27 PAT guidance between INR1,000-1,500 crores
items.quote: The number for the current year, I think, should be in between INR1,000 crores to INR1,500 crores

items.statement: JV with RMZ requires INR3,500-4,000 crores total capex over 4-4.5 years, Signature Global share ~INR1,500-2,000 crores
items.quote: about 5.5 million square feet, you should assume capex in the range of about INR3,500 crores to INR4,000-odd crores should happen by both the parties put together over the next 4 to 4.5 years

items.statement: Launched portfolio of 21+ million sq ft with GDV over INR30,000 crores; total portfolio 40 million sq ft with GDV over INR70,000 crores
items.quote: Put together, the GDV of both these sets of projects crosses INR700 billion, INR70,000 crores of GDV is there in between these 2 subsets of the portfolio

items.statement: FY26 gross margin ~30%, EBITDA margin 9-10%
items.quote: We generated a gross profit margin of about 30%, EBITDA margin of 9% to 10%

items.statement: Realizations crossed INR15,000/sq ft in FY26, up 20%+ YoY; expect normative inflationary increases in FY27
items.quote: per square foot realization crossed INR15,000 mark, which is, of course, a 20% plus realization on a per square foot basis vis-a-vis the previous year

items.statement: Global headwinds uncertain; NGT restrictions and excessive rains caused completion slippage in FY26
items.quote: There are certain global headwinds right now. No one can predict how that's going to pan out for the country or for the region

items.statement: Net debt reduced to near zero (~INR2 billion); operating cash flow INR21 billion in FY26 allocated to BD, debt reduction, approvals
items.quote: net debt is actually down to a near 0 level. It's just 2 billion, could have been positive or minus 2

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY27 maintained at 17-20% including new capacity ramp-up from H1
items.quote: At consolidated level with the planned capacity expansion and the current demand trends, we expect revenue to grow by 17% to 20% in FY27. It's the same guidance that we had in the previous call.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR250-275 crores for capacity expansion across moulding, writing instruments, wooden pencils and land development

items.statement: FY26 revenue INR972.9 cr, EBITDA INR97.9 cr, PAT INR68.6 cr; Q4 revenue INR286.2 cr (+27.6% YoY), EBITDA INR26.8 cr, PAT INR18.9 cr
items.quote: For FY26, the revenue stood at INR972.9 crores, EBITDA stood at INR97.9 crores, and the PAT stood at INR68.6 crores. items.quote: The order inflow we are expecting this year more than INR55,000 crores. That includes, of course, QRSAM, which we are expecting very soon.

items.statement: FY27 R&D investment target of around INR 2,200 crores
items.quote: So, this year, we have targeted a value of around INR2,200 crores investment in R&D.

items.quote: We have around USD96 million order book for this year and subsequent year. Some of the orders are to be executed in 2 to 3 years.

items.quote: So, I would imagine that there is no reason for us to believe that we should be able to maintain these margins and in for the effort that we put in mix, we will try and improve it.

items.statement: Phase 1 and 1A capacity expansion to be completed by end of December 2026.

items.statement: New products like 185 axle for tractor trailers will have marginally better profitability than legacy products.

items.quote: So, about 8% of it was a one-off. So, -- but on a like-for-like, it should be lower by around 8%.

items.statement: Expects pre-sales to grow at 25-30% CAGR.

items.quote: During this quarter under review, we were roughly at about 45% of utilization.

items.statement: FY27 revenue will be back-ended with quarter-on-quarter growth, similar to FY26.
items.quote: So, from FY '25 perspective, you'd see a quarter -on-quarter growth in quarters. But if you look at it historically, it will again be a back -ended H2 year for us.

items.statement: Margins expected to remain stable around 25% EBITDA, with mix-driven fluctuations.
items.quote: I'm very comfortable with our margins of what is 25% plus EBITDA. And sometimes it will go higher, sometimes it will go a little lower.

items.statement: No margin impact from commodity price increases due to rate contracts and pass-throughs.
items.quote: But we do not see that impacting both our supply chain procurement or therefore, our margins.

items.statement: Enquiry book nearly doubled to 18 GW for product segment; India up 100% to 7 GW.
items.quote: And that enquiry book for the product segment of 18 GW is, of course, nearly double of what it was in FY '25. The Indian market itself has also increased in its enquiry book by about 100% odd over this past year to about 7 -odd GW for us.

items.statement: U.S. enquiry book surged nearly 1000% to ~3 GW, driven by data centres and geothermal.
items.quote: we've see n, I would say, a near 1 ,000% increase in our enquiry book in North America, but this is driven by the fact that we had very low visibility. The enquiry generation in that market is somewhere in the range of about 3 GW odd

items.statement: U.S. subsidiary had ₹8 crore loss in FY26; expected to be profitable or breakeven in FY27.
items.quote: Though the full year itself, as you will see from the annual report when it's out and the subsidiary accounts still had a loss of about ₹8 odd crores in that subsidiary. In the coming year, we anticipate not only for that to reverse, but for it to be profitable, largely driven by greater execution.

items.statement: Receivables at ₹6.39 billion; expected to remain high in FY27 due to back-ended execution.
items.quote: receivables at the end of March 31, 2026, stood at ₹6.39 billion, primarily reflecting the execution profile of certain large projects as well as the billing, which was skewed towards the end of March, which will be liquidated in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Exports expected to exceed domestic in FY27; U.S. Aftermarket to contribute more to revenue.
items.quote: So as Mr. Nikhil said, we are looking at Aftermarket contributing more to the revenue in FY '27. Some of the product orders might take some time to execute, but we are quite confident that the conversions will be good.

items.statement: Mid-single-digit revenue growth outlook for FY27; profit growth targeted at close to 10%
items.quote: we're maintaining mid-single-digit growth outlook for the current year and then close to about 10% or so plus broad growth in the profits.

items.statement: Capex during FY26 reduced by more than half compared to FY25, reflecting disciplined capital allocation
items.quote: Capex during the year was almost reduced by more than half compared to FY 2025, reflecting disciplined capital allocation.

items.statement: Top 10 customers expected to grow 7-8% in FY27; new verticals in North America to drive growth above average
items.quote: across our top 10 clients, we should see growth more in the vicinity of about 7-8%, slightly lower than the average. It is the new verticals that will fire the growth. It is in North America, that would be firing the growth.
