items.quote: We've actually brought it down by 27%, and we had said we will be able to bring it down to about ₹80 crores in FY 2027. We remain positive that we will be able to bring it to ₹80 crores, beyond that ₹50 crores to ₹60 crores every year is going to be a recurring investment.

items.statement: Expects 6-7% tonnage growth in FY27 with at least 2% sequential quarterly growth
items.quote: In terms of volume growth, we are expecting to grow at least around 6% to 7% for the full year basis. And we are expecting that at least around 2% quarterly growth on a sequential basis even for the financial year '27.

items.statement: No exposure to bus business; promoter has separate bus company
items.quote: Currently, we are not into bus business. This company is -- the promoter and another company is having the bus business.

items.statement: Western DFC not a risk as commodities carried not linked to railway services
items.quote: DFC is directly related to the full truckload. So, the commodity what we are carrying is not directly linked with the railway services.

items.statement: Targets year-on-year EBITDA growth of over 20% for FY27.
items.quote: So we will be able to maintain year-on-year EBITDA growth of over 20% for FY27.

items.statement: Expects positive headcount on both half-year and full-year basis in FY27.

items.statement: Targets bottom-line growth upwards of 20%.

items.statement: Enterprise segment margin outlook is flattish; relies on operating leverage.
items.quote: And with respect to margins, the outlook is a bit flattish.

items.quote: On capital allocation, the Board has approved a buyback of up to 25% of free reserves at a price of INR1,600 per share to be funded from our existing free cash.

items.statement: Focus on scaling higher-margin businesses like Specialised Staffing and Degree Apprenticeship.

items.quote: Our plan is to reach 10% soon, but the question in the 10% is because it may look as a lower number, but the sales in 2W are also growing.

items.quote: To sum up, we expect a margin pressure of 50 to 100 bps at consolidated level, which is of temporary in nature and expected to normalize as macro environment improves.

items.statement: Enabling approval for debt raise up to INR10 billion; no immediate plan to raise incremental debt; INR30 billion capex to be funded through internal accruals
items.quote: We have also taken an enabling approval for debt raise of up to INR10 billion. To clarify, this is purely enabling in nature, and there is no immediate plan to raise incremental debt.

items.statement: Net debt reduced from INR25 billion (Mar'24) to INR19 billion (Mar'26) despite INR19 billion deployed in growth capex/acquisitions; INR15 billion funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Over the last 2 years, we have deployed approximately INR19 billion towards growth capex and acquisitions. Despite the significant investment phase, net debt has reduced from INR25 billion as of March '24 to approximately INR19 billion as of March '26.

items.statement: Domestic MDF demand expected to grow at early double-digit to mid-teens pace in FY27
items.quote: Domestic demand, MDF demand is expected to continue at a healthy pace of early double digit to mid-teens.

items.quote: The high-value MDF product mix for the year being 43% in volume terms and 55% in value terms.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 MDF domestic volume growth 29.5% YoY, full year 16.9%; total MDF volume growth 27.8% YoY in Q4, 12.9% for full year
items.quote: we achieved MDF domestic volumes growth of 29.5% year-on-year in quarter 4, while the full year growth was 16.9%.

items.statement: New competitor MDF capacity ~400,000 cbm expected in H2 FY27 (Madhya Pradesh and AP); calibrated ramp-up
items.quote: I think the total size that we are looking at is 400,000 for the full year. Obviously, this does not come up at one go, it will be a calibrated and, approach in terms of, volume ramp-up etc.

items.statement: EPCG benefit INR25 crore in FY26 (vs INR35 crore in FY25); remaining ~INR26 crore linked to export volumes, may spill to FY28 if exports don't resume
items.quote: overall INR25 odd crore have been accounted for as EPCG in the year against 35 which were accounted one shot in quarter four last year.

items.statement: Mature units EBITDA margin ~29.5% for FY26; new units eroded INR 128 crore EBITDA.

items.statement: Mahadevapura hospital revenue INR 17 crore/month in Q4; expected to reach INR 25-30 crore over next 12 months.
items.quote: We are doing an average of INR 17 crores a month based on Q4 numbers. And we have very clear visibility of how it will go to INR 25-30 crores over the next 12 months.

items.quote: We expect it to probably settle down at 320 to 340 days going forward.

items.statement: Order inflows in FY26 were INR1,121 crores, up 216% year-on-year.
items.quote: During FY26, the company recorded order inflows of approximately INR1,121 crores, increase of 216% year-on-year, reflecting healthy demand across multiple defence and aerospace programs.

items.statement: Export order book as on date ~INR53 crores; exports remain strategic pillar.
items.quote: The export order book as on date stands at approximately INR53 crores, and exports remain an important strategic pillar of our long-term growth road map.

items.statement: Transport adjusted EBITDA can reach 10-11% from 6.3%.
items.quote: The adjusted EBITDA, which is today at 6.3%, has a potential to go all the way up to at least 10%.

items.statement: Steady-state ROIC for transport business can exceed 25%.
items.quote: The steady state ROICs, currently we are at 16%, but in a steady state, this number for our transport business can certainly go to 25% plus.

items.statement: Fuel price increases passed through via diesel-linked contracts; no broad price hike planned.
items.quote: There will be some impact, as pump prices have obviously gone up right now by about 3 rupees. Those will get passed on to all of our customers. But there's no broad pricing increase that we have planned at the moment.

items.statement: Market structure more settled; expects gradual shift from 1P to 3P logistics.
items.quote: I think the markets are in a better place. It's more settled. What you're seeing is more stable, long-term competitive dynamics as opposed to short-term price gouging

items.statement: Labor shortages and rising wages will drive need for automation.
items.quote: the labor situation in India continues to tighten. And our anticipation is that this will tighten further in the future.

items.statement: Free cash flow positive one year ahead of plan, despite integration costs.
items.quote: We have 89 crores of free cash flow this year and we're really happy about this. A couple of things, this is one year ahead of plan.

items.statement: Net working capital days reduced to 11, sustainable.
items.quote: I think 11 days is sustainable. I mean, it would be very difficult to crunch it precisely for one quarter, right? So, we are confident that it's quite sustainable.

items.statement: SCS pipeline is margin accretive; every project must meet hurdle rate.
items.quote: The answer is yes. There is an internal hurdle rate that every SCS project needs to pass. We do not pick up projects which do not meet that hurdle rate.

items.statement: Delhivery Direct on-demand intracity service to exceed 200 crore external GMV run rate.
items.quote: I think this gets us to north of about a 200-crore run rate in terms of on-demand intracity logistics.

items.statement: Management confident of sustaining 25%+ top-line growth for FY27 and multiyear basis, driven by aligned capacity, qualifications, and customer schedules.
items.quote: We are confident in sustaining strong business momentum and in delivering on our previously communicated top line growth of approximately 25% plus for the current year.

items.statement: CEO indicates 25%+ guidance is conservative; expects to revise upward once new facilities reach full stabilization.
items.quote: My take is I would only give a growth number, what we are saying is conservative, you're right. And this statement is going to change maybe just because in the coming quarter also, we see that the 70%, 80% is what we see the stabilization part done.

items.statement: Order book stands at ~INR6,500 crores net of FY26 deliveries, providing 11-12x revenue visibility; split ~$400M Energy, $200M+ Aerospace & Defence, $100M+ Oil & Gas.
items.quote: Our order book is at approximately INR6,500 crores with INR600 crores delivered in FY '26 and still remains at that level, which is about 11x, 12x our FY '26 revenue.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin ~37.4% consolidated; management maintains 33-35%+ band, expects further upside from operating leverage and continuous improvement.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin are around 37.4% (consolidated), reflecting strong execution discipline, supply chain efficiencies and margin benefit driven by backward integration, which reduced our outsourcing cost.

items.statement: CEO reiterates 33-35%+ EBITDA margin band with upside potential from operating leverage as new plants ramp.
items.quote: We always say 33% to 35% plus, and that plus can be anything. So keep expecting some kind of -- definitely a growth is always because we just don't make -- we just don't produce.

items.statement: Target diversification: Energy 55-60% in 4-5 years, balance from Aerospace & Defence and Oil & Gas.
items.quote: So going forward -- so let's say, we want to look at Azad 5 years from today, you will see that Azad is a fairly diversified business where Energy will be contributing anywhere between 55% to 60% and the balance will be contributed by our other verticals.

items.statement: Strong demand backdrop across aerospace, defense, energy, oil & gas; supplier base capable of meeting technical thresholds remains small.
items.quote: Global OEMs across aerospace, defense, energy and oil and gas are scaling their platforms and the supplier base capable of meeting the technical threshold we operate at remains small.

items.statement: MHI awarded 8-year single-source contract for hot-section nozzle vane segments; strongest endorsement of technical capabilities.
items.quote: Azad has been awarded a prestigious contract by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Japan as a single-source supplier partner. And we have signed an 8-year long contract and purchase agreement for the supply of highly engineered hot section Nozzle Vanes segments for the combustion of a gas turbine engine.

items.statement: ATGG engine program advanced from years to weeks; first qualification batch delivery imminent for national defense program.
items.quote: So Amit, I would just give you an idea, it was years, years got to months, now it has come to weeks. So we are not far away.

items.statement: Pratt & Whitney, Rolls-Royce, Safran airfoil qualifications progressing; first qualification batch for Rolls-Royce expected H2 FY27, revenue from Q4 FY27/early FY28.
items.quote: The first one was Rolls-Royce. So we have -- in H2, we are expecting to supply the first qualification batch. And once that is approved, and I think from -- we can see some momentum coming from Q4 FY '27 or early of FY '28.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia Baker Hughes JV opportunity remains but timelines shifted; current priority is ramping existing 4 new plants.
items.quote: No. So that is still on. From an opportunity perspective, I think we are still going ahead with that. But yes, the time lines have been shifted. We are still in discussions with our customer on how do we best take this forward given the current situation and priorities.

items.statement: Expects 15% overall revenue growth in FY27.
items.quote: We expect a 15% increase in the overall revenue for FY27, FY28. For '26, '27.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to improve by about 100 bps to around 20.2%.
items.quote: So the impact of Jamshedpur shall be nullified, and we expect the EBITDA to move by around 100 basis points.

items.statement: Expects ARPOB to grow around 8% via tariff increase and specialty optimization.
items.quote: We expect the ARPOB to grow by around 8% through a mix of tariff increase as well as specialty optimization.

items.statement: Jamshedpur capex about INR70 lakhs per bed, similar to Raipur.
items.quote: The capex per bed for the Jamshedpur hospital would be around INR70 lakhs per bed. That is very similar to the capex we've incurred in Raipur as well.

items.statement: Raipur to break even monthly by Q3 FY27; full year slight loss, next year positive.
items.quote: We are hopeful that by quarter 3 of this financial year, we should be breaking even on a monthly basis at an operational level.

items.statement: Raipur expected to reach 30% occupancy by end of FY27.
items.quote: We expect to close this year at around 30% occupancy.

items.statement: Jamshedpur 150-bed hospital expected to be commissioned by Q4 FY27.
items.quote: So this year, we are targeting to add around 150 beds through our Jamshedpur hospital, which is expected to be commissioned by quarter 4 of FY27.

items.statement: Salt Lake occupancy expected to reach 70-73% in FY27.
items.quote: We expect the occupancy to move towards the 70% to 73% mark for this FY.

items.statement: Dumdum occupancy expected to reach 72% in FY27.
items.quote: We expect the occupancy level at Dumdum also to move towards the 72% mark in this FY.

items.statement: Howrah occupancy expected to close FY27 in late 50s, moving to 60% by Q1 next year.
items.quote: We expect the occupancy to move towards the 60% by Q1 of next year. So, this year, we expect to close around the late 50s.

items.statement: Agartala occupancy expected to reach 58% in FY27.
items.quote: Agartala should be moving towards the 58% mark.

items.statement: Raipur insurance empanelment delays expected to complete next quarter, aiding ramp-up.
items.quote: We expect the empanelment’s to be complete in the next quarter, post which we will see a significant improvement in the numbers as well.

items.statement: Committed to gross margin guidance of 12-13%, EBITDA 7-7.5%, PAT 4%.
items.quote: the company remains committed to the gross margin guidance of around 12 to 13% with the EBITDA of 7 to 7.5% and a PAT of 4%

items.statement: Plans 5 COCO and 20 franchise stores in FY27, mostly outside Maharashtra.
items.quote: we plan to open 5 COCO and 20 franchise for this year.

items.statement: A&P spend to be 1.5% or lower, including festival schemes.
items.quote: Guiding on the on the A&P spend, both ATL and BTL, 1.5 is what we would stick to or in fact we would try to go a little lower

items.statement: Import duty hike passed on to consumers, no margin impact; may reduce bars/coins demand.
items.quote: As far as import duty is concerned, it's directly passed on to the consumer. So, it will not have an impact on the margins

items.statement: Expects gold bars and coins share to stabilize at ~25% in FY27, down from 40% in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: I think this year it should again stabilize back to the 25% or even lower levels

items.statement: Expects bars and coins sales to decline drastically due to duty hike and old gold exchange push.
items.quote: I'm expecting that the sale of coins and bars will go down drastically.

items.statement: Old gold exchange currently 40% of business, expected to rise to 50%+.
items.quote: old gold today is around 40% of our entire business, and we expecting that this the old gold trend picks up, we should be at around 50% plus

items.statement: Hedging to increase to 75-80% in FY27 to reduce margin volatility.
items.quote: next year we should be at 75% to 80%.

items.statement: Franchise gross margins are 2.5-3%, impacting overall margins as franchise share grows.
items.quote: the franchise gross margins are in the range of 2.5 to 3%.

items.statement: Gold bar and coin margins are 0.5-1%, while gold jewellery margins are 12.5-13%.
items.quote: on the gold bar and coins we operate on a very thin margins in the range of half a percent to 1%. And on the normal jewellery on the gold jewellery which is not studded, which is not non-studded jewellery is in the range of 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Retail revenue target for FY27 is INR9,800 crores, 23% increase.
items.quote: the next year targets and the guidance for the retail, which we have taken under in our AOP, is around INR9,800 crores, which is a 23% increase.

items.statement: Plans to introduce lightweight and lower-caratage jewellery (18K, 14K) in FY27.
items.quote: We are also toying with lightweight jewellery and lighter-caratage jewellery. That's something which is on the cards for this year. So, we're looking at 18-carat jewellery, also 14-carat jewellery.

items.statement: QIP not an impediment; enabling board resolution till August, no immediate plans.
items.quote: there is an enabling board resolution which is till end of August. So that is where we are. We haven't really thought on, you know, going ahead on that front at this point of time.

items.statement: Plans further capex of INR100 crores in FY27, calibrated to market conditions and EXIM normalization.
items.quote: Seeing better opportunities, our intention is a further capex of INR100 crores in this FY27, which remains linked to strong customer demand and will be calibrated to market conditions as year goes on, including the pace of EXIM normalization.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to sequentially improve and return to around 7% seen at start of FY25.
items.quote: The EBITDA margins which are 4.6%, 4.7%, we hope to bring it back to where we were starting FY25 which is around almost 7% and even higher the year earlier.

items.statement: Targets debtor days below 120 in the current financial year.
items.quote: We are targeting to bring our debtor days to below 120 in this current financial year.

items.statement: Expects EXIM situation to improve or rationalize within this quarter, with green shoots from this month.
items.quote: My gut feel is that the situation especially in the EXIM side should start improving or rationalizing itself within this quarter.

items.statement: Sees top and bottom line sequentially improving from this quarter, with bottom line recuperating.
items.quote: I feel fairly confident that from here both the top and the bottom line should start showing a sequential improvement.

items.statement: Pivoted EXIM business toward East Coast exports to buffer West Coast disruptions.
items.quote: We've pivoted on our EXIM side more to our East Coast exports to sort of buffer the hits that are happening on the West, that's something we cannot control, but obviously a highly profitable business that we can't do.

items.statement: Domestic volumes expected to rise from this month, driven by Morbi multimodal park and Western seacoast clients.
items.quote: The volumes have been subdued, but we expect it to start rising from this month onwards.

items.statement: Order book remains strong with pedigreed customers; domestic and East Coast EXIM pipelines robust.
items.quote: The order books remain very strong, the domestic pipelines are good and the Exim pipeline especially on the East Coast are very robust.

items.statement: FY26 capex deployed over INR70 crores on specialized containers, handling equipment, and vehicles.
items.quote: Total capex deployed in FY26 was over INR70 crores, including in specialized TEUs, handling equipment such as reach stackers, commercial vehicles, all completely aligned to our customers' requirements and operating needs.

items.statement: Procured 161 specialized containers in FY26; similar orders in pipeline for FY27.
items.quote: Your company procured 161 specialized containers during FY26 and we have similar orders in pipelines for FY27 as well.

items.statement: EXIM volumes fell 11% in Q4 versus 40% industry decline due to Middle East crisis.
items.quote: Luckily for our company, we have been very resilient in this regard, with our EXIM container movement dropping less than 11% compared to the 40% overall.

items.statement: Insurance premiums rose by USD1,200 for 20ft and USD2,400 for 40ft containers; war risk surcharges nearly doubling ocean freight.
items.value: USD1,200 for 20 feet and 2400 USD for 40 feet
items.quote: The war has resulted in insurance premium going up by USD1,200 for 20 feet and 2400 USD for 40 feet in some cases.

items.statement: IPO funds: under INR100 crores still to be deployed; INR92 crores of IPO funds remain for FY27 capex.
items.quote: We used the capex mostly for domestic and this year also the Exim that we've planned is a INR100 crores of which we have INR92 from our IPO funds still to be deployed.

items.statement: Expects FY27 revenue growth >20% on capacity additions and order inflows.
items.quote: We expect revenue to grow by more than 20%, supported by capacity additions and strong order inflows, and increased contribution from high-margin engineered products.

items.statement: Long-term target of INR650+ crore revenue with 15-16% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Our long-term inspiration remains to build a INR650 crores plus revenue platform with sustainable EBITDA margins in the range of 15% to 16%.

items.statement: No additional capex needed up to INR800-900 crore revenue.
items.quote: I think that the capex that we are doing, the INR100 crores capex that we have indicated should be enough to propel us to INR800 crores to INR900 crores in the coming years.

items.statement: Order book ~INR200 crore as of 30 Apr 2026; 80-90% executable in FY27.
items.quote: Our order book remains healthy at approximately INR200 crores as of 30th April 2026, providing strong visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Passes on raw material price hikes to customers with a lag; fixed-price contracts cause margin fluctuation.
items.quote: Also, the volatility in the raw material prices, we are able to pass it on to the customers for all the subsequent contracts that we are executing for them.

items.statement: No demand slowdown from West Asia crisis; projects not on hold.
items.quote: We don't see any slowdown happening as of now. So, none of the projects have gone under hold.

items.statement: Raw material volatility (tungsten, nickel, cobalt) impacts margins; fixed-price contracts bear brunt.
items.quote: Of course, if the prices go up, we take a margin hit in these contracts. But subsequently, whatever we are quoting for new contracts, the prices go up.

items.statement: Railway developmental orders execution 6-9 months; substantial revenue from next year.
items.quote: So, we expect the execution to take anywhere between, since they are developmental orders, we expect the execution to take anywhere between six to nine months.

items.statement: No revenue from Tejorup (defense) this year or next; prototype development ongoing.
items.quote: I don't think and I don't foresee any revenue coming in from Tejorup in this financial year. And also, I think, nothing significant coming in the next financial year.

items.statement: International sales to grow >20% YoY, targeting 15% of revenue.
items.quote: We expect the international revenue to go up to 15% in the next, in this year and the next year.

items.statement: Debtor days target 80-90 days, inventory days 60-65 days.
items.quote: No, our target would be anywhere between 80 to 90. We are targeting 80 to 85, actually, and inventory days of 60 to 65.

items.statement: FY26 new orders secured worth INR 4,125 crores plus INR 3,800 crores variation/change orders; order intake below expectations due to deferment of large awards and L1 conversion delays
items.quote: Coming to order inflows during the financial year, we secured new orders worth INR 4,125 crores, excluding approximately INR 3,800 crores of variation and change orders received on existing projects.

items.statement: INR 15,000 crores of orders booked or declared L1 in current FY so far; expect L1 orders to convert in Q1 FY27
items.quote: You would have noticed that we have booked around INR 8,000 crores of orders and declared L1 in another around INR 7,000 crores of new orders so far in this financial year. We expect these L1 orders to get converted in this quarter.

items.statement: Order booking guidance of INR 30,000 crores for FY27 (INR 15,000 crores certain including L1 + INR 15,000 crores more expected)
items.quote: Having a certainty of about INR 15,000 crores order including L1 in the current financial year, we expect to book another INR 15,000 crores of more orders, making a total order booking guidance of INR 30,000 crores for the current financial year.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance of INR 725 crores
items.quote: So, FY27, we are looking at a CAPEX of around INR 725 crores.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 11.7% vs 12.8% in FY25; Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 6.1% vs higher previous year
items.quote: For the overall year, the absolute number of EBITDA was INR 1439 crore which is 11.7% as compared to last year's INR 1662 crore which is 12.8%.

items.statement: Overseas projects (30% of turnover) severely impacted by POL/gas supply chain disruptions and logistics challenges due to geopolitical developments in Q4
items.quote: In Q4, after the war, there were Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants (POL) and gas-related issues in projects consumables and logistic-related challenges. Especially, this was in the overseas market which kind of marred the planned progress.

items.statement: Payment delays from clients (both government and private) constrained working capital, limited project funding, and reduced Q4 turnover
items.quote: Specifically in Q4, we have seen that the payments were not coming from the customers. Payments were not very smooth from majority of the customers. Working capital, funding to the projects continued in Q4 as well and under the circumstances, we decided to balance between funding projects and maintaining liquidity.

items.statement: Q4 provisions of INR 160 crores; FY26 total provisions INR 325 crores including shift to ECL matrix, arbitration award provision, and marine cost overruns
items.quote: FY26, the number is close to INR 325 crores. See, Parvez, I will just explain you. What we have done is, this year we have, in Q4, what we have done is we have made a ECL provisioning matrix.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of INR 4 lakh crores for next two years (70% domestic, 30% overseas); Middle East opportunity emerging post-war
items.quote: Our bid pipeline remains healthy for the next two years, which we track. It's close to INR 4 lakh crores, which we are tracking across segments, and out of that, 70% is domestic and 30% is from the overseas market.

items.statement: Overseas order book 13% but contributes ~30% of turnover; domestic projects have cost pass-through, overseas mostly fixed-price
items.quote: In terms of our existing order book, nearly about 10% to 11% only is currently in the overseas segment. 13% is the overseas segment. All others are domestic segment. As you know, domestic segment, we have a pass-through mechanism and international segments, we do not have a pass-through segment.

items.statement: Croatia road tenders where Afcons was L1 cancelled by client due to budgetary constraints; railway project L1 formalities expected to conclude shortly
items.quote: As disclosed recently to the stock exchanges, the two Croatia Road tenders, where we were declared L1, have been cancelled by the client due to budgetary constraints. While this is disappointing, we continue to remain positive on the long-term opportunity in the region.

items.statement: Mumbai-Ahmedabad HSR C2 project: second TBM consignment received, assembly progressing, tunneling expected to commence before end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: On the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail C2 project, the second consignment of the tunnel boring machine, which had remained held up for several months, has now been received at site. Assembly activities are progressing well and the main drivers has already been lowered into the shaft. We expect tunneling operations to

items.statement: FY26 capex incurred INR 1,069 crores (Q4 alone ~INR 700 crores)
items.quote: So, in FY26, we have incurred a CAPEX of INR 1069. And this number was in December, this number was around INR 370 odd crores. So, in Q4, we have done close to INR 700 crores.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 32,500 crores with INR 15,000 crores assured inflows and INR 15,000 crores more expected, targeting INR 60,000 crores.
items.quote: We are saying we have INR 32,500 crores of order book. We are saying we have INR 15,000 crores of assured inflows and INR 15,000 crores of inflows are going to bag more. That will take me to around INR 60,000 crores of order book.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance for FY27 is INR 30,000 crores; INR 8,000 crores already confirmed (including Croatia), INR 7,000 crores at L1 stage.
items.quote: New order inflow, we have indicated INR 30,000 crores, out of which we have already received INR 8,000 crores and another about INR 7,000 crores were L1 and further INR 15,000 crores.

items.statement: FY27 depreciation expected similar to FY26 with marginal increase due to TBM additions of ~INR 1,000 crores.
items.quote: FY27, it will be the similar number, maybe marginally it will be up from because you yourself have said that these CAPEX, whatever TBM, we have added INR 1000 odd crore.

items.statement: Interest-bearing advances increasing but management expects margin improvement once revenue scales; ROE impacted but ROCE not affected.
items.quote: Once the top line kind of elevates, we will not have this kind of a situation.

items.statement: Domestic projects have escalation formulas covering 90-100%+ of cost increases; Croatia contract has pass-through beyond 10% cost absorption.
items.quote: In Croatia, which is our biggest contract to date, is something where up to 10% of cost increase, we need to absorb. Beyond that, it has a pass-through.

items.statement: Order pipeline visibility across marine, urban infrastructure, hydro, and surface transport; 60% domestic, 40% international split expected.
items.quote: We have good visibility in marine, in urban infrastructure, in hydro and certain projects in surface transport as well. So, visibility is also across the various segments we operate in.

items.statement: Widespread payment delays from government customers (central and state) increasing receivable days to 143; targeting reduction to 120 days by June.
items.quote: At the moment, this networking capital number of around 143 days and in last call, we had talked about that we are looking at somewhere around, say, 120 odd days.

items.statement: UP Jal Jeevan Mission and Gabon projects facing collection issues; management slowing execution to match cash inflows.
items.quote: Other than UP Jal-Jevan Mission Project and maybe project in Gabon, we do not have any specific names to be given.

items.statement: Contract assets liquidation of ~INR 1,000 crores expected by June 2026 to reduce working capital days.
items.quote: We are looking at those liquidation, maybe say by June, we should see a sizable liquidation in the range of say INR 1000 odd crores.

items.statement: Croatia railway project funding secured via ECB approval; road projects cancelled due to budget overruns but not affecting railway contract.
items.quote: ECB has already approved the entire amount, and funds are already there with them. Therefore, we don't find any issues.

items.statement: Expects to end FY27 with over 1 million sq ft operational area.
items.value: more than a million operational area
items.quote: So all these center, all these signed off centres and the additional centres that we are signing off will be developed and we will be ending the year with more than a million operational area.

items.statement: Managed office share to rise to 70% of portfolio, co-working 30%.
items.quote: I think will be 70% managed office and 30% of the co-working, which over a period of next three to four years will come down to 90% of managed office and 10% of co-working.

items.statement: Managed office growing at 30-40% annually vs co-working at 10%.
items.quote: So probably in co-working, we are growing at the rate of 10% every year, but in managed office, we are growing at the rate of 30, 40% per year.

items.statement: FY27 will see significant growth; full benefit of 10 lakh sq ft in FY28.
items.quote: So all this leads to not all 10 lakh contributing to the revenue in financial year 27, but you will get the benefit of these 10 lakh square feet in the financial year, 27, 28 entirely.

items.statement: Plans to sustain current growth momentum for at least five years.
items.quote: We have an internal plan which we intend to implement and this kind of growth momentum. we want to sustain for at least this five-year period that you have mentioned.

items.statement: Will convert accounts to Ind AS in FY27.
items.quote: We are going to soon getting our accounts converted to index in this financial year itself.

items.statement: Expects to enroll first GCC client very soon; participating in RFPs.
items.quote: We have been getting a lot of requirements and recently we have started participating in the RFPs as well. And if everything goes the way it is going, we will be enrolling the first GCC client with us very, very soon.

items.statement: Co-working ~30% margin, managed ~25%, back-to-back ~20%.
items.quote: Even if that matters, that maybe the coworking has a profit percentage of near about 30%. I'm just quotin g an example, not in real terms. Managed office will have a profit percentage of maybe 25%. And when we'll talk about back -to-back, that will have a profit percentage of maybe 20%.

items.statement: No dynamic pricing; manual pricing to achieve 85-95% occupancy.
items.quote: We cannot do automation in terms of pricing and dynamic pricing. But yes, from the launch of the centre to getting a certain percentage of occupancy, we have a little bit of variation and probably, you know, those lucrative pricing.

items.statement: Industry is commodity-like; scale needed to survive consolidation.
items.quote: But this is a commodity business. And if you don't become very big, very fast in a commodity business, it is very, very less probable to sustain and survive in the market.

items.statement: Aims to be one of the biggest in next three years.
items.quote: We will be one of the biggest in next three years. That is what I can assure you today.

items.statement: Plans to expand into Bangalore, Pune, and Hyderabad.
items.quote: similar kind of strategy we are going to replicate in cities like Bangalore, Pune and Hyderabad to have the similar kind of impact that we have in NCR market now.

items.statement: New centers take 3 months to set up, 6 months to stabilize.
items.quote: It's a 3 months investment cycle for establishing the center . Prior to that, we do the design and the development of the concept. And once the centre is ready, let's say after the end of second month, We start marketing the center

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected early to mid-teens, double-digit.
items.quote: Yes, early to mid-teens. Now coming to the FY31, look, our FY31 goal was INR 8400 crores, of which we had highlighted that about 1700 crores will come from inorganic route.

items.statement: 100 bps EBITDA margin expansion by exit FY27.
items.quote: We are looking at a strong 100-basis point expansion by the time we exit FY27.

items.statement: FY31 revenue target INR 8,400 crores (~USD 1 billion), 14-15% organic CAGR.
items.quote: We have built a resilient foundation aligned tightly with our “3x3 Strategy” to scale to USD 1 billion, or approximately INR 8,400 crores, by FY31 and we are exiting the year with powerful momentum.

items.statement: FY27 cash deployment ~INR 100 crores, INR 70-80 crores maintenance capex, INR 15-20 crores leasehold.
items.quote: So, we have typically around INR 100 crores of cash deployment, typically around INR 70-80 crores into my maintenance CAPEX. And typically, this year, like this year, and FY26-27, we have two large leasehold premises, which we are also moving into. So, around 15-20 crores into that.

items.statement: Q4 TCV bookings INR 620 crores, second consecutive 600+ quarter.
items.quote: Our commercial engine is firing on all cylinders. Sales momentum remained exceptionally healthy in Q4, with TCV bookings of INR 620 crores. This marks our second consecutive quarter of 600-plus TCV, providing us with high revenue visibility heading into the new fiscal year.

items.statement: FY26 TCV bookings INR 2,355 crores, 114 new logos added.
items.quote: For the full year, TCV bookings stood at INR 2,355 crores, with 114 new logos added during FY26.

items.statement: Tech and Digital revenue grew 27.2% YoY to INR 249 crores, 31% of total.
items.quote: Our Tech and Digital revenues climbed 5.8% quarter-on-quarter and 27.2% year- on- year to INR 249 crores. This segment now accounts for 31% of our total revenue mix up from previous quarters, proving our rapid transition to higher-value technology-led services.

items.statement: International revenue grew 16.4% YoY to INR 304 crores, 38.1% of total.
items.quote: Our international footprint expanded 4.3% sequentially and 16. 4% year -on-year to INR 304 crores, lifting our international mix to 38.1% of revenue.

items.statement: Healthcare vertical targeted to be 12-15% of revenue by FY31, $120-150 million.
items.quote: By 2031, we believe that healthcare will be 12 to 15 % of our revenue mix. So, that means we are looking at about $120 to $150 million.

items.statement: Wage code compliance absorbed INR 4 crores one-time impact in Q4, no margin compression.
items.quote: Importantly, this is after absorbing approximately INR 4 crores of one-time impact from the implementation of the new wage code.

items.statement: Evaluating six acquisition targets, two advanced, hopeful of at least one acquisition this year.

But given that we are a value investor, whatever acquisition that we make will have to pass through the lens of our value thesis. We are hopeful that this year we will be able to make at least one acquisition.

items.statement: Steady-state depreciation guided at ~INR 60 crores quarterly.
items.quote: Overall depreciation, if that was the question, they take around INR 60 odd crores.

items.statement: Normalized OCF conversion target ~70% of EBITDA.
items.quote: But on an overall basis, you should assume around 70% of cash conversion from the EBITDA.

items.statement: FY26 adjusted PAT margin 2.3%, baseline for future improvement.
items.quote: After adjusting for exceptional items of 65 crores relating to demerger-related costs, the new Labor Code for the past service cost and the wage restructuring impact, the FY26 adjusted PAT margins to 2.3%.

items.statement: Organic revenue growth guidance for FY27 is 15-16%.
items.quote: So organic growth in terms of revenue our guidance is 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Organic EBITDA margin expected around 4% in FY27.
items.quote: Organically, we've touched 4% EBITDA. So that's the range of EBITDA that we want to be from an organic businesses.

items.statement: With acquisitions, EBITDA margin to jump to 5%.
items.quote: With these two acquisitions, the EBITDA margins jump from 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Inorganic revenue addition of INR 800 crores annualized from acquisitions.
items.quote: And to top it up, another INR 800 crores comes from the inorganic route.

items.statement: Expect to cross INR 100 crores PAT with acquisitions integrated.
items.quote: we should cross on an annualized basis a INR 100 crores PAT company with both these acquisitions integrated well.

items.statement: foundit to achieve EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27.
items.quote: we are on that trajectory of an internally aligned of taking the company to a EBITDA break-even company by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: STEAG acquisition enterprise value INR 180 crores, with INR 140 crores cash.
items.quote: STEAG acquisition, we're going to pay enterprise value of INR 180 crores. We got almost INR 140 crores of cash in the business.

items.statement: FY26 secured 164 new contracts with ACV INR 459 crores.
items.quote: In FY26, we have secured new 164 contracts with a total annual contract value of INR 459 crores.

items.statement: STEAG to add 90-100 bps to pro forma EBITDA margins.
items.quote: the acquisitions of STEAG India is expected to add nearly 20% to our top line and improve our pro forma EBITDA margins for the year by approximately 90 basis to 100 basis points.

items.statement: LSG Sky Chefs has mid-to-high teens EBITDA margins.
items.quote: EBITDA margins of this business are in mid -to-high-teens, which would augment our margins further.

items.statement: Telecom segment growth muted due to delayed capex by operators.
items.quote: the overall segment growth was muted due to delay in planned capital expenditure from leading telecom operators

items.statement: Post-acquisition, high-margin telecom and industrial share to rise from 19% to 33%.
items.quote: Post-acquisition, the share of our high margin telecom and industrial verticals would grow from 19% to 33% of revenues.

items.statement: Q1 seasonally soft for food and telecom due to summer holidays.
items.quote: Quarter ones would be an exception, because two of our high-margin businesses, which is food and telecom, have a seasonality effect in quarter ones.

items.statement: STEAG acquisition funded primarily through debt and internal accruals.
items.quote: We plan to fund this acquisition primarily through debt and internal accruals.

items.statement: Unit 4 Phase 1 capex of Rs. 1,200 crores over FY27 and FY28, completion by March 2028.
items.quote: In Phase 1 of that expansion, and we are looking at investing almost about Rs. 1,200 odd crores across two years, this year FY27 and in FY28.

items.statement: FY27 capex approximately Rs. 700 crores, followed by Rs. 500 crores.
items.quote: Roughly about Rs. 700 crores and then post that will be about Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: Aspire to maintain historical 20%+ growth, but refrain from giving FY27 guidance.
items.quote: We want to refrain from giving any guidance for FY27 or FY28, but long-term, have we put in the ingredients from a growth point of view? I'd say that the answer is yes.

items.statement: Aspire to keep EBITDA margins constant at 38-40% going forward.
items.quote: We've delivered so far, and we’ll continue to deliver those numbers going forward as well.

items.statement: Destocking is behind; restocking expected to positively impact top and bottom line.
items.quote: I think mostly it's behind us, and we expect that this will have a very positive impact on Anthem's top line and bottom line.

items.statement: Commercial molecules 60% of revenue, specialty ingredients 17%, R&D 8-9%, development/manufacturing 15%.
items.quote: Commercial is about 60% and 14%. R&D is about 8% to 9% of our business, and the balance is specialty ingredients. Specialty ingredients is about 17% of our business.

items.statement: Late-stage pipeline at 10 Phase 3 molecules, all from emerging biotech, non-lateral.
items.quote: In terms of the additions, which have happened in Phase 3, all of them are non-lateral. These are molecules where we were working with them on early Phase 2, and they have moved to Phase 3.

items.statement: Four new commercial molecules contributed 8-9% of revenues; ramp-up expected over 2-3 years.
items.quote: Ballpark, the current contribution from these four molecules will be in the range of closer to about 8% to 9% of our revenues.

items.statement: No tariff impact due to separate deals with US administration; biotech funding recovering.
items.quote: No tariffs is not a problem, because most of the big pharma that we work with already have separate deals with the administration in the US.

items.quote: Biotech funding has been recovering, and I think till about April, the four months, it's gone up by about 50-odd percent YoY.

items.statement: Specialty ingredients aspire to 20% growth; dedicated Unit 4 facility to reduce cannibalization.
items.quote: We delivered about 8% growth in the fourth quarter and we would aspire to grow that business also in a similar growth trajectory as what we are looking at growing for our CDMO business. Overall, a 20% growth for specialty ingredients as well.

items.statement: Biosimilar asset to hit P&L next year, classified under CRDMO.
items.quote: I think, which will hit our P&L next year. Where will we classify it? I think it will go in CRDMO.

items.statement: GLP-1 commercialization expected in 6-8 months, potential big contributor.
items.quote: That could happen in six months, it could happen in eight months, but I think we're there.

items.statement: Unit 3 turning positive this year; Unit 4 ready next financial year.
items.quote: Unit 3 is already turning around and it's going to be in the positive territory this year. Unit 4 will be ready by the next financial year.

items.statement: Targets INR1,000 crores revenue by FY28; FY27 will be a significant step.
items.quote: Our target of INR1,000 crores revenue by financial year '28 is firmly on track. Financial year '27 will be a significant and visible step towards that milestone.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR600 crores is achievable.
items.quote: Yes, it is very much achievable. We are on line.

items.statement: Current unexecuted order book stands at INR825 crores.
items.quote: Our order book as of now stands around INR825 crores and we have already participated on the various other tenders whereby we expect some reasonable and sizeable orders to come in during the course of this year.

items.statement: Tenders under evaluation worth INR1,225 crores; expected order inflow INR200-300 crores.
items.quote: The total tenders which are at various stages of evaluation is around INR1,225 crores. Over and above and our strike rate somewhere goes around 20% to it stays between 20% to 30%. So we can say around 200 to 300 out of these we are going to book.

items.statement: INR3,000 crores of tenders identified for bidding in next two months.
items.quote: And around INR3,000 odd tenders we have already identified for which bidding, bid preparation is undergoing and we will be bidding in a month or in next two months.

items.statement: Confident of maintaining FY26 margins in FY27.
items.quote: We are very much confident of maintaining the same.

items.quote: Yes, you are very right. FPI, the more is the contribution from FPI, the better will be the margins.

items.quote: Yes, we are very much hopeful that the contribution in FY '28 may be even better than 10%.

items.quote: We are for INR1,000 crores, we are making arrangements for a credit limit of around INR300 crores, INR300 crores to INR350 crores, mix of both fund-based and non-fund-based.

items.statement: No immediate fund-raising plans; may explore if valuations are good.
items.quote: As on date, we do not envisage any need of raising any funds from the market. But again, now if there is some very good decent valuation and if it is in the interest of stakeholders, definitely we can explore.

items.statement: Majority of orders have price variation clause, protecting against commodity price fluctuations.
items.quote: Yes, Deepak, majority of our orders are with price variation clause. Like if there is any change in the commodity prices, the same gets, you know, passed on to the customer.

items.statement: Expects at least one large SCADA-type project order in FY27.
items.quote: But yes, in this financial year, we expect similar such project, at least one similar such project in this financial year.

items.statement: Receivables concentration in Q4; working to improve collection and avoid last-month revenue concentration.
items.quote: Now we are working on, you know, making some arrangements and doing some things so that we can avoid this concentration of revenues in the last month of the year.

items.statement: Compact FPI to be launched by Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Latest by Q2, we will be able to, you know, launch this FPI into the market.

items.statement: Targets 60-70% CAGR revenue growth in FY27 and subsequent years
items.quote: In the medium term, we are confident to achieve 60% to 70% CAGR growth in the upcoming financial year, that is FY 2026-27, and relatively the next years as well.

items.quote: So, for the next financial year, FY2026-27, we are trying to continue with the Q4 performance. So, the PAT that we have achieved in the Q4 was between 20% to 23%, I guess, and then EBITDA was approximately 35%. So, we are trying to maintain the same values in the upcoming year.

items.statement: Current active order book stands at Rs 25 crore across structural and architectural segments
items.quote: Today, across our structural and architectural business segments, our current active order book stands at approximately Rs. 25 crores.

items.quote: So, as I mentioned, we are having our current order book of Rs. 25 crores, and there is a pipeline of Rs. 6 crores approximately that is in the bidding stage or we call it as an RFQ stage.

items.statement: Order book builds Rs 4-5 crore monthly; expects continued expansion
items.quote: So usually, our order book keeps building throughout the year. So, it's not like at the start of the year, but every month we have added almost Rs. 4 crores to Rs. 5 crores of order book in the last year.

items.quote: Now what we are targeting is $45 to $60 per hour even. And that's why we are optimistic that going forward our project prices will increase comparatively.

items.quote: Now we have added architectural design as well as interior design, both the services into our existing portfolio.

items.quote: We have taken deviation in the object issue from office buying office premises. So, Rs. 5 crores we have made provision for this kind of acquisitions only.

items.quote: There has been no change into our business so far. There was a critical situation in last few months globally, but that has not impacted in any sense to our business.

items.quote: So, for Edward Farr Architects, in last calendar year, the firm has added Rs. 14 crores of turnover in calendar year 2025, and they are PAT margins of around 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Employee count 200-250; added ~70 in FY26; US headcount ~25; attrition ~10% in India, zero in subsidiaries
items.quote: Right. The total headcount at the moment is between 200 to 250. And compared to the last financial year, we have approximately increased 70 people internally.

items.statement: ISG to be introduced on three popular motorcycle models of three of top four OEMs; two launches in Q1, one in Q4.
items.quote: the SEDEMAC ISG issue is going to get introduced on three popular That is, you know, models that consistently feature in the top 10 sold in India, motorcycle models of three of the top four OEMs.

items.quote: Then the second driver is going to be the e2W MCUs. It got launched in Q3 of FY26 and a partial ramp up had happened. We expect it to ramp up further this financial year.

items.quote: And then the ramp up of ISG ECUs for the export three-wheeler. I briefly mentioned this, that for the India market, the three-wheeler ISG ECUs is now widespread and for export it has started. The SOP has already happened in Q4 and now we're in the ramp up phase.

items.statement: RM cost increase from commodity inflation and semiconductor tightening expected to mildly pressure EBITDA percentage.
items.quote: some RM cost increase is likely and it will, you know, it is expected to put a mild pressure on EBITDA percentage. We don't expect this to be anything dramatic, but some pressure is to be expected.

items.quote: there are reports of a strong El Nino in CY26 being active. So if that happens, then it could potentially have negative impact on Indian monsoon and also on the US hurricane season.

items.quote: Then there is also this MF4, which is a plant that is made for manufacturing of electric machines / electric motors. And we expect the shipments to start from Q3 of this financial year.

items.statement: Acquired land in Shoolagiri for future shipments to customers with plants in southern India.
items.quote: In addition, we have also acquired land in Shoolagiri for future shipments to customers who have plants in the southern India region.

items.statement: For 100 crore additional revenue, need ~20 crore fixed assets and ~12-15 crore working capital.

items.quote: On the commercial vehicle, our after treatment controller is likely to get into production in H2 of FY27. The development is on track. This will of course be the first SOP for us for the CV market.

items.statement: Management believes all ICE two-wheelers will eventually have ISG, though timing uncertain.
items.quote: we think all ICE 2 wheelers will have ISG eventually. So when that eventuality will happen, we don't know.

items.statement: ISG+EFI integrated ECU offers significant cost benefits and will increasingly win on numbers and performance.
items.quote: ISG plus EFI will win on numbers and on performance, it will win.

items.quote: our FY26 revenue was 1,058 crore, the first time that we have crossed 1,000 crore in revenue, highest ever. And it was a 61% up compared to FY25 revenue.

items.quote: So the electric machine will also, to some extent, start getting shipped from our facilities beginning Q3 is our expectation.

items.statement: Most three-wheeler exports will have ISG over FY27.
items.quote: And in exports as well, they've just started going and over FY27, most exports will have it.

items.quote: About 10 million, I don't know what the export number was, maybe something like $10 million in FY26 we exported. All of that is in the genset space.

items.quote: It could have some impact on our EBITDA numbers being a little bit under pressure if our costs go up.

items.quote: And as far as our capacities are concerned, concerned even with the current shipments, what we have seen in Q -4 still we continue to maintain possibility to grow by another 20% because we did all the capacity additions what we have to, in the past.

items.quote: So, this would, we would expect this to continue and as the turnover goes up, definitely to have this.

items.quote: I mean I would probably give you overall number. It's around 20. Around 20% you can take 22% you can take as composite and 78% is metallics.
