items.statement: PPA coverage: 79% FY27, 71% FY28, 66% FY29.
items.quote: For FY27, it is 79%. FY 28 CODs of 8,069 MW we are already covered with 71% PPA. And the year next around 8,400 MW, it is 66%.

items.statement: FY27 8 GW renewable addition: 1.9 GW via JVs; FY28: 624 MW via JVs.
items.quote: in FY27, out of the 8 GW around 1.9 GW would come through JVs, primarily through Ayana and a part of that would come through a JV with IOCL that is INGEL. And in FY 28, out of the 8 GW around 624 MW would come through the JV route.

items.statement: Mahi Banswara nuclear: first concrete Aug 2027, first unit sync Nov 2032.
items.quote: The first pour of concrete is anticipated by August 2027. And first unit synchronization we are planning in November 2032.

items.statement: Pump storage: 3-5 GW expected commercialized by 2032-33.
items.quote: Another 3 GW to 5 GW, you can expect to be commercialized by 2032 to '33.

items.statement: Coal gasification pilot at Talaipalli: 4 lakh tonnes per annum synthetic natural gas.
items.quote: we have taken up a pilot project at one of our mines, Talaipalli. And we are going to EIL, and this has a capacity of 4 lakh tonnes per annum.

items.statement: Aims to maintain CASA ratio at 33% plus and CD ratio at 80%.
items.quote: While focusing on CASA, we have assured that 33% plus, we want to maintain 33%-plus of CASA percentage. And all these ratios, once we do that with the CD ratio of 80%...

items.statement: Holds ROA guidance at 1% plus, expected to trend toward improvement.
items.quote: ROA, I was telling 1% plus. 1% plus may be anything. So 1% plus, I will still hold on to it.

items.statement: Plans to increase provision coverage ratio by about 1% every quarter.
items.quote: We want to increase 1% every quarter. That number still I'm holding on.

items.statement: NIM has bottomed out; will work on sustaining 3% plus NIM going forward.
items.quote: As I was telling in the beginning, if you have seen, I am working on that 3% plus NIM. I will be working on it.

items.statement: ECL guidelines impact estimated at 1-1.5% of net worth, spread over 4-5 years at 25-30 bps annually.
items.quote: I believe the guidelines which has now come, which is available to spread over to the next 5 years and we have studied the impact also maybe around 1% to 1.5% overall will be there. Even that also available for the next 4 years or 5 years, that will be spread over to 25 basis points, 30 basis points.

items.statement: Will consciously reduce bulk advances and grow retail and mid-corporate portfolios.
items.quote: Going forward, consciously, we will reduce the bulk advances and we will grow in retail and mid-corporate.

items.statement: Had INR2,000 crores of sanctioned but undisbursed advances as of March; disbursements started post April.
items.quote: And as of March, we had INR2,000 crores of sanctioned but pending for disbursal. It has not happened for various reasons. It started happening post April.

items.statement: Aims to recover 50% of NPA book and 50% of technically written-off book.
items.quote: What quantum, what number, our aim is always to recover 50% of the book of NPA, 50% of the technical written-off.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict in West Asia and rising input costs could weigh on growth and inflation.
items.quote: However, the war in West Asia, along with the rising input costs driven by higher energy prices and supply chain disruptions, could weigh on the growth.

items.statement: Plans FY27 technology projects: loan origination system revamp, DevSecOps, HRMS and Treasury revamp, BHIM 3.0.
items.quote: A few major solutions that are planned for completion in FY '26-'27 are loan originating system revamp with collateral management, implementation of DevSecOps, HRMS revamp, Treasury revamp and BHIM 3.0.

items.statement: Middle East NRI deposit exposure is not sizable; bank expects limited impact from regional conflict.
items.quote: But with regard to your specific question of the deposits from Middle East, it is not sizable one and we will not be affected much.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% year-over-year.
items.quote: So, from a guidance perspective, I would try to give anywhere between 20% to 25% growth.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin 12.5-13% in short term, 15% long term.
items.quote: So short term, we should be able to do 12.5%, 13% and on the longer term, we should be able to be 15%.

items.statement: Won Mumbai government contract worth Rs 150-200 crore, announcement in 2-3 weeks.
items.quote: It should be to the tune of about anywhere between Rs. 150 crore to Rs. 200 crore.

items.statement: Maharashtra pipeline over Rs 2,000 crore; two large contracts worth Rs 600 crore each upcoming.
items.quote: If I look at Maharashtra as a state, we have close to about Rs. 2,000 crore plus worth of pipeline coming up only in the state of Maharashtra, for which we are very keen on bidding and getting major contracts out of this.

items.statement: Q4 new orders and renewals secured around Rs 166 crore.
items.quote: We secured around Rs. 166 crore in new orders and renewals during this period, reflecting continued demand for our capabilities across digital transformation, infrastructure modernization, managed Services and AI-led Solutions.

items.statement: Government business expected to rebound in FY27 and FY28.
items.quote: At the same time, Government business continues to remain an important and strategic component of our revenue mix, and we anticipate a meaningful rebound in this segment during FY '27, '28.

items.statement: Aim for Services to be 75-80% of revenue for consistency.
items.quote: But if you ask me personally, I would want our Services business to keep on growing and take about 75% to 80% of our top line revenue because that gives a lot of consistency from a growth perspective because most of the Services contracts are signed for 5 years.

items.statement: Western Railway project dropped due to 25-30% equipment cost increase; retender expected mid-July.
items.quote: So that Western Railway project , unfortunately, we had to let it go because by the time the pricing was about to open, the equipment procurement cost went up by 25%, 30%.

items.statement: Audit qualifications to be fully resolved in next 2 quarters after RBI approval.
items.quote: So in next 2 quarters, we should be able to get a clean sheet coming in from everywhere.

items.statement: Long-term aspiration to scale business 10x over next decade, implying 20-25% CAGR.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we aspire to scale the business 10x over the next decade, which would imply a compounded annual trajectory growth of approximately 20% to 25%.

items.statement: FY27 tax rate expected around 25%, with some deferred tax benefit.
items.quote: It should be 25%, maybe 1%, 2% or 3% here or there, depending upon the deferred tax we get.

items.statement: AI implementation reduces resource count by 20-25% in 6-12 months.
items.quote: So, we see definitely a reduction on the resource count for any customer close to 20%, 25% in a matter of 6 months or a year.

items.statement: Long-term like-for-like growth guidance of 5% to 7% remains; Q1 FY27 already better than Q4 FY26.
items.quote: So SSSG, we've given a commentary already, right, on Q1 and the longer term or the annual number, 5% to 7% remains. The quarter 1, we've already done better than Q4.

items.statement: Long-term margin guidance of 200 bps expansion holds, but short-term margin pressure expected.
items.quote: In the letter also we have said the long -term margin guidance on 200 bps holds and we'll try as quickly to get to that elevated number. But short-term pressure exist.

items.statement: Plans to open 230 to 250 restaurants this year; capex per store down 20% for nearly 3 years.
items.quote: So from all accounts, right, store addition and expansion is not a worry, we would open similar to about 230 to 250 kind of restaurants this year.

items.statement: Took 120 bps of pricing to offset energy cost inflation of 100-120 bps.
items.quote: We've already passed on the pricing to the tune of 120 basis points to the customers.

items.statement: Energy cost inflation of 100-120 bps already hitting P&L; LPG and PNG costs up.
items.quote: To some extent it's been very hard to calibrate Avi, but the energy is definitely the tune of 100 to 120 basis points, that hit we are already beginning to see come into the P&L.

items.statement: Labour Code adds ~20 bps; state minimum wage hikes add 20-30 bps; delivery mix adds further labor inflation.
items.quote: One is, of course, Labour Code is absolutely write-up of about 20-odd bps. But the minimum wage increases that we have seen across some of the states that have already gone live over 11 states out of 29 have already announced, and we'll wait and see some more, but that's another 20, 30 bps, which is there.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement is sustainable, driven by wastage reduction, premium products, mix changes and calibrated price increases.
items.quote: Actually, gross margin is sustainable. I think we answered that before.

items.statement: Will tighten belts first and not pass on all inflation; calibrated price increases to consumers later.
items.quote: What we are doing is, of course, first tighten our belts and not pass on everything to the consumer and the resul tant will have to pass on to the consumer after doing a thorough calibration of price increases.

items.statement: Domino's gained market share in pizza category and QSR space per Nielsen panel of 50,000 customers.
items.quote: And we have a separate panel of 50,000 customers run by Nielsen. They are also indicating that we have gained share, and we have gained share materially in pizza as a category.

items.statement: Consciously reduced minimum order value from Rs.149 to Rs.99 to gain share and acquire customers, lowering average ticket size.
items.quote: We have very consciously taken a call to reduce minimum order value from Rs.149 to Rs. 99. And as a result, there was a drop in the average ticket size.

items.statement: Near-term inflation pressure high across energy, labor and commodities; hard to predict duration.
items.quote: We're entering an inflationary environment; at least near-term inflation pressure is high. To some extent it's been very hard to calibrate Avi, but the energy is definitely the tune of 100 to 120 basis points, that hit we are already beginning to see come into the P&L.

items.statement: Launched premium products (Big Big Pizza, Sourdough Pizza) with better margins; supply chain cost lowest ever.
items.quote: We launched Big Big Pizza, we launched Sourdough Pizza, we launched some of the more premium products.

items.statement: Converting LPG ovens to electric and piped natural gas; large part of delivery fleet is electric, an advantage.
items.quote: Where the teams have done an amazing job of converting LPG to electric, we have developed our own solution kits. We've also been able to import quite a lot of electric ovens. And we are also converting very quickly to pipe natural gas, and there is a mandate from the government to convert to pipe natural gas.

items.statement: No major price increases planned; will not do major price increases.
items.quote: We will not do major price increases that is out of the table. Otherwise, we know what needs to be done on the margin front.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20% for FY27.
items.quote: As we have said, we are targeting 20% of revenue growth we are looking at.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance of INR8,000-10,000 crores for FY27.
items.quote: So order book guidance, as I said, it is INR8,000 c rores to INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 9.5-10.5% for FY27.
items.quote: Our estimation for FY '27 based on the order book which we have, we will be in the range of 9.5% to 10.5% for next year.

items.statement: Capex plan of approximately INR100 crores for FY27.
items.quote: We're planning approximately around INR100 crores o f capex, which includes certain capex on the international projects also.

items.statement: Monetization of 4 HAM assets by June 2026, expecting INR750+ crores.
items.quote: So to continue on that, out of the 6 projects, 4 we are definitely targeting by June end, which will typically bring in cash of around INR750-plus crores.

items.statement: Monetization of remaining 2 HAM assets by December 2026, expecting INR400 crores.
items.quote: And the balance we expect by December, which should bring in another INR400 crores.

items.statement: Working capital expected to normalize to 110-120 days post September.
items.quote: we believe that we should go back to the old norms of 110 to 120 days, this is more of a transitory as in the last call also, we had said there was some buildup of receivables in our Power division, which probably by end of June and September quarter, most of things would get cleared.

items.statement: Debt level expected to be INR500-600 crores by March 2027.
items.quote: And we believe that the debt level will be in the range of INR500 crores to INR600 crores by March '27 also, keeping all almost similar kind of turnover with a 20% jump.

items.statement: Balance HAM equity investment of INR325 crores, with INR175 crores in FY27.
items.quote: So on the equity side, the balance investment to be made in the HAM projects is around INR325 crores.

items.statement: Deferred consideration of INR550 crores expected in 24-36 months.
items.quote: And there are certain deferred consideration, which is based on toll extension, which is approximately INR550 crores, which will come in the next 1 or 2 years' time.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 was INR67 crores, with Q4 at INR16 crores.
items.quote: Q4, so total capex for the year was, INR67 crores, of which Q4 was INR16 crores.

items.statement: Effective tax on HAM asset sales expected at 6-7%.
items.quote: So effective tax on al l the put together would be in the range of 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Long-term vision to deliver INR 17,500 crores top line with 12.5% EBITDA margin by 2030.
items.quote: Yes. So we have kept the long-term vision in mind for 2030 to deliver INR 17,500 crores top line with 12.5% EBITDA margin. And the whole group is working towards achieving those stated numbers.

items.statement: Guiding principle to grow at least 50% more than industry growth; if industry grows 10%, revenue growth 15%+.
items.quote: While we don't give future outlook in terms of revenue guidance, but our guiding principle has been that we want to grow our business at least 50% more than the industry growth. So if the industry grows about 10%, so we should look at revenue growth in Minda Corporation to the tune of 15% plus.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected INR 400-450 crores, up from INR 350-400 crores range.
items.quote: So our capex has been in the range of INR 350 crores to INR 400 crores. And this year also, we expect to be in that range, maybe 10% plus of that, close to about INR 400 crores, INR 450 crores capex we are expecting for fiscal year 2026-27.

items.statement: Lifetime order book of INR 10,000 crores with execution timeline of 48-60 months.
items.quote: Now our order book is INR 10,000 crores, which we have registered throughout the year, and different product, different customer will have a different life cycle. Some maybe order for 5 years, so maybe for 6 years. But by and large, you can say it ranges anywhere between 48 months to 60 months.

items.statement: Commodity inflation passed through to customers, but no profit element, so some EBITDA margin impact.
items.quote: So any escalation should not necessarily eat up our margin. But definitely, since there is no profit element attached to the escalation, you would see some bit of impact on the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Commodity prices (copper, zinc, aluminum) escalated 30-40% throughout the year; contracts on pass-through basis.
items.quote: And when I look at across our main commodity, whether it is copper, zinc and aluminum, throughout the year, we saw escalation anywhere between 30% to 40% and most of our contracts with our customers are on pass-through basis.

items.statement: Passenger Vehicle segment at overall Minda Corporation level will grow north of 20% in FY27.
items.quote: So, the Passenger Vehicle segment at the overall Minda Corporation level will grow north of 20%.

items.statement: Instrument cluster and wiring harness to see maximum product launches in FY27, followed by die casting for exports.
items.quote: However, in terms of the products wise, you can say the instrument cluster business as well as the wiring harness business will see the maximum amount of product launches, followed by the die casting for exports will be the top 3.

items.statement: Minda VAST consolidation from FY27 to accelerate vision of 25% revenue from Passenger Vehicle segment.
items.quote: With the consolidation of Minda VAST business with Minda Corporation from FY 27 onwards, it will certainly accelerate our vision to achieve 25% revenue from Passenger Vehicle segment, which currently stands at about 14%.

items.statement: Sunroof JV received lifetime order of INR 350 crores; mass production in next 4-5 months; FY28 first full year.
items.quote: So yes, for sunroof, we have received the lifetime order of about INR 350 crores last year. We are getting into the mass production in the next 4 to 5 months. So yes, FY28 will be the first full year revenue.

items.statement: Switches JV mass production by March; FY28 ramp-up year, FY29 first peak year.
items.quote: When it comes to the switches, which is coming again into the mass production by March this year, so the FY28 will be the ramp-up year, I would say. So the first peak year would be, let's say, FY29 for the switches joint venture.

items.statement: Commodity inflation expected to continue at least next quarter due to geopolitical situation.
items.quote: So unless and until the geopolitical situation improves, we don't see this cooling off at least in the next quarter or so.

items.statement: Turntide JV orders for motor controllers to start SOP in 5-6 months; motors under advanced discussion.
items.quote: Number two, when it comes to the Turntide joint venture. As I mentioned, we've already won orders when it comes to the motor controllers as well as the other electronic space. So that is going to start SOP in about 5 to 6 months.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 outlook positive with several high-profile releases; confident of continuing last year's momentum.
items.quote: The outlook for the upcoming quarter remains positive, with several high-profile releases, including “Peddi”, “Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai”, “Welcome to the Jungle”, “Sarpanch”, “Cocktail 2” etc. With this robust lineup, we remain confident about continuing with the momentum of last year.

items.statement: Caravan business fully shut down; assets already disposed, realizing about INR 2-3 crores.
items.quote: We have already disposed of the assets, and these vans were quite old, more than 10 years old. So the amount of realization on that front totally would have been around INR 2 crores to INR 3 crores.

items.statement: Caravan business discontinued due to inconsistent pipeline; may operate via third-party tie-ups with no cost.
items.quote: Secondly, on the Caravan front, we have discontinued the Caravan business operations because there was significant inconsistency in the business pipeline.

items.statement: Ad revenue-sharing ratio should gradually decline as revenues scale up; ~80% of sharing expense is minimum-guarantee based.
items.quote: Therefore, nearly 80% of the revenue-sharing expense falls into this category, and that is the reason why, as revenues scale up, the sharing ratio should gradually decline.

items.statement: Ad-sharing with theatres rose to 50-60% from legacy 30-35% due to multiplex-heavy network; not losing pricing power.
items.quote: So, I think that’s a very valid observation regarding ad-sharing increasing from the earlier 30–35% range, which used to be our legacy percentage, to now being in the 50% –60% range.

items.statement: Where UFO invests in infrastructure, sharing percentage is lower, typically 35% to 45% depending on revenues.
items.quote: One, where we invest in the infrastructure, in which case the sharing percentage is relatively lower and typically ranges between 35% to 45%, depending on revenues.

items.statement: Consolidated DSO rose to 147 days in FY26 from 121 days in FY25, largely due to Dhurandhar receivables.
items.quote: To give you some perspective on DSOs, or Days Sales Outstanding, the consolidated DSO for the current year stands at 147 days, compared to 121 days in FY25, and this increase is largely attributable to the reasons I just mentioned.

items.statement: Net cash improved from INR 48.3 crores to INR 59 crores during the year despite working capital getting tied up.
items.quote: Our net cash has improved from INR 48.3 crores to INR 59 crores during the year, despite nearly INR 11 crores getting further tied up in working capital.

items.statement: Company will maintain both cash and debt on books; debt funds theatre equipment via LC converted to loan.
items.quote: The debt is taken specifically to fund the expensive equipment installed in theatres. Typically, we open a n LC, which subsequently gets converted into a loan.

items.statement: Company may reward shareholders with excess cash again once profitability turnaround sustains.
items.quote: And obviously, whenever excess cash is not required and there is an opportunity to reward shareholders, as we have done in the past, we will continue to ev aluate that.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 saw improving theatrical momentum; March strongest led by Dhurandhar: The Revenge.
items.quote: March was clearly the strongest month of the quarter, led by the exceptional success of “Dhurandhar: The Revenge”, which emerged as one of the biggest box office successes of the year.

items.statement: UFO network contributes 40-45% of footfalls for major blockbusters; got ~30% ad revenue share for Dhurandhar.
items.quote: For example, for any major blockbuster movie, the UFO network contributes nearly 40 –45% of the overall footfalls. However, historically, we were not receiving a proportionate share of advertising revenues associated with those movies.

items.statement: Employee cost rise largely due to ~INR 9 crores variable payouts after better profitability; costs under continuous monitoring.
items.quote: If you refer to Slide 18 of the investor presentation, we have highlighted that, on a full -year basis, there has been a variable payout of around INR 9 crores during the current year.

items.statement: VPF and CDC revenues declined in Q4 due to blank February and blockbuster clustering; full-year both grew.
items.quote: CDC and VPF revenues have gone down . So, that observation is correct for Q4. However, if you look at the full -year performance, revenues in both the CDC as well as VPF categories have increased.

items.statement: Expects 10-12% cement volume growth in FY27, excluding clinker sales.
items.quote: What we are looking for in the coming year is about 10% to 12% growth.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR600-700 crore, FY28 at INR1,500 crore.
items.quote: I think the estimate for FY27 will be about INR600 crores to INR700 crores given we follow these timelines.

items.statement: FY28 capex estimated at INR1,500 crore.
items.quote: In FY28, I think the estimate would be about INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton expected INR1,500-1,700 for next 2-3 years until Rajasthan project.
items.quote: I think for the next 2, 3 years till when we get the Rajasthan project, I think the EBITDA is -- because it is only in Northeast sales, the EBITDA should be between INR1,500 to INR1,700, right, at least.

items.statement: Long-term blended EBITDA per ton expected INR1,300-1,400 after Rajasthan ramp-up.
items.quote: But I think in the long run, we should be able to maintain it at about INR1,300, INR1,400 blended.

items.statement: Fuel cost to increase by INR0.10-0.15 per GCV in Q1/Q2 due to rake shortage, normalizing by Q3/Q4.
items.quote: So, I think there would be an impact of, I think, about INR 0.10 to INR0.15 per GCV cost in coal.

items.statement: Price increase of INR6-7 per bag in Northeast and INR10 per bag outside Northeast in April-May.
items.quote: Northeast, I think it may be about INR6 to INR7. Outside Northeast was about INR10.

items.statement: Demand sluggish in April due to elections, pickup in May; too early to predict full year.
items.quote: So, the current scenario right now, because of April, there was elections in April and May in Assam and also West Bengal. So, I think the demand was a bit sluggish because of that. I think we do see a pickup in May.

items.statement: New entrants to Northeast may pressure pricing for 1-2 years, but rationality expected to normalize.
items.quote: So, I think it's something that probably may happen for a year or 2, but then I think it should normalize because everyone is there to earn, right?

items.statement: Premium cement share was 15.1% in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: The premium cement share for this quarter was 15.1%.

items.statement: Trade share decreased to 78% in Q4 FY26 from 81% last year.
items.quote: So, trade share is about 78%. Last year, same quarter, it was 81%.

items.statement: QIP decision not yet taken at Board level; will inform in advance when planned.
items.quote: I think that decision we still not have taken at the Board level. We have, of course, taken the permission for raising money in the Board. I think in quarter 3, we did that. But we haven't planned it also because the markets were, of course, a bit weak as well, right?

items.statement: Subsidy expected to reduce by INR40-50 crore per quarter in FY27, totaling INR145-150 crore.
items.quote: So current year, we have done INR184 crores of subsidy. So what Tushar ji is saying INR40 crores to INR50 crores, somewhere in the INR145 crores to INR150 crores sort of thing you can estimate for the coming year.

items.statement: Targets 8% store EBITDA for Spencer's in FY27.
items.quote: And we are quite confident that going forward in FY'27, we will be able to achieve that 8% store EBITDA.

items.statement: Plans to break even on offline business this year.
items.quote: The plan is that this year, we will be able to break even on the offline business, definitely.

items.statement: Aims to reduce online business loss to low double digit or single digit.
items.value: low double digit, ideally in single digit
items.quote: we want to reduce this to low double digit, ideally in single digit.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA breakeven at operational level in FY27.
items.quote: the management ask is that in FY'27, we breakeven at an EBITDA level, at an operational EBITDA level.

items.statement: Will add 3-4 Spencer's stores this year, not as growth basis.
items.quote: you will see 3 -4 stores of Spencer's coming up in this year.

items.statement: Interest cost expected to remain 9.5-10.5% in FY27.
items.quote: Right now, we are in the range of 9.5 - 10.5%, and we expect that to continue in the financial year as well.

items.statement: Confident to sustain growth in Q1-Q4 of current year.
items.quote: I'm quite confident that we'll be able to sustain this in Q1-Q4 of the current year.

items.statement: Online business to grow from INR200 crores to INR250 crores next year.
items.quote: The idea is for it to go from INR200 crores to INR250 crores next year

items.statement: Nature's Basket faces internal challenges; next 2 quarters critical.
items.quote: Nature's Basket is, I would say, next 2 quarters are going to be critical, and we will demonstrate and drive growth over the next 2 quarters on that.

items.statement: Membership program has ~100,000 members, 20-22% of monthly sales.
items.quote: we closed the year with close to 100,000 members who had not only bought into the membership, but had also used the membership.

items.statement: Online business grew 37% YoY to INR200 crores in FY26.
items.quote: The online part of the business grew by 37% YoY. So closed at INR200 crores for FY'26, which was 37% increase over the previous year.

items.statement: SPSF improved from INR1,400 to INR1,700 per month per sq ft; target INR2,000.
items.quote: On Spencer's, in FY'25, we were at around INR1,400 per month per square foot. That number has gone up to close to INR1,700.

items.statement: Membership cash back impacted Q4 margins by 120 bps; real margin 18.6%.
items.quote: the 17.4% margin in Q4 on Spencer's is actually there is a 120 -basis point impact of the membership cash back. So, the real margin delivered on the category intake side is 18.6%.

items.statement: Internal aim to deliver double-digit SSSG in FY27, with H1 continuing Q4 momentum.
items.quote: Internal aim is to definitely cross double-digit same-store sales growth on the full financial year basis.

items.statement: Target pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin of 9-10% in FY27.
items.quote: Our internal aim is to take pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin to 9% to 10% in FY'27 with a path towards double-digit margins going forward.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR140 crores for FY27, including 40 new restaurants.
items.quote: We are planning a capex of approximately INR140 crores for next year.

items.statement: Mature portfolio ROM to improve to 17-18% in FY27.
items.quote: Mature portfolio ROM, which is approximately 16% on an H2 FY'26 basis, will move to 17% to 18%.

items.statement: Consolidated ROM expected at 15.5-16.5% in FY27.
items.quote: That takes consolidated ROM to approximately 15.5% to 16.5%.

items.statement: Back-end cost to compress to 6.5% of revenue in FY27.
items.quote: We expect back-end cost to compress from 7.1% to approximately 6.5% as a percentage of revenue in FY'27 and further down to 6% over the longer term.

items.statement: Net debt to remain at INR102 crores in FY27, funded by internal accruals.
items.quote: As our operating cash flow scales with the H2 run rate, we expect our net debt position to remain the same.

items.statement: H1 FY27 expected to continue Q4 momentum, with possible improvement in Q1.
items.quote: First half FY’27, I expect the Q4 level numbers to continue. And if the momentum that has built up in Q2 versus Q3, there may be some improvement also in Q1.

items.statement: Aim to achieve INR15-20 additional net realization per cover through pricing tweaks.
items.quote: What we're talking about on a net basis is approximately INR15 to INR20 net realization from each of the covers done.

items.statement: Cautious on Middle East due to inflation and uncertainty; no new store signings.
items.quote: We are very cautious about signing any new store in that market. We have not sort of looked at anything for the last 3 months.

items.statement: Target 400-425 restaurants by FY30.
items.quote: Our internal target is to reach 400 to 425 restaurants by FY'30.

items.statement: NCR region targets INR800+ crore revenue in FY27, up from INR585 crore in FY26.
items.quote: So INR585 versus, say, we end up doing INR800-plus odd crores in FY27, that is the target that we're looking at.

items.statement: NCR EBITDA margin expected to reach 2-4% in FY27.
items.quote: And then with a good summer or a good festive period, we would definitely look at a little lighter bump there and then if we achieve that kind of a number, we would look at an EBITDA margin of at least 2% to 4% kind of a number there.

items.statement: Delhi cluster to grow 25-30% in FY27 from INR590 crore base.
items.quote: So sir, at least for that particular cluster, we will do at least a 25% to 30% kind of a growth from the existing 590 kind of a number.

items.statement: Delhi EBITDA margin to improve to 2.5-3% from 0.2-0.3%.
items.quote: Margin will improve, so right now, I would consider at 0.2%, 0.3% kind of an EBITDA margin, which would be definitely 2.5% or 3% kind of a number.

items.statement: Andhra and Telangana clusters to contribute INR2,400-2,700 crore in coming year.
items.quote: So, both the clusters would definitely contribute to anywhere between INR2,400 crores and INR2,700 crores in the coming year.

items.statement: Plan to add 12-15 stores organically in NCR, AP, Telangana; 7-8 in Delhi NCR.
items.quote: So organically, we will be looking at anywhere between 12 to 15 stores in this region. We'll be opening up at least 4 to 5 stores, which are getting ready in Delhi region and adding up another, 3 or 4 new contracts in that region as well.

items.statement: Entering East market with 5-7 stores in Kolkata by end Q2/early Q3 FY27.
items.quote: We would at least start off with 5 to 7 stores in that region by the end of Q2 or the beginning of Q3.

items.statement: Real estate investment in Kolkata not more than INR50 crore this year, INR100 crore over 12-14 months.
items.quote: But for this financial year, I wouldn't look at more than INR50-odd crores investments happening in real estate there. So probably over a period of time, you might end up doing not more than INR100 crores of acquisition there in the next, say, 12-14 months.

items.statement: Mature stores EBITDA margin 7.3%, newer stores 3.1%, expected to improve as they mature.
items.quote: From a profitability standpoint, mature stores continue to demonstrate strong performance with an EBITDA margin of approximately 7.3%, while newer stores are currently operating at 3.1%, consistent with their stage of ramp-up.

items.statement: RAC price hikes of 2-3% fully passed on to customers; no margin impact.
items.quote: But at the same time, going probably going another 20 days or so, we would be then picking up a little more inventory than required. That would be at a newer price, but not with a major price increase, I'm talking about 2% or 3% maximum, not more than that. And we don't absorb any improvement in -- the hike in the pric

items.statement: Summer season strong in AP and Telangana, Delhi started late but expects double-digit growth.
items.quote: AP and Telangana have definitely outperformed on our expectations. But we still have 45 days left for this quarter to end, and that is 50% of the quarter time still left on board with us.

items.statement: Mobile phones ASP at INR35,000-40,000; entry-level price hikes not significant for company.
items.quote: Our ASPs are about INR35,000, INR40,000 per mobile phone today. So if you look at the upper category, the price of iPhone, Google, FoldFlip, S20 Ultra, has not increased.

items.statement: NCR faces higher competition from Croma, Reliance, Vijay Sales; lower footfalls than South.
items.quote: Sir, in Delhi, not only, like you say, your competitive intensity with bigger guys like Croma, Reliance, Vijay Sales, fighting there, whereas here you're fighting with mom-and-pop stores.

items.statement: Inventory days at 73 as of March 31, 2026; working capital efficiency improving.
items.quote: On inventory days outstanding as of 31st March'26 stood at 73 days. We have managed inventory efficiently throughout the year, maintaining a well-calibrated mix of carry forward and of new AC models ensuring we were well positioned heading into the summer season.

items.statement: India growth should accelerate further in FY27 after Q3/Q4 data launches; international rebound expected from Q1 onwards.
items.quote: we expect that the India growth should accelerate further following the launches that we had done in Q3 and Q4 and on the international front we expect rebound to you know play out from Q1 onwards.

items.statement: Company aims to return to more than 20% growth rate even if market stays weak.
items.quote: you want to basically, you know, reach to like a more than 20% sort of growth rate.

items.statement: Closing sales teams to nearly double from 34 at Dec-25 to 60 by Dec-26.
items.quote: We had about 34 closing sales teams as of end of December 25 and we plan to nearly double this to 60 at the end of this calendar year which is December 26.

items.statement: India closing sales team to grow from ~25 at Dec-25 to ~40 by end of calendar year.
items.quote: we'll grow this from a team of about 25 at the end of December to about 40 at the end of this calendar year.

items.statement: International closing sales team to double from under 10 to about 25 people.
items.quote: we are also doubling our closing sales team here which is from less than 10 people to about 25 people.

items.statement: AI-native access segment expected to start contributing to revenue from this financial year.
items.quote: We expect that this segment should start contributing to revenue from this financial year onwards.

items.value: 4 lakh vs 5 lakh per account per year
items.quote: today our ASP is about 4 lakh per account per year, you know, which is slightly lower than 5 lakh per account per year last year, right?

items.statement: Pricing within customer segments has not reduced much; ASP decline mainly due to mix change.
items.quote: our blended ASP has reduced, but our pricing within the customer segment is actually not reduced that much, right?

items.statement: Company is adding pricing tiers and starting metered usage-based pricing for some segments.
items.quote: we are starting metered pricing, right? So based on the number of usage, so it's a little bit of, you know, usage based pricing that we also launching for these segments.

items.statement: Deal volume remains at nearly a 10-year low in India and internationally, including late-stage funding.
items.quote: deal volume continues to remain low at nearly a 10 year low both in India as well as internationally and in late stage funding so you see a similar trend.

items.statement: Global M&A rebound strong; 2026 could be second highest year after 2021 peak.
items.quote: The current run rate suggests that 2026 could actually become the second highest year after the peak of 2021 both in terms of global M&A deal value as well as IB advisory field.

items.statement: Historically converted as high as 80% of incremental revenue into EBITDA; expects pattern to repeat as growth re-accelerates.
items.quote: historically we have converted as high as 80 percent of the incremental revenue into EBITDA so once the growth re-accelerates we expect this Pattern to repeat driving non-linear expansion.

items.statement: ESOP expense expected to remain in the same range as historically.
items.quote: We expect that it should remain in the same similar range of what it has been, it has been fairly range bound, right, the ESOP charge, because of the way, you know, things are structured, it should remain in the same range.

items.statement: TMX partnership already generating small revenues, expected to increase; large partnerships take one to two quarters to close.
items.quote: No, we've started generating revenues from that. Right. Though they're small, and we expect that to increase.

items.statement: Management expects India growth trajectory to continue and accelerate in subsequent year.
items.quote: And that trajectory we expect, you know, that should continue in the subsequent year, because, you know, we have, you know, sort of made investments that is working out very well.

items.statement: International growth improvement expected from Q1/Q2 onwards, meaningful impact after launches in next couple of months.
items.quote: you should start seeing some impact, you know, from, you know, like Q1, Q2 onwards itself. But I would say the meaningful impact will also come in, you know, once we have those launches, which is probably, you know, like maybe the next couple of months

items.statement: Expenses expected to grow at single-digit percentage, similar to historical 5-10% range.
items.quote: our expenses grown at single digit percentage, right between 5 to 10%. You know, that's what it has grown. And even going forward, we expect that it should probably be in the similar range, a single digit percentage

items.statement: ESOP expense expected to remain in the same range-bound level.
items.quote: We expect that it should remain in the same similar range of what it has been, it has been fairly range bound, right, the ESOP charge

items.statement: Company gearing to reach 20% overall growth level soon.
items.quote: we are gearing for, you know, sort of reaching that at the overall level soon.

items.statement: AI-native data access and platform partnerships should start contributing to revenue from FY27.
items.quote: we believe that in FY27, you know, that should actually be a percentage of your revenue as well, right? It should start contributing in the, you know, in the revenue from this financial year onwards

items.quote: we are also adding public market data. And you will see that's actually getting launched this quarter itself, which is mainly for private market investors are looking to benchmark

items.statement: Corporate segment has grown to more than 40% of customer base and remains a focus area.
items.quote: right now, corporate is actually grown to, you know, more than 40% of our, if you look at our customer base, right? And that is a segment that we continue to sort of invest in.

items.statement: VC segment impacted by software market; funds shrinking and cutting headcount.
items.quote: the segment that is impacted is the same, right? Like we talked about, which is your investment, which is your VC as a segment, which you, because of the software market and then that we have seen impact

items.statement: Deal volume continues at a 10-year low.
items.quote: like the deal volume today, right, continues, is at a 10 year low.

items.statement: ASP per user now about 1.5 lakh per year versus 2.5 lakh earlier, driven by customer mix shift.
items.value: one and a half lakh per user per year
items.quote: currently, it's about one and a half lakh per user per year, right? Which is probably used to be like about two and a half per user per year, right?

items.quote: India ASP would be probably about half. So, for average ASP is about, you know, say 4 lakh, India would be less than that and international would be double of India.

items.statement: Company will consider another buyback once eligible; buyback preferred over dividend due to accumulated losses.
items.quote: we'll probably be eligible for doing another buyback soon. So, you know, probably once that window opens up, we would be, you know, as we mentioned that we would want to sort of keep doing buyback

items.statement: GTM team grew from 23% to about 30% of headcount; may go up a few percentage points.
items.quote: it has grown from about 23% overall of the headcount to about 30%, right.

items.statement: FY27 same-store revenue growth guidance of 9-11% with healthy margin expansion.
items.quote: Looking ahead, FY27 builds from the FY26 base, we are confident of delivering 9 to 11% same-store revenue growth with healthy margin expansion on top of the ongoing contribution of the assets that opened during FY2026.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected around 38% despite permanent GST impact.
items.quote: So Karan, the margins we expect to be around 38% or so. There is an impact of GST for sure, which is permanent in terms of absolute basis. But even then, we should maintain a 38% margin through the year.

items.statement: FY27 capex allocation INR 250-270 crores, largely for W Hyderabad.
items.quote: Coming to your second question, for FY27, we have allocated about INR 250 crores to INR 270 crores of capital, capex. Large part of this is actually towards the W in Hyderabad.

items.statement: GIC platform: INR 600 crores received, balance INR 150 crores over next two years.
items.quote: We've received INR 600 crores so far. The balance investment is INR 150 crores. That could come over the next two year period because that's coming in line with the capex spending on the Westin - Tribute Bangalore.

items.statement: ROCE target maintained at 14-15% for current assets and new openings.

items.statement: FY26 free cash flow INR 300 crores, run-rate INR 315 crores after interest savings.
items.quote: Our FY26 free cash flow of approximately INR 300 crores became approximately INR 315 crores on a run rate basis once the additional interest savings we have secured is factored in.

items.quote: So, 13% to 14% gross margins and around 7 % of EBITDA, normalized EBITDA is what the company is expecting and to improve.

items.statement: SDA and LDA segment grew ~53% YoY in Q4 FY26, driven by new products and order inflows.
items.quote: The SDA and LDA segment delivered robust growth of approximately 53% Y-o-Y, supported by healthy order inflows across both existing and newly launched products.

items.quote: The premium segment and when I say premium, I mean, people who earn more than, let's say, Rs.25-30 lakhs a year. That segment has been growing faster than the mid-level segment for the last few quarters.

items.statement: AI-driven search changes affecting Shiksha traffic and billings.

name: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd

items.statement: Standalone cash utilization plan: INR1,000 cr in FY26, INR600 cr in FY27, INR500 cr in FY28, aiming FCF positive in FY29.
items.value: INR1,000 crores in FY '26, INR600 crores in FY '27 and INR500 crores in '28
items.quote: As stated, we are planning to utilize it INR1,000 crores in FY '26, INR600 crores in FY '27 and INR500 crores in '28, post which we aim to be FCF positive in FY '29.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance INR250-300 crores at consolidated level, no one-off GL capex.
items.quote: Next year, this one-off type of thing will not come. So, we have -- in our plan, I already conveyed roughly INR300 crores capex, INR250 crores to INR300 crores at console level.

items.statement: Raw material inflation 3-4%, may take price increases of 5-8% in H2 depending on category.
items.quote: And therefore, effectively, it would sort of put pressure in the second half of the year to take -- to fully counter it, take price increases between 5% to 8% depending on the category.

items.statement: Tasva expected to breakeven by FY28; TCNS breakeven by end FY27, profitable FY28.
items.quote: We had said FY '28, and we still feel that's the right assessment at this point as well. As far as TCNS is concerned, Jagdish in his opening remarks had talked about how the losses have halved this year versus FY '25. We're still not profitable. We'll probably towards the end of FY '27 is when we would expect to breake

items.statement: TMRW portfolio expected to become profitable by FY29.
items.quote: As far as profitability of TMRW is concerned, we had indicated FY '29 as the year in which we expect that TMRW as a portfolio level, some of all brands to become profitable.

items.statement: TMRW raised INR440 cr equity and INR500 cr NCDs, now has INR800 cr cash for growth.
items.quote: As you are aware, with equity issuance of INR440 crores during the year and more recent fund tie-up of INR500 crores through NCDs, TMRW is now adequately funded with INR800 crores cash to pursue its aggressive growth plans.

items.statement: Demand normal in April and current quarter; inflation may pressure H2 demand.
items.quote: But we have seen demand nearly normal for most part of April and going into this quarter. So, as of now, while we feared a significant sort of risk on demand, as of now, we have not seen it play out.

items.statement: Pantaloons standalone margin 18-18.5% for quarter and year, slightly higher than last year.
items.quote: Pantaloons margin for the quarter, and I think for the year are also between 18% to 18.5%, which is the margin that Pantaloons has consistently delivered slightly higher than last year.

items.statement: Pantaloons online share 3-4% of business, plans to scale profitably.
items.quote: Today, it's about 3%, 4% of our business. It's not very large. But with all the shifts we have made this year, we feel confident of scaling up this business.

items.statement: Inflationary pressures may fully play out over next 3-4 months, risking demand in H2.
items.quote: Having said that, most of the inflationary pressures are perhaps still at work and may play out fully over the next 3 to 4 months. And therefore, consequent sort of pressure on demand is something that we'll have to wait and watch for in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Ethnic business FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 560 bps to 10.8%.
items.quote: Profitability improved significantly with FY '26 EBITDA margin expanding by 560 basis points to 10.8%.

items.statement: FY28 standalone revenue guidance of another 25% growth, roughly INR 7,500 crore.
items.quote: for FY28, from there we are looking at another 25% guidance, so that will roughly translate into INR 7,500 crores.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of around 12%.
items.quote: The EBITDA will continue to be around 12% for FY27.

items.statement: Expects new order inflow of around INR 15,000 crore in FY27.
items.quote: we are expecting an overall new order book of around INR 15,000 crores in FY27

items.statement: FY27 capex target of INR 150 crore.
items.quote: CAPEX for Financial Year ‘27, we are targeting INR 150 crores.

items.statement: Solar EPC revenue target of INR 600 crore in FY27 and INR 1,400 crore in FY28.
items.quote: We are targeting around INR 600 crores in FY27, and INR 1,400 crores in FY28.

items.statement: Mining EPC revenue target of INR 400 crore in FY27 and INR 600 crore in FY28.
items.quote: we are expecting another INR 400 crores turnover in FY27 , and in FY28, we are expecting around INR 600 crores.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission revenue target of INR 750 crore in FY27.
items.quote: for FY27, we are targeting INR 750 crores in revenue, with the hope that the government will release more and more funds for this project, both central and state.

items.statement: Varanasi-Kolkata packages expected to contribute INR 1,600-1,800 crore revenue in FY27.
items.quote: going forward in FY27, we are looking at around INR 1,600 crores to INR 1,800 crores revenue from these packages.

items.statement: Pune Ring Road and Jalna-Nanded expected to contribute INR 1,500-1,600 crore revenue in FY27.
items.quote: we are targeting around INR 1,500 crores to INR 1,600 crores in FY27 from these two projects

items.statement: Margin pressure expected in Q1/Q2 due to commodity price volatility, but recovery in Q3/Q4.
items.quote: Certainly, there will be pressure on our margins given the current scenario.

items.statement: Remaining equity investment of INR 542 crore to be invested over next 2 years; INR 350 crore in FY27.
items.quote: Out of INR 542 crores, around INR 350 crores will be infused in current Financial Year ‘27 and the balance will be in Financial Year ‘28.

items.statement: Targeting 60-70% of new orders from highways, rest from non-highways sectors.
items.quote: 60% to 70%, we are still targeting the highways sector because NHAI has declared that they are coming out with a large number of highways projects, both on HAM and as well as BOT Toll apart from the EPC.

items.statement: Acquiring Randstad Technology and Consulting Services for €160 million enterprise value, with annualized revenue of €469 million.
items.quote: The technology and consulting services business across these two big markets comes to annualized revenue of €469 million and we have a proposed enterprise value of €160 million on a cash free, debt free basis.

items.statement: Five-year IT services partnership with Randstad Group; initial scope TCV around €55-60 million.
items.quote: the initial scope value is somewhere around 55 to 60 million.

items.statement: No material impact on EBIT margin this year and next year after acquisition closure.
items.quote: there is going to be no material impact to the margin, for this year, even after closure and for the next year, we have plan in place to make sure that there is no material impact.

items.statement: Acquisition consideration will be 10-15% of cash on balance sheet.
items.quote: it is not going to be more than 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Post-closure, Europe business will exceed $1 billion; APAC will double; Australia will exceed $100 million.
items.quote: Post closure, we will be in excess of a billion dollar business in Europe and we will be 2x in APAC and as I mentioned, we will be in excess of $100 million business in Australia.

items.statement: May trim about 10 more tail accounts in short term to focus on scaled accounts.
items.quote: If that results in trimming 10 more tail accounts over a period of time, it may not happen at one shot, but if we need to do that, we will do it but that may be just a short-term thing.

items.statement: Acquisition expected to be EPS accretive from day one due to minimal margin impact.
items.quote: if the margin impact is not there, it is not going to be EPS dilutive also.

items.statement: Minimal sales and marketing investment needed, mainly overlay sales for cross-sell/upsell.
items.quote: the investment will be very minimal and will be more on the overlay sales.

items.statement: Client MSAs allow cross-selling; may need to add offshore rate cards in some cases.
items.quote: The answer is yes, because even the existing business is a mix of the normal kind of contracts that we see in any IT services company, which is T&M, fixed price, solutions, all of those things, so the MSAs do provide for that.

items.statement: Top 25 customers in Europe contribute 65% of revenue; top 10 in Australia contribute 80%.
items.quote: In Europe, the top 25 customers contribute 65% of the revenue. In Australia, top 10 customers contribute to 80% of the revenue.

items.statement: Average consultant tenure in accounts is over five years, with some 7-8 years.
items.quote: the average tenure of consultants in an account is greater than five years in these accounts.

items.statement: Commercial arrangements are a mix of T&M and managed services, with significant T&M.
items.quote: the commercial arrangements are a mix of T&M, managed services and so on. But yes, it is a significant commercial arrangement of T&M

items.statement: No conflict with group company LTTS; capabilities are complementary.
items.quote: There is absolutely no conflict with any of our group companies.

items.statement: Acquisition will be kept as a separate subsidiary to avoid integration distractions.
items.quote: We intend to keep this as a separate subsidiary of LTM so that we do not spend time on integration or anything

items.statement: Targets 10-15% operating revenue growth for FY27.
items.quote: Firstly, we are looking to grow Operating revenues by 10%-15% for the year.

items.quote: Secondly, we are giving an EBITDA margin band guidance of 17%-19%. This guidance is lower than last year on back of increased costs due to escalation in the prices of paper/logistics/transportation/packaging due to currency depreciation and higher fuel prices in the current year

items.statement: Targets content licensing revenues of more than Rs400m in FY27.
items.quote: Fifth, We are looking to target revenues more than Rs400m in the Content Licensing opportunities of our text, images and videos repositories and growing the number of clients.

items.statement: Expects operating cash flow over Rs1,000m for FY27.
items.quote: We expect to deliver OCF of over Rs1,000m for FY27.

items.statement: Plans capex of about Rs20 crores, mainly for a new printing plant near Delhi.
items.quote: Considering we have a capex of about Rs20 crores coming up, I would say, we should be around Rs130 crores, Rs135 crores.

items.statement: Expects paper and other raw material prices to increase 10-15% this year.
items.quote: Paper prices, definitely, we expect to grow by 10% to 15% this year at least, maybe more also.

items.statement: Plans to take price hikes of 6-8% to partially offset cost increases.
items.quote: We expect that the price hike would be in the range of 6% to 8%. That's only maximum we can take.

items.statement: Expects complete adoption of new syllabus books for K-12 over FY27-28, supporting growth.

items.statement: Considering buyback but waiting for war situation to settle; cash position expected at Rs130-135 crores next year.
items.quote: Yes, yes, we are considering that. Unfortunately, because of the war situation, we are waiting for things to settle down because it's best to have cash in books for this uncertain period.

items.statement: Plans small capital investment of Rs5-7 crores over next 2-3 years for international business expansion.
items.quote: So, we are not going to spend too much of money, maybe a small capital investment in the next 2 to 3 years of maybe Rs5 crores to Rs7 crores, nothing large, nothing major.

items.statement: Management guides over 15% revenue growth for FY27, excluding potential price retrigger benefits.
items.quote: I do expect that even on a conservative level, I am happy to give a guidance of over a 15% growth in the overall revenue.

items.statement: Company aims to double revenues every three to four years with improving margins and returns.
items.quote: we expect to double our revenues every three to four years with consistent improvements in margins and return on investments.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected at INR 275-310 crores, 5-7% of revenues, including growth, maintenance and upgradation.

items.quote: you can expect somehow capital outlay of INR 275 crores to around INR 310 crores for the upcoming financial year, which will include a part of growth CapEx, part of maintenance CapEx, part of upgradation CapEx

items.statement: Existing projects expected to improve EBITDA margins by about 0.25% in FY27.
items.quote: yes we could expect a growth of 0.25% in EBITDA margins.

items.quote: while EBITDA levels will remain constant around 11%, but with the volumes coming up and the revenue going up, automatically in terms of absolute returns, our multiplier will be giving us a more return on capital employed.

items.statement: Targets post-tax ROCE improving from 15% to a peak of 20%.
items.quote: we are targeting an improvement return on capital employed starting with a post-tax return of 15%, going something at a highest peak of 20%.

items.statement: Pricing retrigger mechanism likely activated due to rising input costs, benefiting company versus older customer pricing.

items.statement: Manpower availability and rising state minimum wages (30-50%) pose significant industry-wide risk.

items.statement: Term loans of INR 384 crores to be repaid over 3-4 years; FY27 repayment commitment around INR 103 crores.
items.quote: This year we have a repayment commitment of around close to INR 103 crores with various banks.

items.quote: So we are, as a team, fully committed to enhancing the revenue by 15% to 20% year-on-year, and achieving EBITDA of closer to 20-odd percent in the medium term, and we continue to work on that journey.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected around INR110 crores, including announced projects and maintenance.
items.quote: Yes. INR110 crores -- I mean, broadly, yes. Yes, broadly. It can go -- maybe it can go up depending on more projects through the year. But at the moment, yes, that's correct.

items.statement: Two approved expansion projects total about INR90+ crores; maintenance capex INR20-25 crores annually.
items.quote: Yes. So capex, these 2 capex, which I already said earlier, is about INR90 plus crores. There's maintenance capex of roughly INR20 crores, INR25 crores a year, which should continue.

items.quote: The company is further investing INR75 crores towards setting up a 20-megawatt ground-mounted solar plant with a battery energy storage system, which will further reduce the overall power cost, and the same is expected to be commissioned in this quarter, Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Solar plant expected to deliver about INR28 crores EBITDA-level cost savings in FY27.
items.quote: Yes. So that will be -- that is estimated to be about INR28 crores at EBITDA level, for FY27.

items.statement: Price hikes of 8-10% taken in glassware and opalware to cover cost inflation; full benefit may take 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: It's more because to get customers to accept substantially higher pricing, let's say, 8% to 10%, which is what prices we have taken, that takes a bit of time.

items.statement: Direct gas cost increased from INR20 crores to INR50 crores per annum due to West Asia crisis.
items.quote: Increased to INR50 crores.

items.statement: In-house manufacturing of vacuum bottles expected to improve gross margin by at least 10%, but not in first couple of quarters.
items.quote: But my sense is on the gross margin side, 10% at least we should get an increase. Otherwise, there's no benefit of manufacturing in India, so -- but I don't think that will be realized in like the first couple of quarters.

items.statement: Opalware demand growth muted; expects muted growth for next year or so.
items.quote: And we are working on that, but at the moment, I think we are -- for the next year or so, I think we are going to expect to see muted growth.

items.quote: No, just now we answered, the revenue from the Shalvis facility will be around INR 70 crores to INR 80 crores in this financial year, FY27, including the new block, what we are going to construct.

items.quote: Sir, FY27, I think we will be utilizing the full capacity of the products because we increased the capacity last quarter, which was commissioned only in March. So we hope that this year, we should be able to utilize fully.

items.quote: Yes. So the operational EBITDA, as you must have seen, if we exclude the ESOP expenses has actually improved a lot. And in the long run, we maintained that we expect the overall EBITDA level to grow.

items.quote: Yes. In terms of run rate, we do not -- as you are aware, do not give guidance. But we have seen positive traction in exports.

items.statement: Order book visibility supports INR 8,000-8,200 crores revenue, targeting INR 10,000 crores.

items.statement: Energy storage program expected to generate INR 80-100 crores annual revenue.

items.statement: FY27 volume guidance of 350,000-360,000 tonnes, implying 20-25% growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 12.5-12.6% is sustainable and will continue.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA per tonne expected to be at least current level, with continuous efforts to grow.
items.quote: So, if at all everything goes well without the geopolitical issues and the scenario on the pricing hit and other things. So, we feel that this will be the minimum one and this should continue.

items.statement: Solar project to be completed by FY27, with 10 MW production starting next month.
items.quote: For us '27 is the last deadline to complete our entire 13 locations, 60 megawatt AC projects. So, out of 13 locations, we have almost of start of the project, 8 locations, 2 are yet to be coming for commencement and remaining will be completed within this financial year.

items.statement: Backward integration benefits quality and security of raw material, not major margin impact.
items.quote: So, the margins would not be a very big thing, but only the quantity and the quality and the consistency of the supply for the raw material will get improved.

items.statement: B2B contribution increased from 15% to 20%, targeting further increase.
items.quote: Earlier it was 15% now it has become increased up to 20%.

items.statement: Current quarter demand is good, but no specific growth guidance provided.
items.quote: Current quarter is good, sir. So far it is absolutely good.

items.quote: So, per unit we are getting around INR3.21paise, apart from capital subsidy. So, as and when it will be generated that is the fixed tenurity and fixed revenue will be coming.

items.statement: No impact from gas supply disruptions, own suppliers and storage intact.

items.statement: Expects VNB margins to further improve, but no specific target; focus on VNB growth.

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio expected to be sustained in future.
items.quote: We expect it to be sustained in the future also, that also has been kept in mind before the board decided the amount of dividend to be declared.

items.statement: VNB margin improved 360 bps YoY to 21.2% in FY26.
items.quote: Further, net VNB margin has improved by 360 basis points on a year-on-year basis to 21.2% for the year ended 31 March, 2026 from 17.6% for the previous year.

items.statement: Operating assumption changes (persistency, expense, GST) negatively impacted VNB margin by 2.8%.
items.quote: So the combined effect of the persistency and expense in some line of business adjustments based on the experience along with the GST impact, which has been taken as part of the policy expenses, the contribution is negative 2.8%.

items.statement: Business mix shift to non-par contributed 3% to VNB margin.
items.quote: So this business mix which has gone up has contributed to 3% to the VNB margin.

items.statement: RFR changes contributed 3.4% to VNB margin.
items.quote: So this RFR has contributed to 3.4%.

items.statement: Non-par share of individual APE settled at ~35% for last three quarters.
items.quote: Our non-par share of individual APE business has now consistently settled at about 35% sequentially over the last three results performance updates.

items.statement: Aims to increase guaranteed business (non-par savings, protection, annuity) while maintaining margins.
items.quote: We would naturally like to increase our contribution from guaranteed business, both in terms of non-par savings as well as protection as well as tap the market in full in terms of annuity business that is possible.

items.statement: Cautious on dividend due to expected risk-based capital (RBC) regime; building reserves.
items.quote: We are not sure when it is going to be introduced, so we need to build some reserves so that we remain at a comfortable level of solvency throughout.

items.statement: High equity exposure may impact RBC; monitoring regulatory developments.
items.quote: But the point here is sensitivity to the volatility in equities is a significant factor for -- which will impact the risk-based capital.

items.statement: No immediate plan to increase non-par IRR; will balance investment opportunities and competition.
items.quote: So we'll continue to watch and see whether there is a possibility of -- also added to it the hedging possibilities, particularly in the non-participating portfolio, how much of the risk can be hedged, because as of now, these hedging instruments are not available for very long duration.

items.statement: April 2026 saw good growth in both par and non-par, number of sales and premium.
items.quote: We are seeing a good growth in terms of both the number of sales as well as the premium that is being accumulated. Particularly, the April figures have been a testimony to that.

items.statement: FY27 volume target 231,000 MT, capacity utilization 73%, revenue growth 13% YoY, EBITDA margin ~11%.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin anticipated at approximately 11%.
